title: Yeast Dough Base for Coffee Cake
directions: Crumble yeast into mixture (referencing prior steps not shown) and stir until dissolved.
Stir in 2 eggs.
Stir in 1/2 cup shortening.
Mix in first with a spoon, then with hand.
Add 7 - 7 1/2 cups sifted flour in 2 additions, using the amount necessary to make it easy to handle.
Knead the dough according to directions.
After second rising, divide dough for desired rolls & coffee cake.
Round up, cover, & let rest 15 min. so dough is easy to handle.
Shape doughs, let rise until light (15 to 30 min.), & bake according to directions for each type of roll or coffee cake.
notes: The recipe assumes prior steps (likely involving liquid ingredients for the yeast mixture) were performed before the start of this excerpt.

title: 13 Bean Soup
ingredients: 13 Beans (Cow Peas, Black Eyed Peas, Yellow Eyed Peas, Yellow Split Peas, Green Split Peas, Kidney Beans, Pinto Beans, Navy Beans, Cranberry Beans, Black Beans, Red Beans, White Lima Beans, Green Lima Beans, Colored Lima Beans)
Meat (hamhocks or bacon drippings, or substitute meat: beef stock or chicken broth)
directions: No presoaking needed.
Wash beans.
Place meat and beans in a 2 quart size pot.
Fill completely with water.
When water comes to a boil, turn stove on medium temperature.
Add onions, tomatoes (16 oz.), celery, and other spices to taste.
Let simmer one (1) hour and 45 minutes.
Serve as a soup or over rice.
notes: Guaranteed to make you act just like a real 'CHARLESTONIAN'.

title: Acorn Squash with Baked Apples and Pecans
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Halve squash and remove seeds; remove a small slice from the rounded bottom to allow squash to sit flat.
Place squash, cut side up, in baking dish just large enough to hold squash in a single layer; set aside.
Combine all remaining ingredients, except pecans and butter or margarine; fill centers of squash.
Pour hot water around sides of squash to a depth of 1/2 inch; cover dish tightly with foil and bake 30 minutes.
Uncover; top with pecans and dot with butter or margarine and bake an additional 25 to 30 minutes or until squash is fork tender and pecans are golden brown.
Serves 4 generously.
notes: To halve winter squash: The hard outer covering requires a sharp, large knife. The squash covering can be softened slightly by piercing the outer edges with a large fork and placing on a plate in the microwave, on medium heat, for a few minutes. Do not overcook in the microwave; as soon as the outer covering is softened, it is ready to halve. "Delicious with roasted pork or turkey!"
pdfLink: pdfs/ACORN SQUASH WITH BAKED APPLES AND PECANS.pdf

title: Arugula and Red Onion Salad
ingredients: 1/2 pound arugula leaves, rinsed and dried
directions: Place chilled arugula, onion and parsley in a chilled flat serving bowl.
Put vinegar in small bowl and whisk in olive oil until well blended.
Add salt and pepper.
Spoon over salad.
Serves 4-6.
notes: Our grandmothers grew arugula but called it rocket. They also loved the peppery bite that arugula gives a salad. Serve with a great pasta dish!

title: Asparagus with Prosciutto
ingredients: 1½ - 2 pounds medium asparagus spears, trimmed and cooked until fork tender
⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
directions: Butter sauce: Melt butter and add lemon juice, parsley, salt and pepper.
Place steamed asparagus on serving plates; top with butter sauce and place a slice of ham over top of asparagus.
Garnish with green onions and serve immediately.
notes: Serves 4. Delicious and amazingly easy!

title: Almond Skillet Cake
directions: Line a heavy iron skillet c/a (with a) large piece of heavy duty foil.
Preheat oven to 350°.
Pour batter into skillet, spreading evenly - Batter will be stiff.
Top c/ (with) slivered almonds & sprinkle sugars - colored sugars for holidays.
Bake 35-40 mins until light brown.
Remove from skillet c/ (with) foil - cool on wire rack, wrap in foil around cake.
Freezes well.
notes: From the Kitchen of Lynn Johnson / Bea Taylor / Shirley Whitley

title: Alouette Grilled Cheese Sandwich
ingredients: 1 bunch watercress, stems removed (or fresh parsley)
12 one inch slices wheat, French or Italian bread
1 6.5oz package of Alouette "Sundried Tomatoes and Basil" or Alouette "Garlic & Herbs Classique" flavored Gourmet Spreadable Cheese
directions: Arrange watercress and tomatoes on 6 slices of the bread.
Spread Alouette "Sundried Tomatoes and Basil" or "Garlic & Herbs Classique" on the remaining slices.
Put sandwiches together.
Pre-heat a skillet to medium.
Brush sandwiches with melted butter and grill on each side until the cheese is warm and the bread is toasted.
Makes 6 sandwiches.
notes: Handwritten addition of 'Sandwich' to the original printed title.

title: Ann's Potato Salad
ingredients: 3# red skin potatoes - cook in beef broth
directions: Cook potatoes in beef broth.
Mix together white wine, salad oil, white wine vinegar, scallions, and minced garlic.
Add sliced red onions.
Add sliced, drained, and chopped kielbasa.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Makes 4 servings.

title: Apple Pancakes with Honey Almond Cream Syrup
ingredients: 4 T finely chopped toasted almonds (for syrup)
directions: In a large bowl, beat eggs and add remaining ingredients (except apple).
Beat until all combined; do not overmix.
Add apple and stir.
Make pancakes and serve with almond syrup on top.
For the syrup: simmer all ingredients (except vanilla) for 5 minutes or until thick.
Add vanilla.
notes: Makes 12 pancakes. Makes 1/2 c syrup.
pdfLink: pdfs/Apple Pancakes with Honey Almond Cream Syrup.pdf

title: Apple Puffed Pancake
ingredients: 2 large apples, peeled and thinly sliced
directions: Preheat oven to 425°.

In a food processor fitted with the metal blade or a large bowl, combine eggs, milk, flour, sugar, vanilla, salt and cinnamon. Process or whisk with a wire whisk until blended. If mixing by hand, the batter will be a little lumpy.
Place butter in a 12-inch fluted porcelain quiche dish or a 9-by-13-inch baking pan. Place in oven until butter melts. Add apple slices and bake until butter sizzles (do NOT allow to brown).
Remove dish from oven. Pour in batter and sprinkle with brown sugar. Bake 20 minutes or until nicely browned and puffed. Serve immediately.
notes: Makes 6 to 8 servings. Nutrients per serving: 335 calories, 20 grams fat (52 percent total calories), 225 milligrams cholesterol, 368 milligrams sodium. Recipe from "Cooking for Entertaining" by Marlene Sorosky.

title: Artichoke Bread
ingredients: 1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
directions: Melt butter; add garlic and sesame, cook stirring constantly till brown.
Stir in artichoke hearts and next 3 ingredients (Monterey Jack, Parmesan, and sour cream).
Cut bread lengthways.
Scoop out middle and mix bread with artichoke mixture.
Pack into cavity and sprinkle with cheddar.
Cover with foil and bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Uncover and bake 5 minutes.
notes: Recipe written on the back of a rental advertisement for Meadow Lane Apartments.

title: Asparagus and Prosciutto Bundles
ingredients: 2-1/2 ounces soft fresh goat cheese (such as Montrachet), room temperature
2 ounces thinly sliced prosciutto, cut into twenty-four 4 x 1-inch strips
directions: Cut stalks from asparagus, leaving 2-inch-long tips. (Reserve stalks for another use.)
Cook tips in large pot of boiling salted water until just crisp-tender, about 1 minute.
Drain. Transfer to paper towels; drain well.
Blend goat cheese, basil, pine nuts, water and orange peel in small bowl. Season with salt and pepper.
Spread scant 1 tsp. filling over each prosciutto strip.
Arrange 2 asparagus tips atop filling at short end of prosciutto.
Roll up prosciutto, enclosing base of asparagus. Press to seal.
notes: Time-saving secret: Make this terrific cocktail party fare a day ahead. Cover and chill.

title: Asparagus with Sage Butter
directions: Preheat oven to 450°.
Toss asparagus c olive oil & 1/2 teas. salt. Spread on baking sheet & roast in the oven for about 5 mins or until spears are tender.
In a small skillet, melt butter, add sage leaves & cook until butter is lightly browned - 2 mins.
Stir in lemon juice & 1/4 teas. salt.
Transfer the asparagus to a warmed platter, spoon sage-lemon butter on top.
Garnish c lemon zest & cheese.
notes: 6 servings

title: Aunt Cheryl's - Apple Cider
directions: Put cloves in orange.
Bake in oven at 350° for 1 hour.
Remove cloves and slice orange.
Add all ingredients together.
Heat in crockpot on low.

title: Aunt Lydias - Crepes
directions: Mix all ingredients.
Cook in crepe pan, using about 1/8 - 1/4 cup.
Brown lightly on each side.
notes: May be frozen.

title: Autumn Harvest Soup
directions: Brown beef in a soup pot.
Add onion and cook 5 minutes more.
Add water and heat up.
Add remaining ingredients, except tomatoes.
Bring to boil, lower temp., cover and simmer for 20 mins. or until veggies are done to your liking.
Add tomatoes with juice, bring to boil, and simmer 10 mins. longer.
Correct to taste.
notes: I dice up whole tomatoes in med. size chunks.

title: Autumn Squash Soup
ingredients: 2 large Granny Smith apples, coarsely chopped
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Place squash, cut side down, on an oiled baking pan; bake 30 minutes or until soft. Let cool and scoop out pulp. Set aside.
In a large sauté pan, melt butter and add onions and apples. Saute over medium low heat for 6-9 minutes or until softened and translucent.
Transfer onion mixture and squash to food processor; add curry and puree.
Slowly add chicken broth while processor is running until soup reaches desired consistency.
Season to taste with salt and pepper.
When ready to serve, warm gently. Pour into bowls and float a tablespoon of warm cream over each serving. Top with a parsley sprig.
notes: Perfect to make ahead for a holiday meal!

title: Avocado Dip
directions: Gradually add the avocado to cream cheese, blending until smooth.
Add lemon juice, Worcestershire sauce, onions & salt & mix thoroughly.
notes: The recipe refers to Worcestershire sauce as 'Worcestershire sauce' and the measurement '1 teak.' is interpreted as '1 teaspoon'.

title: Bacon and Mushroom Dip
directions: Cook bacon until crisp; drain and set aside.
Reserve 2 tablespoons bacon drippings.
Saute mushrooms, onions and garlic in reserved drippings until soft and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Stir in flour, salt and pepper and allow to bubble on medium heat for 2 minutes; stir frequently.
Add cream cheese, Worcestershire and soy sauce; heat on low until cheese melts.
Stir in sour cream and crumbled bacon.
Serve warm. Yields 2 1/2 cups. Serve with melba toast, bread sticks or crackers.
notes: Can be made a day ahead and reheated in a double boiler, or microwave. Additional cooked bacon can be used to garnish the top. Do not allow to boil when reheating. Extra delicious!

title: Baked Potato Soup
ingredients: 6 large baking potatoes, baked and diced with skin on
1/4 - 1/2 cup reduced calorie sharp cheddar cheese, grated
3-4 tablespoons reduced calorie sharp cheddar cheese, grated
2-3 tablespoons green onion tops, chopped finely
directions: Saute onion in oil until tender; add to soup pot.
Stir in flour and cook over medium heat until golden brown; slowly stir in milk and cook over low heat until thickened slightly.
Add potatoes and continue cooking over medium low heat for 10-15 minutes.
Do not allow to boil!
Just before serving, add crumbled bacon, cheese and sour cream and heat completely.
Spoon into bowls and top each with bacon, cheese and green onions.
notes: Great for the football crowd Serve with a citrus fruit salad! Serves 8-10.

title: Basic Split Pea Soup
ingredients: 3/4 lb smoked ham, cubed or 1 ham hock
directions: In a 6-8 quart pot, combine all the ingredients.
Bring to a boil.
Reduce heat, cover and cook on low for 2 hours.
Remove ham and bay leaf.
With immersion blender, puree soup.
Replace ham and serve.
notes: Serves 6-8.

title: Breakfast in a Bun
ingredients: 4 soft rolls (Vienna rolls or hamburger buns)
directions: Saute the ham until lightly browned, combine eggs and milk and beat gently.
Add eggs to the ham and scramble. DO NOT OVERCOOK!
Add seasonings.
While eggs are cooking, lightly toast the buns which have been spread lightly with margarine.
Spoon egg mixture on the bottoms of 4 buns; top each with a slice of cheese.
Place under broiler until the cheese melts.
Remove from oven and cover with top half of bun.
Serve immediately or wrap in aluminum foil and keep warm.
notes: This is a great breakfast to serve to a crowd or for a family that doesn't all eat breakfast at the same time. Add sauteed onions or green pepper for an extra-special taste!

title: Broiled Crab Puffs
ingredients: 1 pound crab meat, special or backfin
6 English muffins, halved and quartered (48 pieces)
directions: Gently pick through crab to remove all shell.
Heat the jar of cheese in a pan of hot water or in the microwave long enough to soften.
Combine all ingredients except crab and muffins; mix well.
Gently add crab.
Spoon crab mixture on uncooked triangles of English muffins.
Freeze the crab-topped muffins for at least 30 minutes before broiling.
When ready to serve, broil until bubbly and slightly golden brown (only takes a few minutes).
notes: Yields 48 pieces. Be sure to use all 48 pieces of muffins; if made too thick, the outside will get too brown before the center cooks. Can be made ahead of time and kept in the freezer for 3-4 weeks before baking; keep well sealed. "The author of this recipe promises they will be the talk of the evening! You can just stand back and listen to everyone carry on!"

title: Bacon, Water Chestnut & Chutney
directions: Cut bacon in half
Spread 1 slice with Dijon mustard
Thin sprinkle with brown sugar
Place a water chestnut on 1 slice
Roll up and secure with a toothpick
Bake 20 minutes in a 350° oven
Drain on paper towel
Serve with warm chutney
Return to oven for 5 minutes at 350°
notes: Use foil lined pans with sides Use a lot of mustard Drain quickly Do not let sit on paper towel

title: Bacon-blue Dip
directions: Beat blue cheese, cream cheese, white wine, and minced onion until fluffy.
Stir in sour cream and crumbled bacon.
Chill.
Serve with green pepper and Fritos.
notes: Dated Sept. 1971. The abbreviation 'c' with a line over it in the original text is standard shorthand for 'with'.

title: Baked Curried Scrambled Eggs
ingredients: 1/4 cup softened butter, sour cream or cottage cheese
2 cups fine cracker crumbs or fresh bread crumbs
1 quart vegetable oil for deep-fat frying
directions: Peel and cut eggs in half, keeping the whites together, so you can put the two halves back together later.

Sieve egg yolks. Add butter or sour cream or cottage cheese, mustard, salt and pepper. Fill halves (level) with yolk mixture. Put the two halves back together using toothpicks through egg at each end to hold firmly together.
Add raw eggs to leftover yolk mixture. Dip stuffed eggs into this mixture, then into crumbs.
Fry breaded eggs in vegetable oil heated to 350° for one-half to one minute or until golden brown. Remove toothpicks and serve hot.
notes: Mrs. Louis Haywood sends this unusual French Fried Stuffed Egg recipe to us from New Richmond, Indiana. While the origin of it is lost, it's been a family favorite for years. Mrs. Haywood especially remembers serving the eggs to her children and their friends at Easter brunch, along with sweet rolls and ambrosia. We think it's a tasty brunch idea for Easter or any other time of year.

title: Baked Fresh Fettuccine with Spinach
ingredients: 1 lb. fettuccine, cooked barely al dente
directions: Rinse spinach, drain & cook in a covered pan until soft - There's no need to add water; the water that clings to the leaves is sufficient.
Drain spinach, press all the liquid from it & chop it.
In a large sauté pan, cook onion, garlic & prosciutto in butter & oil until onion is soft but not brown.
Blend in flour & cook, stirring for 2 min. w/out letting the flour brown.
Add cream slowly & stir until the sauce is smooth.
Blend in spinach, lemon juice, salt, & pepper.
Place freshly cooked fettuccine in a large warm bowl, pour over the spinach sauce, & toss to mix.
Place fettuccine in a buttered gratin dish & sprinkle w/ Parmesan.
Bake in a 375° oven for 10 min. or until cheese browns & the sauce bubbles.
Serves 6

title: Baked Grits
directions: Cook 1 cup grits in 3 cups boiling salted water until thick, stirring constantly.
Add 1 cup milk, cover and cook on low heat for 5 minutes.
Add 2 beaten eggs, 1 roll garlic cheese, and black and red pepper.
Sprinkle paprika on top.
Bake for 30-40 minutes at 375°.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mary Kaye Long. Serves 10-12. (For see Athens Cookbook)

title: Baked Manicotti with Cheese Filling
ingredients: 1 can (2 lb, 3 ounce) Italian tomatoes, undrained
directions: Make Sauce: In hot oil in 5-quart Dutch oven, sauté onion and garlic 5 minutes. Mix in rest of sauce ingredients and 1 1/2 cups water, mashing tomatoes with fork. Bring to boiling, and reduce heat. Simmer mixture, covered and stirring occasionally, 1 hour.

Make Manicotti: In medium bowl, combine 6 eggs, the flour, 1/4 teaspoon salt, and 1 1/2 cups water; with electric mixer, beat just until smooth. Let stand 1/2 hour or longer. Slowly heat an 8-inch skillet. Pour in 3 tablespoons batter, rotating the skillet quickly to spread batter evenly over bottom. Cook over medium heat until top is dry but bottom is not brown. Turn out on a wire rack to cool. Continue cooking until all of the batter is used. As the manicotti cool, stack them with waxed paper between them.

Preheat oven to 350F. Make Filling: In large bowl, combine ricotta, mozzarella, 1/3 cup Parmesan, the eggs, salt, pepper, and parsley; beat with wooden spoon to blend well. Spread about 1/4 cup filling down the center of each manicotti, and roll up.

Spoon 1 1/2 cups sauce into each of two 12-by-8-by-2-inch baking dishes. Place eight rolled manicotti, seam side down, in single layer; top with five more. Cover with 1 cup sauce; sprinkle with Parmesan. Bake, uncovered, 1/2 hour, or until bubbly.

To freeze: Line baking dish with large piece of foil; assemble as directed. Fold foil over to seal, and freeze in dish. When frozen, remove dish. To serve: Unwrap; place in baking dish, and let stand 1 hour to thaw. Bake, covered, 1 hour in 350F oven.

title: Baked Pineapple Pudding
ingredients: 1 #2 size can (20 ounce) unsweetened crushed pineapple, drained
5 slices Pepperidge Farm (or Arnold's) white bread, cubed
directions: Cream butter and sugar together.
Add beaten eggs.
Add drained crushed pineapple and stir just to blend.
Add the cubed bread to the mixture.
Stir gently or fold to blend.
Place in a 1 1/2 - 2 qt casserole dish (greased or ungreased, no cover).
Bake at 350° for 1 hour, or until the top is brown.
notes: Serves 4-6. Can be served hot (traditionally with ham) or cold. The cook notes that you can use a little less sugar, and that you do not need to grease the casserole dish. If using Arnold's bread (which is thicker and larger than Pepperidge Farm), use 5 or 6 slices; if using Pepperidge Farm, use 6 slices. Margarine can be used in place of butter without adverse effects.

title: Banana Nut Bread
directions: Beat oil & sugar together.
Add eggs & banana pulp, beat well.
Add dry ingredients, milk & vanilla.
Mix well & stir in nuts.
Pour into greased & floured loaf pan (9x5x3).
Bake in preheated oven @ 350° for 50 mins.
Cool well.
notes: Recipe by Mary Armada, 1990. Marked as VG.

title: Barbecue Salad
directions: Mix all ingredients well.
Make day ahead of time so it will get flavor.
Keep covered in refrigerator for one week.
notes: Kidney beans and lima beans are marked as optional.

title: Basic Switzerland Cheese Fondue
directions: Grate, shred or dice 1 pound Switzerland Swiss Cheese and dredge with flour.
Cut bread into 1" cubes.
Rub inside of pot with cut garlic clove. Discard garlic.
Place pot on stove. Pour 1½ cups of wine into pot.
Heat over medium flame until wine is warm but not boiling.
Add lemon juice.
Add cheese by handfuls, stirring constantly with wooden spoon until cheese is melted and cheese-wine mixture has the appearance of a light creamy sauce.
Add pepper and nutmeg to taste.
Let boil once.
Remove pot and put on lighted burner on table.
notes: Serves four persons for dinner or 12 to 20 as a snack. Allow 15 minutes for preparation and an additional 15 minutes for cooking. If prepared in advance, keep bread in a closed plastic bag and keep cheese refrigerated in a tightly closed plastic bag.

title: Bean Pasta Soup
directions: In a dutch oven, cook onion, garlic, ham, and oil for 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, water, oregano, thyme, and pepper; heat to boiling.
Stir in pasta and potatoes; cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in zucchini and beans; cook for 3 minutes.
Sprinkle each serving with parmesan cheese.
notes: Recipe by Janet Shawalter, 1-90.

title: Beef Fondue - Creamy Horseradish Sauce
directions: Combine ingredients.
Chill.
notes: Makes 1 1/4 cups

title: Beef Fondue - Tomato Steak Sauce
directions: Mix all ingredients together.
Bring to boil.
Serve hot.
notes: Makes 1 1/2 cups

title: Bishop's Punch
ingredients: 3 bottles (24 ounce. each) white grape juice
directions: Put stock (lemon, orange, and white grape juices) into punch bowl.
When ready to serve, pour 2-4 quarts of chilled ginger ale into bowl over ice mold.
Slice lemons/limes into bowl.
notes: Very good. Serves 30.

title: Black Pearl Chowder
directions: Heat clam chowder, minced clams, and evaporated milk.
Add butter and cook slowly.
Then add heavy cream & dill weed.
notes: Serve w/a little Harvey's Bristol Cream (Sherry)

title: Blistered Green-bean and Corn Frittata
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper
8 ounces green beans, cut into 1-inch pieces (2 cups)
1 cup fresh corn kernels (from 1 large ear)
directions: Preheat broiler, with a rack in upper third. Beat eggs with ½ teaspoon salt and ¼ teaspoon pepper until combined.

Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a medium (10-inch) nonstick skillet over medium-high. Add beans and cook, stirring, until lightly charred and crisp-tender, 5 to 6 minutes. Season with salt and pepper. Add shallot and corn; cook, stirring, until vegetables soften, 2 to 3 minutes. Add eggs; stir with a wooden spoon until large curds form and edges just begin to set, about 30 seconds.

Transfer skillet to oven; broil until puffed and browning in spots and eggs are just set, about 2 minutes. Let stand 5 minutes before slicing. Meanwhile, toss tomatoes with remaining 1 tablespoon oil, vinegar, and parsley; season with salt and pepper. Serve salad with frittata.
notes: Active time: 25 min. | Total time: 35 min. | Serves: 4

title: Bloody Bull Shot
directions: Keep refrigerated
Add vodka when serving or plain
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mom Kellett

title: Blue Cheese Whip
directions: Soften
Whip
Rechill
Serve w/ crackers or celery
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Date: 6-94. Submitted by Barbara Tyler.

title: Boston Baked Beans
ingredients: 1 orange (sliced thin, use rind, but remove seeds)
directions: Layer in a 2-quart deep casserole:
1. 1/2 onion & orange slices
2. 1/3 beans
3. all of the brown sugar
4. 1/3 beans
5. remaining onion & orange slices
6. 1/3 beans
7. pour maple syrup over all
Cover casserole and bake 6 hours at 300°
Stir before serving
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of: Jeri; Serves 8-10 servings

title: Brandy Eggnog Sauce
directions: Blend sugar with beaten egg yolks until smooth.
Add brandy and vanilla; fold in whipped cream.
notes: Makes 7/8 cup.

title: Breakfast Casserole
ingredients: 1 pound sausage (hot/mild), broken up then drained
Bread crumbs (enough to cover the bottom of the pan)
directions: Grease 9x13" pan.
Cover the bottom of the pan with bread crumbs.
Beat eggs, milk, dry mustard, and salt together.
Put the drained sausage over the bread crumbs.
Pour the egg mixture over the sausage.
Cover with 1 cup of cheddar cheese.
Refrigerate overnight or in the morning.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes.
notes: The recipe specifies to refrigerate overnight or in the morning before baking.

title: Broccoli Casserole
ingredients: 1 pkg. broccoli spears (or cut), chopped & drained
directions: Saute onion in butter.
Add broccoli, rice, soup, cheese, water & milk.
Bake in greased casserole at 350° for 30-40 minutes, uncovered.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mom Willett. Serves 6.

title: Broccoli Salad
directions: Mix the dressing ingredients (mayo, sugar, vinegar) together.
Mix all salad ingredients together.
Save bacon and dressing to mix in at the last minute.
notes: The recipe specifies adding the dressing and bacon at the last minute before serving.

title: Broccoli and Cheese Stuffed Potato
ingredients: 4 medium-large baking potatoes, baked and cooled slightly
1 cup small broccoli flowerets, steamed until fork tender
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Cut baked potatoes in half lengthwise.
Carefully spoon potato out of shells; save shells.
Mash potatoes with margarine until fluffy; add milk, as needed, to make a soft, smooth mixture. DO NOT ADD TOO MUCH MILK!
Add cheese, salt and broccoli; mix gently.
Rub outside of shells lightly with oil; fill centers with potato mixture.
Place in a shallow pan; bake 20-25 minutes or until cheese melts and potatoes are golden brown.
Yields 8 halves.
notes: Can be prepared early in the day and baked at serving time. Delicious as a vegetable entrée! "A meal in itself!"

title: Brunch Eggs for 20
directions: Scramble eggs and milk in butter. Scramble eggs one dozen at a time.
Heat soup until smooth.
Add sherry, mushrooms, and onions.
In 2 - 9"x13" pans, layer eggs-soup-cheese (2 layers of each).
Place cheese on top.
Refrigerate overnight.
Put in cold oven and set at 300°.
Bake for 1 hour.
Sprinkle with paprika and parsley.

title: Brunch Dish
ingredients: 1/4 cup chopped green pepper (can mix in some red peppers)
1 can cream of chicken soup, undiluted
1/2 can or more (to taste) canned french fried onion rings
directions: Mix H2O & soup; add rest of ingredients except topping.
Mix well.
Put into casserole dish.
Add topping (crushed for top).
Bake at 350 until hot & bubbly.
notes: Can cover with foil at start to prevent too much browning. Can make ahead and top before baking.

title: Buckwheat Pancakes
directions: Scald milk; add water and scalded milk together.
Dissolve yeast and sugar in milk/water mixture.
Add both flours (sifted) and salt to the mixture.
Cover and let rise overnight in a warm place.
In the morning, add 1/4 cup warm water and 1/2 teaspoon baking soda.
Use a hot griddle (450°) in which bacon has been cooked or solid shortening.
Turn once when bubbles begin to rise on pancake.
notes: May serve with (Stoneyfield Farm) Vanilla yogurt & fruit or maple syrup.

title: Carrot Ginger Soup
ingredients: 1 2-3 inch piece fresh ginger, peeled and chopped coarsely
8 large carrots, peeled and chopped coarsely
directions: Heat oil over low heat in a large, heavy saucepan with tight fitting lid; add onions and sauté until translucent.
Add ginger and sauté an additional 2 minutes.
Increase heat to medium and add stock and carrots; cover, reduce to simmer and cook until carrots are very tender.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Puree in small amounts and serve warm or chilled.
Serves 6-8.
notes: Soup can be prepared a day ahead and gently reheated. If preparing a day ahead, use a 2-inch piece of ginger.

title: Cheese Soufflé
ingredients: 8 ounces sharp cheese, cut into chunks
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Divide the ingredients in half and process in the blender on high speed.
Pour mixture into a greased uncovered 1 1/2 quart casserole.
Bake 50-60 minutes.
notes: This can be prepared a day ahead and baked the following day or it can be whipped up at the last minute. Foolproof! You would never guess it's made with bread! Delicious!

title: Clare's Salad Nicoise
ingredients: 1 6.7-ounce jar of Italian tuna (or 7-ounce can of good-quality tuna)
About 9 new potatoes, cooked and chilled and sliced just before using
1 cup green beans, cooked and chilled
½ cup nicoise olives (or other black olives), sliced
directions: Assemble vinaigrette at bottom of salad bowl: Add a glug of extra-virgin olive oil, about a third as much red wine vinegar, a smidge of sugar and an ample spoonful of Dijon mustard. No precise measurements needed. Whisk the ingredients and taste, making adjustments to your liking.
Atop the vinaigrette, arrange the tuna, eggs, tomatoes, potatoes, green beans, avocado and olives.
Toss well and serve immediately with a fresh baguette and chilled white or rosé wine.
notes: Makes 3 servings.

title: Crab Meat Quiche
ingredients: 8 ounces crab meat, regular, special or backfin
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Beat egg white until foamy; brush pie crusts with beaten egg white.
Prick bottom and sides of crust; bake for 5 minutes and cool.
Pick through crab 3 times to remove all shell.
Divide crab evenly and place half in the bottom of each pie crust.
Sauté bacon until golden brown. Remove bacon, drain and crumble; place on top of crab.
Sauté onion in bacon grease until soft; drain and distribute over crab.
Beat milk, egg, salt, pepper and lemon juice. Pour over crab; top with cheese.
Sprinkle with chives and paprika. Place on cookie sheet and bake 35 minutes. Serve hot.
Serves 3-6.
notes: Do not use deep-dish pie crusts. Frozen quiche may be baked while still frozen. Bake 40-45 minutes. Serve with sliced lemon and a spinach salad!

title: Cranberry Nut Bread
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups Ocean Spray Fresh or Frozen Cranberries, coarsely chopped
directions: Preheat oven to 350F.
Grease a 9 x 5-inch loaf pan.
Mix together flour, sugar, baking powder, salt and baking soda in a medium mixing bowl.
Stir in orange juice, oil, orange peel and egg.
Mix until well blended.
Stir in cranberries and nuts.
Spread evenly in loaf pan.
Bake for 55 minutes or until a toothpick inserted in the center comes out clean.
Cool on rack for 15 minutes.
Remove from pan; cool completely.
notes: Makes 1 loaf. For more great fresh cranberry recipes visit www.oceanspray.com.

title: Creamed Spinach
ingredients: 1 10-ounce package frozen leaf spinach, cooked and drained OR 1 pound fresh spinach, cleaned and washed
directions: Cook frozen spinach by directions on package.
Melt butter at full power in 1 quart covered microwave-safe bowl; add onions. Cover and cook on full power for 3 minutes; stir once during cooking.
Add flour and mix to a smooth paste.
Gradually blend in milk; stir until well blended.
Return dish to microwave and cook on full power for 2 1/2-3 minutes until well thickened. Stir 3 or 4 times during cooking.
Remove from oven and add remaining ingredients; fold in drained spinach and serve hot. Serves 4.
notes: To cook fresh spinach: use only water that clings to spinach after washing. Place in microwave-safe dish, cover and microwave for 3-5 minutes or until just done. Do not overcook. Drain well. Popular with people that don't even like spinach!

title: Creamy Cole Slaw
directions: Place all ingredients in a large bowl.
Pour dressing over all and toss.
Allow to sit at least 6 hours before serving. It is best made one day ahead.
Serves 8.
notes: This is especially good with pork dishes and barbecue. Everyone will think you made your own delicious boiled cole slaw dressing!

title: California Caviar
directions: Combine all ingredients and serve with corn chips.
notes: Recipe attributed to Robin.

title: Canadian Bacon Puff
ingredients: 8 ounce. cheddar cheese - 1 pkg Old English Sharp
directions: Butter bread slices.
Butter 9x13 dish.
Arrange 8 slices of bread in dish.
Cut cheese into 8 slices - place on bread.
Place C. bacon over cheese - top with remaining bread slices.
Combine eggs, milk, salt & white pepper - mix.
Pour over bread - cover & refrigerate overnight.
Bake @ 350 (preheat).
Place dish in water bath & bake 1 hr. or until puffy & brown.
Cut into 8 servings.
notes: Serve with currant jelly on side. Recipe by Laura Gaugh, 11/88.

title: Carrot Cheese Ring
directions: Add butter to hot mashed carrots.
Combine other ingredients.
Mix well.
Place in well greased ring mold or casserole.
Set in pan of hot water.
Bake about 40 mins. or until set at 325°–350°.
notes: There are notations for a 1 1/2 recipe: (3) cups carrots, (3) cups cheese, (4) eggs, (3/4 cup) milk, (3/4 stick) butter. Recipe attributed to Mary Kaye Longe.

title: Carrot Soup with Orange and Tarragon
directions: Melt butter in heavy large pot over medium heat. Add carrots and onion; sauté until onion is soft, about 8 minutes.
Add broth; cover and bring to boil. Reduce heat, uncover, and simmer until carrots are tender, about 10 minutes.
Working in batches, puree soup in blender until very smooth. Return soup to pot.
Stir in orange juice, brandy, and chopped tarragon. Simmer 5 minutes for flavors to blend.
Season to taste with salt and pepper. Garnish soup with tarragon sprigs and serve.
notes: Serves 4.
pdfLink: pdfs/Carrot Soup with Orange and Tarragon.pdf

title: Carrots - Hot or Cold
directions: Mix the onion, green pepper, tomato soup, sugar, oil, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, salt, and pepper together and cook for 20 minutes.
Cook carrots until tender, then drain.
Layer carrots and sauce.
Serve hot or cold.
notes: Recipe explicitly notes it can be served hot or cold.

title: Celebration Punch
directions: Mix corn syrup and brandy
Stir in Sauterne
Add soda and champagne
notes: Very good. Recipe from the kitchen of: Jane Keyer. Serves: 25-4 ounce. servings.

title: Celery Salt Dressing
directions: Add oil to blender slowly.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Excellent.

title: Chafing Dish Crab
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Mix all ingredients and pour into a buttered 2 quart casserole.
Bake 20-30 minutes.
Spoon into chafing dish and keep warm. If your chafing dish has a glass liner, prepare crab dish in the liner.
Serves 30.
notes: Can be prepared one day ahead and chilled until time to bake. Be sure to pick through the crab three times to remove all shell. Serve this divine dish on Melba toast rounds or toasted bread triangles.

title: Challah Bread Jewish Bread
directions: Let rise
Punch down
Let rise again
Knead and shape
Brush with egg yolk and poppy seeds
Let rise
Bake at 350° for 35-40 minutes
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Aunt Lydia

title: Champagne Punch
directions: Mix in punch bowl.
notes: Serves 25. Recipe credited to Donna Dawson.

title: Charleston Pickled Shrimp
directions: In a large bowl, alternate layers of shrimp with layers of onions, bay leaves, and onions.
Prepare sauce: Mix or put in blender the oil, mustard, Worcestershire, catsup, vinegar, red pepper, and garlic.
Pour sauce over the shrimp to cover.
Refrigerate at least 24 hours.
Turn at intervals.
notes: Recipe dated 1969. Attribution: Bettie Baldwin.

title: Cheese Fondue with Pesto
ingredients: 1 1/2 pound Gruyere or domestic Swiss cheese, shredded
directions: Rub the inside of the fondue pot with the cut surfaces of the garlic. Discard garlic.
On the stove, heat wine in fondue pot until it just begins to bubble. Meanwhile, toss cheese with flour.
Add cheese mixture to fondue pot and stir over medium heat with a wooden spoon until cheese is melted and smooth. Stir in kirsch, if using.
When cheese begins to bubble, remove from stove and stir pesto into the cheese in a swirl. Carry to the table.
Using the warmer that comes with the pot, keep warm enough that cheese remains liquid but does not bubble. Serve with cubes of crusty bread for dipping.
If cheese thickens at the table, stir in a little more wine.
notes: Makes 6 entree servings. Nutrients per serving: 530 calories, 35 grams protein, 2.5 grams carbohydrate, 40 grams fat (68 percent total calories), 126 milligrams cholesterol, trace fiber, 420 milligrams sodium.

title: Cheese Krispies
directions: Using mixer, cream butter & cheese.
Add red pepper to flour & mix this gradually to cheese mixture.
Add Rice Krispies & work into cheese mixture using hand or spoon.
Roll into sm. balls (marble size).
Place on cookie sheet & flatten c fork.
Bake @ 300° for 10-15 minutes.
notes: Makes about 100

title: Cheese Log
ingredients: 3 tablespoons onion, grated or finely chopped
directions: Mix all ingredients, but set aside a portion of the chopped pecans.
Chill well.
Form into a log or ball and roll in the remaining pecans.
Rechill until serving.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Krista Dinges.

title: Cheese and Sausage Brunch
directions: Trim crusts from bread and butter one side.
Place buttered side down in a 9x13 pan.
Layer cheddar cheese, sausage, monterey jack & chilies.
Beat eggs & milk with pepper, paprika & mustard.
Pour over layers.
Refrigerate overnight covered with foil.
Bake uncovered, 350° for 50 min.
Let stand 10 min. before cutting.
notes: From: Geri

title: Cheesy Mashed Potato Casserole
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Heat water, butter and milk in a saucepan.
Combine potatoes, milk mixture and salt; beat with an electric mixer.
Add sour cream and egg and mix well.
Place in a lightly buttered pie plate and top with cheese.
Bake 25-30 minutes or until the cheese is melted.
Serves 4-6.
notes: This can be prepared ahead of time. Cover and refrigerate until ready to bake. This casserole is a great accompaniment for any dish from hot dogs to rare roast beef.

title: Cherry Delight
directions: Prepare Dream Whip and fold into above mixture (use Cool Whip 8 oz).
Pour into lg. jello mold or cake pan.
Freeze until a few mins. before serving.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Also attributed to Joan Evile Warren.

title: Cherry Shakes - Blends
directions: Pour 1 cup boiling water and jello into blender container, cover and blend until smooth.
Chill.
At serving time, divide cherry mixture evenly between 12-14 12 oz glasses.
Add a scoop of ice cream.
Stir to muddle.
Fill glasses with milk.
Stir to mix.

title: Cherrycranberry Relish
directions: In sauce pan, place shallots in boiling water. Boil 1-2 mins, drain & peel; separate into cloves.
In heavy saucepan cook shallots, butter to coat well then add sugar + 1 T white vinegar - cook until caramelized.
Add remaining vinegar + salt - boil 1 min.
Add cherries + white wine - cook until tender 45 mins.
Then add cranberries + water - cook until cranberries pop open about 1-2 mins.
Cool. Serve @ rm temp. May be made ahead (refrig).
notes: Lauren G. 1998, Excellent

title: Chicken Cheese Soup
directions: Saute carrots, onions & butter together until onions are clear.
Add flour, milk, chicken broth - cook until thick.
Add chicken, white wine, Worcestershire sauce and cheese.
Cook until blended and heated through.
notes: Serves 4-6. Recipe from the kitchen of Cathie Van Pelt.

title: Chicken Soup
directions: Boil chicken with carrots, celery, onions, and seasonings.
Boil tiny noodles in separate H2O.
When finished cooking, strain the stock.
Add the drained noodles to the stock.
Serve the soup with a sprinkle of fresh chopped parsley.
notes: The abbreviation 'c' in the text denotes 'with'.

title: Chili Con Queso - Bunny Lazina
ingredients: 3 sm. cans of green chili peppers
directions: Grind onions and garlic in food chopper, but keep peppers separate and grind last.
Brown onions and garlic in a small amount of butter first, then add peppers.
Drain tomatoes (do not use any of the juice) and add to the above mixture and simmer 1 hr.
Add cheese cut in chunks and cook until cheese is melted.
notes: Can be done ahead and reheated in a double boiler. Makes 2 qts.

title: Chilled Vidalia Onion and Watercress Soup
ingredients: 2 1/2 pounds Vidalia or other sweet onions, chopped coarse
4 cups loosely packed watercress sprigs, coarse stems discarded
directions: In a heavy kettle cook onions in oil, covered, over moderate heat, stirring occasionally, 30 minutes.
Reduce heat to moderately low and cook onions, uncovered, stirring, until just pale golden, about 45 minutes.
Add potato, broth, watercress, and sage and simmer, covered partially, 15 minutes.
In a blender purée soup in batches and transfer as puréed to a bowl.
Stir in half-and-half and salt and pepper to taste.
Chill soup, covered, at least 4 hours or overnight.
notes: Makes about 8 cups.
pdfLink: pdfs/Chilled Vidalia Onion and Watercress Soup.pdf

title: Chive Biscuits with Cheddar Cheese
ingredients: 2 T. milk for brushing biscuit tops
directions: Blend biscuit mix, cheese and chives.
Mix gently with milk beginning with 1/2 cup and adding additional milk as needed to form a soft ball.
Turn onto floured board and gently knead 6 to 8 times.
Roll out 3/4 inch thick and cut with biscuit cutter.
Place on lightly greased baking sheet and brush tops with milk.
Bake at 450 for 10 minutes or until golden brown.
notes: ©1995 Shenandoah Growers — Harrisonburg, Virginia

title: Choc. Sauce (for Cottage Pudding)
directions: Mix all together.
Cook until thick.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mother Willey

title: Choc. Sauce - Joan Eisele
directions: Mix well until butter melts.
Then add 1/2 cup milk - stir const. until it boils and thickens.
notes: The recipe calls for 4 squares of chocolate (likely baking chocolate).

title: Christmas Pecans
directions: Preheat oven to 300°.
In a measuring cup mix sugar, salt and cinnamon, set aside.
In a large bowl, whip egg white and water until frothy.
Pour in pecans and mix until they are coated with egg white.
Pour in sugar mixture and mix until coated.
Pour on ungreased cookie sheet (spread out), and bake 40 minutes (you have to scrape off cookie sheet!).
notes: Recipe attributed to Susan Dawson.

title: Christmas Red Cheese Ball
ingredients: dash of ea. garlic, onion & celery salt
directions: Mix all ingredients well.
Let it get firm in refrigerator.
Mold into ball and roll in 1/2 cup coarsely snipped dried parsley.
30 mins. before serving remove to soften.
Serve w/ crackers or rye rounds.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Ann Luther.

title: Cinnamon Cream Syrup
directions: In a small saucepan, combine sugar, syrup, water & cinnamon.
Bring to boil over med. heat, stirring constantly.
Cook & stir 2 min. more.
Remove from heat & cool 5 min.
Stir in the evap. milk.
Serve warm over pancakes or waffles.
notes: Yields 1 2/3 cups.

title: Cinnamon-pecan Biscuits
ingredients: 2 cans refrigerator biscuits (10 count), cut into quarters
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Melt butter in saucepan, add remaining ingredients except biscuits.
Heat until mixture begins to boil.
Remove from heat. Add biscuits and stir.
Pour mixture into greased tube cake pan.
Bake at 400° for 15 mins.
Unmold on serving platter immediately.
notes: Serves 8-10. Recipe by Cheryl Bugen '86.

title: Citrus-sauced Green Beans
ingredients: 2 T. fresh dill or fresh fennel tops
directions: Orange Sherry Sauce: Combine orange juice, cream sherry, lemon juice, and 1 1/2 tsp cornstarch. Cook, stirring often, about 4 minutes. Remove from heat and cover to keep warm.
Lemon Dill Sauce: Combine 1/2 cup lemon juice, broth, sugar, and 1 1/2 tsp cornstarch. Cook, stirring often, about 4 minutes.
Remove from heat and add 2 T. fresh dill or fresh fennel tops.
Add 1/2 cup sliced almonds (toasted) or fresh dill sprigs or fennel tops to the beans.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Patty Jellison. Serves 6-8.

title: Clam Canapes
directions: Whip cheese with fork.
Add clams & mix well.
Add rest & mix well.
Place in refrigerator in a covered dish.
When ready to serve, heap generously on white salty crackers & bake at 300° for 20 min.
Sprinkle paprika for looks!

title: Coffee Cake
directions: Mix ingredients together.
Pour into large cookie sheet with sides.
Add topping.
Bake 20 mins @ 350°.
Sprinkle with powdered sugar while still hot.
notes: Recipe by Donna Dawson, 1986. Marked as 'VG'.

title: Coffee Liqueur
directions: Mix sugar, coffee and water.
Stir until sugar and coffee are dissolved, over low flame.
Put aside and cool.
Put in glass jar or crock with lid, add vodka and vanilla bean.
Stir every day, and let sit for three weeks.
notes: The text suggests using this liqueur to add sophistication to cake and cream desserts, or as a topping for vanilla ice cream, Bavarian cream, angel food cake, or pound cake. The contributor also recommends the book "Making Cordials and Liqueurs at Home" by John P. Farrell for further recipes.

title: Coffee Mocha
ingredients: 1/2 gal vanilla or coffee ice cream
directions: Mix Nescafe w/ 1 qt boiling H2O.
Add 3 qts cold water.
Add choc. syrup, vanilla & rum.
Add milk to above before serving.
Top w/ softened ice cream.
notes: Recipe attributed to 'Des Barrons (1963 - H. Blis)'.

title: Corn Pudding
directions: Mix together.
Pour into a dish sprayed with Pam.
Bake at 350° for approx. 55 minutes.
notes: Recipe attributed to Peggy Sallé, Manakin.

title: Cornbread Dressing - Hodge
ingredients: Milk (enough to make not too thick)
Broth (enough to make the dressing soupy)
directions: Make cornbread the night before: Combine cornmeal, flour, salt, sugar, baking powder, shortening, and enough milk to make a batter ready to pour into a pan.
Pour into a greased pan and bake at 400°.
The next day, crumble the cornbread into a bowl (can also use biscuits, which are better).
Chop onions and add to the bowl with celery, celery seed, sage, and poultry seasoning.
Stir in 2 eggs and enough broth to make the dressing soupy so it won't be too dry when done.
Dot with butter before putting into the oven.
Cook dressing until it bubbles at 350°.
notes: Serve with giblet gravy.

title: Corny Pudding
directions: Mix all ingredients except corn. Blend well.
Add corn and mix well.
Pour into greased baking dish and bake at 400°F for 40 min.

title: Country Breakfast Casserole
ingredients: 4 c. frozen diced hash brown potatoes - thawed
directions: Cook sausage and onions. Drain.
In an 8x8x2" baking dish, layer potatoes, 1/2 of cheese, sausage/onion mixture, and remaining cheese.
In a bowl, combine eggs, milk, and seasonings.
Pour over cheese.
Cover and chill overnight.
Bake covered at 350° oven for 50-55 minutes.
notes: Recipe from Jeri

title: Crab Bisque
directions: Cook onions and butter/margarine together until onions are almost translucent.
Add milk and cream cheese.
Heat slowly until cream cheese melts.
Add crab meat, cooking sherry, and salt.
Heat and serve.
notes: Recipe by Clifford Porter, 10/97. Yields 4 servings.

title: Crab Dip
directions: Bake 350° - 20 mins.
Serve w/ crackers.
notes: Recipe by Carol Bowery; marked as 'excellent'.

title: Crab Mousse
directions: Heat soup to boiling, let cool a little.
Melt gelatin in water.
Add to soup.
Pour cooled mixture over cream cheese.
Beat.
Add other ingredients.
Pour in oiled mold.
Chill a few hours.
notes: Recipe credit: Laura Hodge

title: Crab or Lobster Bisque
ingredients: 1 can cream of chicken & mushroom soup
directions: Mix all together and heat thoroughly.
Do not boil.
notes: From the kitchen of Patty Jellison; Serves 4.

title: Cranberry Jello Mold
ingredients: 1 can (16 ounce) whole cranberry sauce with berries
directions: Pour 1 1/2 cups boiling water over jello until melted.
Add other ingredients and pour into a 9x13 pan.
Refrigerate.
notes: Please bring to church on Friday between 10:00 and 11:00. Note regarding the Huguenot Luncheon, Saturday October 25th.

title: Cranberry Nut Crescents
ingredients: 1 (8 ounce) and 1 (4 ounce) Pillsbury Refrigerated Crescent Dinner Rolls
directions: Heat oven to 375°.
Unroll dough and separate into triangles.
Sprinkle with sugar, cranberries, and walnuts. Press lightly into dough.
Roll loosely from shortest end triangle to opposite point.
Place on ungreased cookie sheet; curve into crescent shape.
Bake 11-13 min. or until golden brown.
Sprinkle powdered sugar over.
notes: Can be shaped and covered up to two hours before baking. Best to serve warm.

title: Cranberry Orange Relish
directions: Put cranberries through food chopper also oranges.
Add sugar & chill.

title: Cranberry Salad
directions: Dissolve jello in water and chill.
Grind cranberries, apple, and orange.
Cover fruit with sugar and let sit.
Combine all ingredients and chill until set.
notes: Recipe yields 8-10 servings. The directions are implied by standard jello salad preparation techniques based on the listed ingredients.

title: Cranberry and Walnut Muffins
directions: In medium bowl, mix flour, sugar, baking powder, soda, peel, nutmeg, cinnamon and ginger.
Cut in margarine with pastry blender.
Mix in juice, vanilla and eggs; gently fold into dry mixture just until moistened.
Gently fold in cranberries and walnuts.
Spoon into 18 well-greased or paper-lined muffin cups.
Bake in preheated 350 oven for 20-25 minutes or until center springs back when pressed lightly.
Yields 18.
notes: A great holiday breakfast treat! Delicious warm!

title: Cream Cheese Puff
directions: Remove crusts from bread and roll flat.
Mix together the cream cheese, egg yolk, and 1/4 cup sugar.
Spread the mixture on the bread thinly.
Roll up and cut in pieces.
Dip in melted butter.
Dip in a mixture of 1 tablespoon cinnamon and 1 cup sugar.
Bake at 400° for 8-10 minutes.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Betty Korpeck. Noted as 'very good'.

title: Cream Sauce Mix
directions: Mix thoroughly the dry milk, flour, and salt.
Mix in the margarine to small pea consistency.
To make 1 cup of sauce: take 1/2 cup of the dry mixture and 1 cup of cold water.
Stir on medium heat until thick.
notes: Recipe attributed to Maurine. The mixing of the margarine with the dry ingredients is akin to 'cutting in' fat.

title: Creamed Onions - Thanksgiving
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups half & half or regular milk
directions: Peel onions and boil until just tender in salt water.
Drain well.
Melt butter in a heavy saucepan. Add flour and cook - slowly add milk stirring constantly with a wire whisk.
Continue cooking until it thickens.
Add cheese, paprika & nutmeg.
Pour over well-drained cooked onions that have been placed in a buttered casserole dish.
Heat in oven at 350° for 30 minutes before serving.
notes: Happy Eating. Mom 11/97

title: Crunchy Cabbage Salad
directions: Mix dry ingredients.
Mix dressing.
Add dressing just before serving.
notes: The sesame seeds and sliced almonds should be toasted.

title: Curried Broccoli Soup
directions: Melt butter, add onion and stir.
Cook 4 mins or until tender.
Add flour and curry powder, cook and stir until blended and thick (1 min).
Gradually stir in chicken broth and frozen broccoli.
Bring to boil, simmer uncovered 5 mins.
Add half & half.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Nancy [Surname illegible]

title: Dutch Apple Pancake
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups Golden Delicious apples, peeled and very thinly sliced
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
In a 9-inch glass pie plate, melt margarine or butter in oven.
Stir in apples, sugar, cinnamon and nutmeg; bake for 10 minutes.
In a medium bowl, combine all batter ingredients; blend well.
Pour over apple mixture.
In small bowl combine all topping ingredients except maple syrup; sprinkle over batter.
Bake an additional 15 to 20 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.
Remove from oven and allow to stand for 2 minutes; invert on serving plate.
Cut into wedges and serve with hot maple syrup.
notes: The perfect lazy vacation breakfast! Serve with scrambled cheese eggs and fresh fruit!

title: Dana and Mike's Caribbean Rum Punch
pdfLink: pdfs/Dana and Mike's Caribbean Rum Punch.pdf

title: Danish Puff
directions: Crust: Cut butter into flour.
Crust: Sprinkle with H2O.
Crust: Round into ball - Divide in half.
Crust: Pat out 2 strips approximately 12 inch x 3 inch on cookie sheet.
Topping: Mix H2O + butter - Bring to boil.
Topping: Add flavoring - Remove from heat.
Topping: Stir in flour - Beat in eggs one at time.
Topping: Divide in half, spread on top pastry to edges.
Bake at 350°.
Cool - Spread with frosting and sliced almonds.
Frosting: Mix milk, confectioners sugar, butter, and vanilla to taste.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Jackie Pfrang.

title: Dessert Coffee Cake Ring
directions: Pour scalded milk over sugar, salt, and shortening and stir until dissolved.
Cool to lukewarm.
Stir egg and crumbled yeast into this until dissolved.
Stir in 1 cup flour, beat smooth with egg beater.
Stir in remaining flour and beat with spoon until blended and smooth.
Brush top with melted shortening, cover with towel, and let rise in a warm place until double, about 2 hours.
Press down and roll out into a 13" by 7" rectangle.
Brush with butter, sugar, etc., and roll.
Let rise until double, about 45 minutes.
Bake 15 minutes at 400°F.
notes: Double recipe for 2 cakes. Labeled 'excellent'.

title: Dilly Bread
ingredients: 1 cup large curd cream style cottage cheese, heated to lukewarm
directions: Lightly spoon onion into butter.
Soften yeast in water.
Combine cheese, sugar, onion, dill seed, salt, egg, and softened yeast in bowl and mix well.
Add enough flour to make stiff dough, stirring well on mixer after each addition.
Let rise until double, about 1 1/4 hours.
Stir down, turn into greased 9 1/2 x 5 x 2 inch pan.
Set to rise 40 minutes until light.
Bake at 350° for 50 minutes.
Place foil over for last 15 minutes.
Brush with butter.
notes: Makes 1 loaf.

title: Do-ahead French Toast
directions: In small saucepan, melt butter. Add brown sugar and cook until syrupy.
Pour into a 9x13 casserole dish.
Remove ends from loaf and slice bread into 12 slices about 1 inch thick. Place over sugar syrup.
In med. bowl, beat eggs, milk, and vanilla. Pour over bread.
Cover dish and refrig. overnight.
Preheat oven to 350°. Uncover and bake for 45 mins.
Sift confectioners' sugar over top.
Serve with syrup.
notes: Makes 6 servings

title: Drambuie
directions: Steep root in Scotch overnight
Strain
Let sit 2 months
Strain again
notes: The recipe refers to a '5th' of Scotch, which is a traditional bottle size equivalent to approximately 750ml.

title: Dutch Hot Chocolate and Chocolate Cappuccino
directions: For Dutch Hot Chocolate: Heat 3/4 cup milk in a saucepan. Sprinkle 1 Tbs. sweet ground chocolate over hot milk, stir until dissolved. Add sugar to taste, serve.

For Chocolate Cappuccino: Mix 1 heaping teaspoon sweet ground chocolate with a little half and half in a cup or heavy glass. Heat additional half and half with the steam jet of an espresso machine or in a saucepan on stove. (If heating on the stove, beat with a whisk or beater until frothy.) Finish filling cup or glass with hot half and half, add 1 oz. cognac, stir and serve.
notes: Published by Williams-Sonoma, 1985. Reference number 23358.
pdfLink: pdfs/Dutch Hot Chocolate and Chocolate Cappuccino.pdf

title: Eastern Shore Oyster Stew
ingredients: 1 pint of oysters, standards or selects, undrained
directions: Combine all ingredients except sprigs of parsley and crackers in a large heavy pot.
Cook over lowest heat for 1 hour.
Do not cover.
Garnish with fresh parsley and serve hot.
Serve with crackers.
notes: This unusual sounding recipe produces a creamy oyster stew with tender oysters and delightfully crisp vegetables. Double or triple and cook the same way to serve a crowd! Serves 4-6.

title: Eggplant Parmigiana
ingredients: 1 medium eggplant, pared and sliced in 1/2-inch slices
directions: Mix flour and salt, and place in shallow dish.
Dip eggplant slices in egg and then in flour mixture.
Brown slices until golden in hot shortening; drain well on brown paper.
Place one layer of eggplant in a glass 8 x 8 baking dish; top with half of the Parmesan cheese, Italian sauce and mozzarella.
Repeat.
Bake at 375 for 15-20 minutes or until cheese is completely melted.
Serves 6.
notes: This dish can be prepared early in the day and baked when ready to serve. So rich it can serve as a main dish!

title: Egg Nog - Mom Willett's
ingredients: 1 quart Apple Brandy or Blended Whiskey
2 quarts milk (or 3 quarts for a milder drink)
directions: Separate eggs and set whites aside.
Blend yolks and sugar.
Set electric mixer on low speed and add brandy. Pour brandy in a steady stream to cook eggs.
Add milk and cream.
Beat egg whites until they form a soft peak.
Whip cream to a fluffy consistency.
Fold in egg whites and whipping cream.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
notes: Written at the top: 'excellent'

title: Eggs Benedict Casserole
ingredients: 2 packages (10 to 12 ounces total) Canadian bacon
1/2 cup heavy (OR whipping) cream (for Hollandaise sauce)
directions: Cut the muffins into 1/2-inch cubes and set aside. Cut the Canadian bacon into 1/2-inch squares and set aside.
Whisk the eggs, milk, and onion powder in a 2-quart bowl.

Spray a 9-by-13-inch glass or ceramic baking dish with cooking oil spray. Scatter half of the Canadian bacon evenly in the bottom of the dish. Top with the muffin cubes, then the remaining Canadian bacon. Pour the egg mixture over the casserole, cover with plastic wrap, and refrigerate overnight (or at least 8 hours).
Preheat oven to 375°F.

Remove casserole from refrigerator, uncover, and sprinkle paprika over the top. Cover with foil and bake for 40 minutes. Remove foil and continue to bake uncovered for about 20 minutes more, until eggs are set and bacon is crisp. Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes before serving.

To make Hollandaise sauce: Cut butter into 4 pieces, place in a 1-quart glass measure or bowl, cover with a paper towel, and microwave on high for 45 seconds to 1 minute until melted. Stir until completely melted.
Separate the eggs, placing yolks in a small bowl and setting whites aside. Beat yolks well and stir into the melted butter.
Stir in cream and lemon juice. Microwave the mixture uncovered on high for 1 to 2 minutes, stopping every 20 seconds to stir until slightly thick.
Remove from microwave, stir in mustard, and serve over casserole.
notes: The sauce may be kept warm in a Thermos container up to 4 hours, or cooled to room temperature and refrigerated in a covered microwave-safe container for up to 24 hours. To rewarm, cover with plastic wrap, pierce to vent, and microwave on 50 percent power for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring halfway through. Do not allow to boil.

title: Eggs Brunch
ingredients: 5 slices bacon, cut in pieces before cooking
5 ounce. dried beef, cut in pieces
2 cans mushrooms, save some for top
directions: To make sauce: Saute bacon until almost done.
In grease, add dried beef, mushrooms, and 1/4 cup butter.
While still hot, add flour and milk.
Add pepper, but NO salt. Stir until thick and smooth.
Mix eggs with evaporated milk and 1/4 teaspoon salt and scramble in 1/4 cup butter.
Butter casserole dish.
Place a small amount of sauce in bottom, then a layer of eggs, layer of sauce, another layer of eggs, and top with sauce.
Garnish with mushrooms.
Heat, covered, for 1 hour at 275°.
Serve with fresh fruit, strawberry sauce, and amaretto.
notes: Serve with ham biscuits and blueberry muffins.

title: Eggs Muchachita
ingredients: 1/2 pt. (1 cup) whipping cream or half & half
8 slices toast or 4 English muffins, split & toasted
directions: Blend cream cheese, whipping cream, sour cream, cheddar cheese, Worcestershire sauce, and seasonings.
Bring to simmering point, stirring constantly.
Break eggs into sauce, cover pan and poach 3-5 minutes or until set.
Serve on toast or muffins.
notes: Serves 4.

title: Eve's Soup
directions: Combine all ingredients in a pot.
Add sherry and a little curry powder.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Eve Schrieder. Serves 6-8.

title: Feta and Sun-dried Tomato Torta
ingredients: 1/2 pound (2 sticks) unsalted butter, cut into pieces
One 8-ounce package cream cheese, at room temperature
Ground white pepper and/or hot pepper sauce or minced, seeded, and deveined fresh red jalapeño pepper (page 20) to taste
8 ounces sun-dried tomatoes, softened and minced (page 22)
directions: Combine the butter, cheeses, garlic, shallot, and vermouth in a food processor with the metal blade and process until smooth, or combine in a bowl.
Season with the pepper hot pepper sauce.
Oil a 4- to 5-cup straight-sided mold, bowl, or pâté terrine. Line with plastic wrap.
Layer in all ingredients in any order you wish. I start with pine nuts, then sun-dried tomatoes, pesto, and the cheese mixture. Repeat until the mold is full.
Fold the plastic wrap over the top and press gently to compact the layers.
Refrigerate until firm, at least 1 hour. Invert onto a platter, remove the plastic, and enjoy!
notes: Imported from archive

title: Fresh Mushroom Tartlets
ingredients: 1/2 pound mushrooms (your choice, or a mixture of button, portabello, cremini, and shitake), finely chopped (for filling)
2 teaspoons finely chopped shallots or green onions (for filling)
1/2 cup heavy cream or half and half (for filling)
directions: Mix all shell ingredients well. Form walnut-sized balls of mixture and use thumbs to press into ungreased miniature muffin tins. Set aside.
Heat butter or margarine in skillet over low heat. Add mushrooms, onions, salt and pepper. Cook over medium heat until vegetables are just soft.
Sprinkle with flour and cook 1-2 minutes, stirring constantly.
Slowly add cream or half and half, stirring constantly until thickened. Cool slightly.
Fill each shell with filling.
Bake in a preheated 450-degree oven for 15-18 minutes, or until filling is set and shells are golden.
Yields 24 tartlets.
notes: For ease of serving, make dough 2-3 days ahead; chill until ready to use. Early in the day, bake tarts for 12-14 minutes. Remove from oven, cool and refrigerate until ready to serve. Pop back in preheated oven for 4-6 minutes or until heated through. "Make plenty; they'll go quickly!"

title: Fresh Spinach Casserole
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Cook the spinach, in a small amount of water, until barely tender.
Drain thoroughly.
Combine all remaining ingredients except crumbs; gently mix with wilted spinach.
Spoon into a buttered shallow baking dish and top with bread crumbs.
Bake in oven for 10 to 15 minutes or until heated through and top is golden brown.
Serves 6-8.
notes: The best bread crumbs are made from torn bread pieces tossed lightly in a small amount of melted butter or margarine. No need to brown; since the browning will occur during baking. Serve with grilled seafood or chicken!

title: Frozen Cranberry Salad
ingredients: 1 8-ounce can crushed pineapple, in heavy syrup (drained well)
directions: Combine cranberry sauce, pineapple, 8 ounces sour cream and pecans.
Blend with an electric mixer; pour into muffin liners which have been placed in muffin tins.
Freeze until ready to serve.
Serves 12.
notes: To serve: Remove foil liners; serve on a lettuce leaf, top with a dollop of sour cream and pineapple chunks. Store in the freezer until ready to serve!

title: Frozen Pineapple Dessert Salad
ingredients: 1 cup mayonnaise or cooked salad dressing
3/4 cup maraschino cherries, drained and chopped
directions: Combine cream cheese with mayonnaise in medium bowl; beat, with spoon or portable electric mixer, until smooth.
Add pineapple, walnuts, and the maraschino cherries; then stir until well mixed.
Beat cream in small bowl just until stiff enough to hold its shape.
Gently fold into cream-cheese mixture until thoroughly combined.
Turn mixture into 1 1/2-quart ring mold that has been rinsed with cold water.
Freeze until firm—about 3 hours.
To serve: Loosen edges of mold with sharp knife. Unmold on lettuce leaves.
notes: Makes 8 to 10 servings.

title: Filling and Topping for Coffee Cake
directions: Combine filling ingredients (melted butter, brown sugar, cinnamon, raisins/dates).
Combine topping ingredients (confectioners' sugar, pecans, warm water).
Put topping on cake after it has cooled slightly.
notes: The recipe is split into a filling and a topping section.
pdfLink: pdfs/Filling and Topping for Coffee Cake.pdf

title: Fire & Ice Tomatoes
ingredients: 1 lg green pepper, sliced in rings
1 lg red onion, sliced in rings
directions: Place tomatoes, green pepper & onion alternately in salad bowl.
Make dressing by mixing vinegar, seasonings & water together. Boil for 1 minute.
While still hot pour over veg.
Cool & chill.
Just before serving peel & slice cucumber & add.
notes: Without cucumber, relish will keep in refrigerator for several days. Serves 6 generously.

title: Fish Chowder - Monozir's
directions: Cut pork into 1/2" cubes; cook in large kettle until brown; remove bits; reserve.
Add onions to pork fat; cook til tender; add potatoes, salt, pepper, water.
Place fish, cut into medium sized pieces on top; cover; simmer 25 mins. or until potatoes are tender. Remove any skin from fish.
Add milk, evaporated milk, butter, pork bits; heat.
notes: Serves 6 Marked as 'good' at the top of the recipe

title: Fondue
ingredients: 6 to 7 ounce. real Swiss cheese (half Emmental and half Gruyere, grated or cut into thin strips)
6 to 8 ounce. white bread (cut into cubes)
1 glass Kirsch or other hard liquor (brandy or gin)
directions: Rub the inside of the Caquelon with the clove of garlic.
Pour the wine and lemon juice into the Caquelon and heat on a strong flame.
As soon as the wine is hot, add the cheese and stir constantly with a wooden spoon.
Once the mixture starts to cook, add the Patent Corn Flour diluted in the glass of Kirsch.
Let it cook for another 2 to 3 minutes.
Place the Caquelon on a burning stove and season with pepper or paprika as desired.
Serve by dipping bread cubes into the mixture, stirring occasionally to prevent burning.
notes: There is a Golden Rule when eating Fondue: the person who drops a piece of bread into the Fondue has to present a bottle to the company or organize the next Fondue evening. Ladies must give a kiss to all other guests if they drop bread.

title: French Dressing - Beed's
directions: Boil sugar, H2O, and lemon juice together for several minutes.
Cool.
Add remaining ingredients.
Beat well.

title: French Green Bean Relish
ingredients: 2 cans french cut green beans, drained well
1 bunch green onions with some top, chopped fine
directions: Combine all ingredients.
Chill before serving.
Serve as a relish.
notes: Recipe by Jerri Burd, 4/2000

title: Fresh Apple Coffee Cake
ingredients: 1 medium apple, peeled and thinly sliced
directions: Preheat oven to 375.
Cream margarine and sugar; blend in applesauce.
Add egg substitute and vanilla; blend well.
With a fork mix together well the presifted flour, baking powder and baking soda.
Gradually add flour mixture and sour cream to creamed mixture, beginning and ending with flour.
When blended, spoon half of batter into sprayed bundt pan.
Layer apples on top of batter; sprinkle with half of topping mixture.
Top with remaining batter and sprinkle with remaining topping.
Bake for approximately 40 minutes or until center springs back when pressed gently.
Yields 16 slices.
notes: Great for brunch, morning coffee break or dessert! Nutritional Analysis per slice: Calories: 179, Cholesterol: 0, Sodium: 128 mg, Protein: 3.7 g, Carbohydrate: 33 g, Total Fat: 4.1 g, Saturated Fat: 0.5 g, Polyunsaturated Fat: 1.4 g, Monounsaturated Fat: 2.2 g, % of calories from fat = 20%.

title: Fresh Green Salad with Peppercream Dressing
ingredients: 2 teaspoons chopped fresh thyme (or 1/2 teaspoon dried thyme)
2 green onions with tops, sliced, for garnish
1/2 cup freshly grated Parmesan cheese (for dressing)
2 tablespoons freshly squeezed lemon juice (for dressing)
1 tablespoon grated onion with juice (for dressing)
1-2 tablespoons freshly ground black pepper (for dressing, use amount for personal preference)
directions: Wash all lettuce and dry very well; tear lettuce into bite-size pieces.
Wash endive; dry and slice over lettuce.
Wash watercress; discard stems and dry well. Place on top of endive.
Top with fresh herbs that have been washed, dried and minced.
DO NOT TOSS SALAD. Cover bowl tightly with plastic wrap and chill several hours.
Just before serving, add sliced avocados and toss; top with dressing. Garnish with green onions and serve on salad plates.
For the Peppercream Dressing: Combine all ingredients in blender or food processor and blend until smooth. Store in covered jar in refrigerator until ready to serve.
notes: This dressing is also delicious made with freshly ground green peppercorns. Great with beef tenderloin or standing rib roast for a special Christmas or New Year's dinner!
pdfLink: pdfs/Fresh Green Salad with Peppercream Dressing.pdf

title: Fresh Zucchini Biscuits
directions: Preheat oven to 400°F.
Sprinkle zucchini with salt and let stand for 30 minutes; rinse and drain well. Squeeze zucchini dry with paper toweling; place in mixing bowl and set aside.
Sift 3 cups of flour and next four ingredients together; cut in butter or margarine with pastry blender until mixture resembles corn meal.
Stir in cheese; mix egg, buttermilk and zucchini and add to flour mixture. Stir only until flour is moistened.
Place remaining 1 cup of flour on large cutting board; place dough on flour and knead 6 times working in all remaining flour as you knead.
Use hands to pat dough to 3/4-inch thickness. Cut biscuits into 2 1/2-inch circles and place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Bake for 12-15 minutes or until golden brown. Yields 30-36 biscuits.
notes: Cooked biscuits can be frozen. After kneading dough, additional flour can be added if dough seems too soft. Serve with fresh summer vegetables, barbecue or homemade soup!

title: Frozen Fruit Salad
directions: Mix ingredients
Pour into ice cube tray
Chill in freezer

title: Fruit Salad Dressing - Buerds
directions: Put strawberries in blender & puree.
Add softened cream cheese and mix until creamy.
Add sugar to taste (it needs very little).
notes: If you want you can use rasp. or blueberries.

title: Garden Green Bean Casserole
ingredients: 1-2 tablespoons chopped green onions, including tops
directions: Wash green beans; remove ends and strings and cut into 2-inch pieces.
Place in saucepan with 1/2 teaspoon salt and water to cover. Bring to boil; reduce heat and cook covered until fork tender. Drain and set aside.
SAUCE: Melt 2 tablespoons margarine in a small saucepan; stir in flour, remaining salt, sugar and pepper; allow to bubble 2-3 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in milk; return to heat and cook on low until slightly thickened.
Remove from heat and add sour cream; mix well.
Place drained beans in a shallow 2-quart casserole; top with green onions and cheese. Cover with sauce.
Mix cornflake crumbs with 1 tablespoon melted margarine and sprinkle over casserole.
Bake uncovered at 400 for 20 minutes or until sauce bubbles and top is golden brown.
Serves 8-10. Serve while nice and hot.
notes: Recipe can be prepared a day ahead. Do not add crumbs until ready to bake. Can be served as a meat substitute! Serve with fresh tomatoes!

title: Gazpacho with Green Chilies
ingredients: 1¼ cups canned tomato juice (Campbells or Sacramento)
⅛ teaspoon finely ground black pepper
2 tablespoons mixed fresh herbs, minced (parsley, chives, oregano, cilantro, thyme)
directions: Place three-fourths of each ingredient in the food processor or blender and blend until smooth.
Save remaining ingredients for garnishing each serving.
Chill well.
notes: Chili Peppers: The smaller the pepper, the hotter! Pick your pepper by your taste preference. Canned green chiles can be used.

title: Goat Cheese, Basil and Olive Oil Pizza
ingredients: 1/2 - 1 cup of your favorite tomato and garlic spaghetti or pizza sauce (the thicker the better)
1/2 cup fresh basil leaves, torn into small pieces
directions: Preheat oven to 475 degrees.
Spread tomato sauce over pizza base but not to the edges.
Place sliced tomatoes evenly over base.
Follow with goat cheese, olives and basil.
Sprinkle Parmesan cheese and olive oil over the pizza.
Bake 15-20 minutes or until crust is crisp and topping is golden brown.
Serves 4.
notes: A summer favorite! Serving Suggestion: Try one of the new thin Boboli crusts. Other cheeses can be used!
pdfLink: pdfs/GOAT CHEESE, BASIL AND OLIVE OIL PIZZA.pdf

title: Greek Vegetable Salad
directions: In a large salad bowl, combine first 11 ingredients.
Lightly dress with a mixture of olive oil, vinegar and lemon juice.
Serve on leaf lettuce, if desired.
INDIVIDUAL SERVINGS: Arrange leaf lettuce on salad plates; top with all remaining salad ingredients and drizzle lightly with dressing.
notes: Serves 4-6. HERB SUBSTITUTIONS: If fresh herbs are not available, use half as much dried herbs. Add dried herbs to liquids and allow to soften before dressing salad. Wonderful with grilled or roasted lamb!

title: Green Beans with Tomatoes
ingredients: 6 large ripe plum tomatoes, peeled, seeded and coarsely chopped
1 pound tender green beans, cut into 3 inch lengths
directions: Heat oil in a large frying pan.
Add onion and cook for 3 minutes; add garlic and cook 2 additional minutes or until onion is softened but not brown.
Add chopped tomatoes, vegetable broth, beans, olives and lemon juice.
Cover and cook over low heat for an additional 12-15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the sauce is thickened and beans are tender.
Season with salt and pepper to taste; serve immediately.
notes: Great with grilled fish! Fresh tomatoes are best. If tomato skins are thin; peeling is not necessary. So good could be a vegetable entrée! Serves 4.

title: Green Tomato Chutney
ingredients: 1 pound Granny Smith apples, peeled and chopped
1-2 large garlic cloves, peeled and minced
3 tablespoons pickling spice, tied in cheesecloth
directions: Place the first five ingredients in a large, heavy-bottom saucepan; add pickling spice bag and half the vinegar.
Bring to a boil and immediately reduce heat to low and simmer uncovered for 1 hour.
Dissolve sugar in remaining vinegar and add to the tomato mixture.
Simmer an additional 1 1/2 hours or until mixture is thick.
Remove spice bag and spoon hot chutney into sterilized jars.
Seal by package directions or see below. Store for 1 month before using.

To seal jars: Fill to within 1/2-inch of top; place flat lid on jar; add outer rim of top and seal tightly. Then unscrew half a turn and leave until completely cool. When completely cool, tighten securely.
notes: An end-of-the-summer treat! Delicious with pork roast or game! Yields 10-12 fruit jars.

title: Garlic Mashed Potatoes
ingredients: 2# all purpose potatoes (Yukon best), peeled & cubed
fresh ground pepper & salt to taste
directions: Cook potatoes & garlic until tender; drain.
Melt butter—cool—then add buttermilk; warm.
Mash potatoes & garlic; add buttermilk & butter.
notes: Serves 6. Recipe by Laura Gough, May 1997.

title: Gazpacho Sevillano
ingredients: 8 large tomatoes or 1 large can (1 lb 14 ounce) peeled
directions: Mash garlic with salt to a paste; add pimiento & mash.
Work in oil & bread crumbs.
If fresh tomatoes are used, scald quickly with boiling water & peel & quarter.
Puree in blender tomatoes & peppers, add garlic paste & vinegar.
Blend til smooth.
Chill.
Add about 3 cups of water when ready to serve & more salt if desired.
Garnish with cucumber, croutons, hard cooked eggs or scallions.
notes: Possibly substitute garlic powder for cloves.

title: Gazpacho
directions: In a food processor, combine 1 cup V8 juice, lemon juice, garlic, 2 tomatoes and one-third of the carrot, onion, cucumber, green pepper, parsley and basil. Process, then pour into a large bowl.
Repeat the process, using 1 cup V8 juice, olive oil, jalapeño pepper, 1 tomato and one-third of the remaining vegetables.
Repeat the process, using the last cup of V8 juice and the remaining tomato and vegetables.
Mix the three batches together. Add salt and pepper to taste.
Refrigerate for at least 4 hours before serving.
Garnish with chopped cucumber or tomato, croutons, slivered basil or a drizzle of olive oil.
Makes 8 cups.
notes: THIS RECIPE RESULTS in a finely chopped soup; using a lower setting on the food processor will keep the ingredients chunky. * To easily peel tomatoes, drop in a pot of boiling water for 1 to 2 minutes, until skin pulls back. Remove from boiling water, peel and use.

title: German Potato Salad
directions: Boil potatoes, keep hot, and dice.
Fry bacon, crumble, and place over potatoes.
Add celery and onion to the potatoes.
In a small saucepan, take bacon drippings and heat over low heat until it bubbles.
Add 4 tbsp flour one at a time, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and stir in 1 cup sugar and 1 cup vinegar.
Replace to low heat and stir until the consistency is like a medium white sauce.
Pour the sauce over the potatoes and toss to combine.
notes: Recipe from Jerri Burd; serves 6-8.

title: Gin Punch
directions: Pour over large piece of ice or 2 trays of cubes.
Add 2 large bottles of club soda.
Mix together.
Decorate with fruit slices.
notes: Makes 50 servings, 4 ounce each.

title: Ginger Muffins
directions: Cream margarine and sugar; add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Add molasses and beat well.
Mix soda and buttermilk and set aside.
Mix flour with cinnamon and ginger; set aside.
Alternately add buttermilk and flour to the egg mixture.
Fold in nuts and raisins.
Cover mixing bowl and let stand in refrigerator overnight.
When ready to bake, fill greased muffin tins two-thirds full; bake in a preheated 400-degree oven for 20 minutes.
Yields 24-30 muffins.
notes: Dough can be kept in a covered bowl in the refrigerator for 2 weeks. Bake muffins as needed. A wonderful taste for fall meals.

title: Goat Cheese Ball with Pesto with Sundried Tomatoes
directions: Reconstitute tomatoes in boiling water - 15-20 mins - drain & chop.
Blend cheeses.
Line bowl w/ plastic wrap.
Layer 1/2 cheese, 1/2 tomatoes, 1/2 pesto, 1/2 walnuts.
Repeat layers.
Refrigerate.
notes: Recipe by Julia Dawson, 2004.
pdfLink: pdfs/Goat Cheese Ball with Pesto with Sundried Tomatoes.pdf

title: Gourmet Golden Squash
directions: Place squash in saucepan with small amount boiling salted water.
Cook 15 minutes or until tender.
Drain squash and add remaining ingredients; mash.
Mound mixture into 2 quart casserole.
Bake in 400° oven 20-30 minutes til heated.
notes: Shirley Adams, 1971; marked 'very good'. Serves 12.

title: Gratineed Eggs
directions: Preheat oven to 400°. Grease a shallow baking dish—set aside.
Crumble sausage into skillet & fry over med-heat, stirring constantly until sausage is no longer pink. Drain well & transfer to bowl.
Wipe out skillet—add butter & melt over med heat—add mushrooms & onion & sauté until onion is soft but not brown.
Stir in sausage.
Blend in remaining ingredients & mix well.
Turn into prepared dish. Bake until knife comes out clean, 30-35 mins.
notes: Recipe by Laura Gaugh, 1/88.

title: Grecian Party Squares
ingredients: 1 pkg (10 ounce) frozen chopped spinach, thawed and squeezed to drain
1 can (14 ounce) artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1 can (8 ounce) water chestnuts, drained and chopped
directions: Preheat oven to 375°.
Mix soup mix, mayo, and sour cream; set aside.
Unroll 2 packages of crescent dough, laying sides of dough across width of pan; seal dough—press up sides to form crust.
Bake 10-12 minutes until golden brown.
Drain spinach, artichokes, and water chestnuts; chop if need be.
Add feta cheese and garlic; mix all ingredients.
Spread mixture over crust, then sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake 10-12 minutes.
Cut with pizza cutter.
notes: Yields 28 squares.

title: Green Goddess Salad Dressing
directions: Chop garlic clove, green onion tops, and anchovy paste until very fine, almost a paste.
Add sour cream, mayonnaise, tarragon vinegar, black pepper, lemon juice, and green food color.
Chill for 2-3 hours.
notes: Yields about 2/3 cups.

title: Green Pea Soup
ingredients: 1/2 lb shelled fresh green peas or a 10 ounce package of frozen peas
4 1/2 c. hot broth (total, including cooking liquid)
directions: Cook peas in 1 1/2 cups of strong chicken broth.
When peas are tender, put them through the blender.
