Add the cooking liquid to 4 1/2 cups of hot broth.
Season as needed with salt and pepper and heat.
notes: A similar soup may be made with asparagus, broccoli, spinach, or watercress, using freshly cooked or left-over vegetables.

title: Green Beans
directions: Cook green beans until just tender, still a little crisp.
Toss with lemon vinaigrette.
Add toasted walnuts, feta cheese, and red onion.
Serve at room temperature.
notes: Recipe by Laura Gough, May '97

title: Homemade Hot Fudge Sauce
directions: Combine all ingredients in the top of a double boiler.
Cook over medium-high heat until the sauce thickens.
The cooking time will vary but it averages 15 minutes. The longer it cooks, the thicker it gets.
notes: Yields 1 1/2 cups. If a double boiler is not available, use a very heavy sauce pan and cook over lower heat. Watch carefully!

title: Hamburger Quiche
directions: Remove pie crust from freezer.
Brown meat, drain & set aside.
Blend & warm mayo, milk, eggs and cornstarch just until smooth.
Stir in meat, cheese & onion.
Pour into shell & bake 35 min @ 350°.
notes: Recipe from: Jeri

title: Henry Bains Cream Cheese Dip
directions: Mix all together.
Store in refrig.
Serve over 8oz brick cream cheese.
Serve w/ crackers.
notes: Makes 1-2 qts. Signed by Nancy Dawson, July 1, 1991.

title: Hidden Ranch Oyster Crackers
ingredients: 1 pkg Hidden Valley Buttermilk Original Ranch Salad Dressing Mix
directions: Combine all ingredients.
Stir to coat.
Place in warm oven for 15 minutes.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson.

title: Holiday Crab Dip
ingredients: 2 8 ounce packages of cream cheese, softened
1/2 cup grated sharp white cheddar cheese
1 - 1 1/2 cups fresh special or backfin crabmeat
directions: Preheat oven to 325.
Grease a 2 quart baking dish and set aside.
Combine first 9 ingredients and mix until well blended.
Gently fold in crabmeat.
Spoon into baking dish and bake in oven for 35-45 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Sprinkle mozzarella cheese on top and place back in oven until melted.
Serve with toast points or crackers!
notes: Be sure to triple pick crab to remove all shell.

title: Holiday Crab Soup
ingredients: 1-1 1/2 pounds backfin or special crab meat
directions: Gently pick through crab to remove all shell.
Mash potatoes until smooth; set aside.
Place onion, celery and 1/4 cup water in blender; blend until smooth.
Combine onion mixture with 1 tablespoon melted butter and cook over medium heat for 5 minutes stirring constantly; set aside.
Prepare a white sauce from 1 tablespoon butter, 1 tablespoon flour and 1 cup of milk.
Bring white sauce to a boil and cook over medium heat for 1 minute.
Transfer mixture to a large heavy pot and stir in 1 additional cup of milk, onion mixture, salt and next four ingredients.
Gradually add lemon juice stirring constantly.
Add mashed potatoes, half and half, crab, 6 tablespoons butter, Old Bay seasoning and remaining 2 cups of milk.
Cook over low heat or simmer until hot.
Spoon soup into 8-10 bowls.
Garnish with lemon and paprika.
Serves 8-10.
notes: Be sure to slowly add lemon juice. Can be prepared 1 day ahead. This outstanding soup is great for a crowd!

title: Holiday Punch
ingredients: 1/2 pt. maraschino juice and cherries, halved
directions: When ready to serve, pour the mixture over a cake of orange ice (about 1 qt.).
notes: The recipe says it serves 20 people for 2 hours; however, we served 15 people for 1 1/2 hours with about a pint left over on Easter. (Annotation: 'very good.')

title: Horseradish Cream Sauce
directions: Mix

title: Horseradish and Walnut Sauce
notes: For tenderloin or roast beef.

title: Hot Apple Cider
directions: Stick the cloves into the peeled orange.
Put on a piece of foil & bake at 350 for 1 hr.
Put everything else in a big pot (crock pot is great) or tea pot - bring to simmer.
Remove orange from oven - discard cloves (I left cloves in) - put orange in punch mixture.
notes: I doubled

title: Hot Broccoli Dip
directions: Cook broccoli in the bag in the microwave for 6 minutes, or cook it the conventional way.
Sauté onion in butter, add cheese, soup & seasonings.
Heat slowly until cheese is melted.
Add broccoli, almonds, mushrooms, etc.
Serve in chafing dish with corn chips.

title: Hot Buttered Rum
ingredients: 1/4 cup molasses or dark corn syrup
directions: With the back of a spoon, mash together butter, brown sugar and molasses in a small bowl until thoroughly mixed.
Place 1 1/2 or 2 rounded teaspoons of mixture (or to taste) in a mug.
Add 1 ounce of rum.
Fill with boiling water, stirring until butter mixture has melted.
Top with whipped cream.
notes: Servings vary depending on amount of mixture used for each cup. Nutrients per serving: 188 calories, 0.24 gram protein, 19 grams carbohydrate, 6 grams fat (26 percent total calories), 15 milligrams cholesterol, no fiber, 64 milligrams sodium.

title: Hot Choc. Sauce
ingredients: 8 sq (8 ounce.) semisweet chocolate, cut into small pieces
directions: In the top of a double boiler set over hot water, melt the chocolate and the strong coffee.
Keep the sauce warm over hot water until serving time.
If the sauce becomes too thick, add a little coffee, water, or Cognac.
notes: None

title: Hot Crab - Julia
ingredients: dash of tabasco, salt & white pepper
directions: Combine all ingredients.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 300 degrees for 20-30 minutes.
notes: Dated 4/20/01

title: Hot Crab Dip
directions: Soften cream cheese and add sour cream. Stir till smooth and creamy.
Add crab meat, Crab Dip Blend, and sherry.
Place in a greased casserole dish and top with grated cheese.
Garnish with paprika.
Bake in a preheated oven at 350 degrees for 15-20 minutes or until bubbly and lightly browned.
Serve with chunks of warm French bread.

Optional: Scoop out the center of a round loaf of bread and fill the center with mixture. Place on baking sheet and bake at 350 degrees for 20 to 30 minutes or until bread is warm and top of mixture is lightly browned.
Served with cut-up vegetables and chunks of bread.
notes: There are several typos in the original text (e.g., 'lace n a', 'ovef', '15-209 miutes', 'load of bread', 'afll thet cener', 'bakig', 'a350', 'brornwed', 'sna'). These have been corrected for clarity in the transcription.

title: Hot Spiced Wassail
ingredients: 6 inches cinnamon stick, broken into pieces
directions: Tie broken cinnamon sticks, 16 cloves, and whole allspice in a cheesecloth bag.
Stud the 3 medium oranges with whole cloves.
In a saucepan, combine apple juice or cider, cranberry-juice cocktail, sugar, and aromatic bitters.
Add the spice bag and the studded oranges to the saucepan.
Simmer, covered, for 10 minutes.
Stir in 2 1/2 cups of rum and heat through.
Remove the spice bag and oranges.
Pour into a warm serving bowl and float the oranges on top.
notes: Makes 9 cups.

title: Huevos Rancheros
directions: Brown onions & peppers, & add remaining sauce. Heat thru.
Fry eggs or scrambled.
Pour sauce over - shed [shred] cheese.
Cover pan 3-5 min.
notes: Excellent

title: Hungarian Coffee Cake
directions: Make 1/2 Sweet Dough. After second rising, cut dough into pieces the size of walnuts or little smaller.
Form into balls.
Roll each ball in 1/2 cup melted butter.
Roll in a mixture of 3/4 cup sugar, 1 tsp. cinnamon, and 1/2 cup finely chopped nuts.
Place 1 layer of balls so they barely touch in a well greased 9-inch tube pan.
Sprinkle with a few raisins.
Add another layer of balls and sprinkle with more raisins, pressing them in slightly.
Let rise 45 minutes.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes at 375°.
Loosen from pan and invert pan so butter-sugar mixture runs down over cake.
To serve, break apart with 2 forks.
notes: The Sweet Dough recipe appears incomplete as it cuts off after the initial ingredients.

title: Ice Box Rolls
directions: Cream shortening and sugar, add boiling water and cool.
Dissolve yeast in cold water, cool H2O and add to cooled mixture.
Beat eggs stiff and add to creamed mixture.
Add flour and salt through sifter to creamed mixture.
Cover bowl with waxed paper, then a plate or lid.
Place in refrigerator overnight or until you wish to use.
Take out and place on a well-floured surface. Work until a smooth ball.
Roll into a round pie shape about 1/2" thick.
Spread with soft butter or shortening.
Cut as for pie into 8-10 pieces. Roll wide end up.
Place on cookie sheet 3" apart.
Let rise 1 1/2 hours or until ready.
Bake at 400° for about 12-15-20 minutes.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Gretchen Jones.

title: Instant Chocolate
directions: 1/3 c. / cup hot water
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of: Ann Cook

title: Instant Russian Tea
ingredients: 1/2 to 3/4 c. instant tea (1 cup better)
notes: You can buy this but buying small size jars.

title: Italian Tomato Salad
ingredients: 4 med. tomatoes, cut into small wedges
directions: Combine ingredients and marinate for 4 hrs.

title: Jeri's Egg Casserole
ingredients: 1 cup whipping cream, at room temperature
directions: To prepare sauce, sauté garlic briefly in melted butter.
Add flour, stirring constantly, until mixture bubbles.
Gradually add cream and milk, while continuing to stir.
When mixture thickens, add cheese and seasonings and stir until cheese melts.
Spoon 1/3 of sauce into a 9x13" baking dish.
Top with 1/2 of eggs and 1/2 of bacon.
Spoon 1/3 more of sauce on top and repeat egg and bacon layers.
Top with the rest of the sauce.
Bring casserole to room temperature before baking at 350° for 20-30 minutes or until bubbly.
notes: Casserole is best if made one or two days in advance and refrigerated.

title: Jeri's Salad
ingredients: 1 whole sweet Spanish onion, sliced thin and separated into rings
directions: Blend together sour cream, sugar, salad dressing and vinegar until smooth.
Pour over torn lettuce in serving bowl.
Top with onion, Parmesan cheese and bacon.
Serve immediately.
notes: The recipe card is from CURRENT, INC., Colorado Springs, CO 80941.

title: Jerry's Rum & Limeade
directions: Mix and serve cold.

title: Jill's Best Quiche
ingredients: 1/2 lb Swiss cheese or Monterey Jack
directions: Mix flour, butter, and Velveeta cheese together for crust and press into pan.
Layer spinach, onions, mushrooms, and bacon.
Season with salt, pepper, and nutmeg.
Mix together eggs, sour cream, and cheese (Swiss/Monterey Jack) together and spread over the top.
Sprinkle lots of Parmesan cheese on top.
Bake at 375° for 25-30 minutes.
notes: The crust ingredients (flour, butter, Velveeta) are mixed together and pressed into a pan.

title: Kiss Me at Your Own Risk Salad
ingredients: 1 14-ounce can hearts of palm, drained and cut up
directions: Combine oil, vinegar, garlic, sugar, salt, dry mustard and pepper.
Pour over tomatoes, zucchini and hearts of palm.
Marinate overnight.
Serve on individual plates of Bibb lettuce and top with blue cheese.
notes: The title implies a strong garlic flavor profile.
pdfLink: pdfs/KISS ME AT YOUR OWN RISK SALAD.pdf

title: Karen's Bread
directions: Score bread lengthwise in 1" sections.
Turn and do same in other direction.
Stuff bread with cheese and mushrooms.
Sprinkle onion, poppy seeds, and salt on top.
Melt butter, add lemon juice and dried mustard; stir to dissolve.
Spread butter mixture over bread.
Wrap in foil.
Bake at 350° for 10 minutes.
May take foil off 1/2 way through so bread will brown.
notes: Very good.

title: Kings Armes Peanut Soup
ingredients: 2 quarts chicken stock or canned chicken broth
directions: Saute onion and celery in butter until soft - but not brown.
Stir in flour until well blended.
Add chicken stock, stirring constantly, and bring to a boil.
Remove from heat and rub through a sieve.
Add peanut butter and cream - stirring to blend thoroughly.
Return to low heat - do not boil and serve - garnished c (with) peanuts.
notes: This soup can be served iced cold.

title: Kuralt Crab Spread
directions: Mix with a fork.
Place in a mold and chill.
After unmolding it, sprinkle with sweet Hungarian paprika to serve.
notes: We served cocktail sauce in a separate dish.

title: Lemon Chicken Soup with Orzo
ingredients: 8 cups chicken broth, regular or reduced sodium
8 ounces boneless chicken breast, cut crosswise in thin slices
directions: Pour chicken broth into a large, uncovered saucepan; bring to a boil and stir in orzo.
Reduce heat to medium-low and cook uncovered for 15 minutes; add chicken slices and continue cooking 5-8 minutes.
While chicken cooks, prepare eggs and lemon: In a separate bowl, whisk eggs while slowly adding lemon juice; add zest.
Continue whisking and slowly warm egg mixture by gradually adding 1 cup of hot chicken broth.
Reduce heat of saucepan and slowly whisk warmed eggs into pan.
Stir constantly as soup thickens slightly. Add salt and pepper; remove from heat and ladle into bowls and garnish with parsley.
notes: Based on an old recipe for avgolemono, a traditional Greek soup! Delicious as a first course for a lamb dinner!

title: Laura's Cheese Tortellini Soup
directions: Brown onion in olive oil.
Take casing off sausage before adding to onion.
Add garlic and fennel.
Simmer.
Add other ingredients.
notes: The ingredient list specifies '1/2 T thyme' and '10 cans - chicken or beef broth' (interpreted as 10 cups based on standard recipe ratios).

title: Laura's Sausage Soup
ingredients: 1 pkg sweet sausage (or whatever kind you like)
8-10 cups chicken broth (or vegetable broth, or a combo)
directions: Saute onion, garlic, carrots, and fennel (or celery).
Saute sausage.
Add broth and tomatoes, then cook for 20 minutes or so.
Add beans and spinach last.
Optional: may add tortellini, pasta, or barley, etc.
notes: Parmesan cheese is recommended to be served on top.

title: Layered Antipasto Salad
ingredients: 2 (6 1/2 ounce) jars marinated artichoke hearts, undrained
4 med. tomatoes, cut into wedges (plum tomatoes used)
8 ounce mozzarella cheese, cut into thin strips
1 sm. purple onion, sliced & separated into rings
directions: Drain artichokes (save marinade).
Combine marinade, olive oil, vinegar & garlic in jar - shake.
Layer 1/3 lettuce, 1/2 of tomatoes - top with artichoke hearts & pepperoni.
Layer 1/3 lettuce, cheese, onion & olives - drizzle with half of dressing.
Top with remaining dressing - sprinkle with bacon.
Cover & chill at least 3 hrs.
Toss gently before serving.
notes: Recipe from Cheryl Bergen. Serves 8.

title: Lemon Sauce
directions: Mix sugar, cornstarch and salt.
Add boiling water slowly, stirring constantly.
Boil for five minutes.
Remove from heat and add egg yolk, butter and lemon extract.
notes: Lemon extract to flavor.

title: Lemon-marinated Mushrooms
directions: Rinse mushrooms and wipe clean with damp paper towels; place in a shallow bowl.
Combine remaining ingredients in a jar and mix well.
Pour marinade over mushrooms and refrigerate overnight, stirring occasionally.
notes: Serve as appetizers or add to a salad! Serves 8 for appetizers. Travels well for picnics and cookouts!

title: Lime Jello Mold
directions: Pour off juice from canned fruit and bring to a boil.
Add jello and dissolve.
Add softened cream cheese and beat well.
Add other ingredients (pears, pineapple, nuts).
Let cool (chill).
Beat 1 package Dream Whip according to directions.
Add to jello mixture until firm; serve.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Thelma Wortman. Serves 6-8.

title: Lime Jello Salad
directions: Dissolve lime jello in 2 cups boiling water.
Mix the jello, cream cheese, and crushed pineapple until smooth.
Add the chopped celery, English walnuts, sugar, whipped cream (or Dream Whip), and vanilla.
Fold into mixture.
Chill until firm.
notes: Recipe suggests using whipped cream or Dream Whip as a substitute.

title: Lobster Stew
ingredients: 1 cup cut up boiled lobster (or more)
3/4 of a 1/4 lb stick of butter, melted
directions: Add lobster to melted butter and sprinkle with paprika.
Keep stirring until hot.
Add whole milk and evaporated milk.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Allow to get hot but do not boil.
Let stand awhile and then reheat before serving.
notes: Ensure the mixture does not reach a boil during the heating process.

title: Lobster Titus
ingredients: 1/4 lb boiled lobster, cut into chunks (shrimp may be used as ornament)
directions: Cut 4 thin slices of fresh pineapple.
Cover each slice with 1/4 lb of boiled lobster cut into chunks.
To make the cocktail sauce: In a bowl, put wine vinegar, dry mustard, egg yolks, minced celery, horseradish, chopped chives, chopped parsley, chopped shallots, salt, and pepper.
Beat until smooth and light.
Beat in 4 oz olive oil and mix well.
Add 2 oz cognac and 2 oz chili sauce, mixing well.
Add juice of 1/2 lemon and mix thoroughly.
Chill.
notes: Serves 4. Shrimp may be used as an ornament.

title: Maytag Blue Cheese Dip
ingredients: 8 ounces regular or reduced-fat cream cheese, softened
1/4 cup regular or reduced-fat sour cream
2 - 3 tablespoons heavy cream or plain yogurt
2 tablespoons finely minced green onion tops, divided
1 - 2 cups each, sliced carrots, cucumber or sweet red pepper
directions: Mix the first three ingredients in a medium sized mixing bowl.
Add the crumbled blue cheese, 1 tablespoon of the green onion tops and black pepper; stir until blended but chunky.
Chill until ready to serve.
TO SERVE: Put mixture into a serving bowl and garnish with reserved green onion tops. Serve with sliced vegetables.
notes: This also makes a delicious salad dressing by adding an additional 2-3 tablespoons of milk.

title: Mexican Corn Bread
directions: Preheat oven to 375.
Grease a 9 x 13 baking pan.
Combine all ingredients except eggs and cheese.
Mix well and add eggs and cheese.
Mix and pour into baking pan.
Bake 40-45 minutes or until the center springs back when touched lightly.
Do not overbake.
notes: 2-3 tablespoons diced, cooked bacon can be substituted for the pepper. Pepper should be adjusted to personal taste. Guaranteed to take the chill off a cold night!

title: Mexican Corn Bread
ingredients: 1/2 cup (4-ounce can) diced green chilies, drained
directions: Combine cornmeal, flour, non-fat dry milk, sugar, baking powder and salt in a medium bowl.
Stir in cheese and chilies.
Beat water, oil and eggs together.
Stir into dry ingredients just until blended.
Pour into buttered, 8-inch square baking pan.
Bake at 375 degrees for 30 to 35 minutes, or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean.

title: Manakin's Sauce for Chicken
directions: Mix together and heat until butter melts.
Then baste chicken as needed with sauce.

title: Margarita's La Paz
directions: Rim glass with salt.
Combine tequila, triple sec, and sweet n sour.
Serve chilled.
notes: Serves 2.

title: Margarita
notes: Recipe from: Art of the Cocktail

title: Margaritas
directions: Add crushed ice
Mix in blender
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson; provided by Linda Roberts, Oct 1986.

title: Mashed Potato Casserole
directions: Peel, cut, and boil potatoes.
In mixer, blend cream cheese, butter, and milk (all of which have been left to soften at room temp).
Add this to potatoes (mashed).
Add a little cut up onion, salt, and pepper.
Bake at 350° for 25 minutes.
Bake uncovered, you'll love the golden brown crust.
notes: Can be made the night before. Enjoy!

title: Mashed Potatoes
directions: Boil potatoes, drain, add cr. cheese, milk, butter, S&P.
Mix w/ beaters.
Put in a 9x13 pan - spray w/ Pam.
Bake @ 350° for 40 mins.

title: Meatless Vegetable Soup
directions: Melt 3 Tbsp butter.
Add carrots, celery, and onions; cook slowly for 10 minutes.
Add potatoes and cook for 2 minutes longer.
Add 3 cups of water and simmer covered for 1 hour.
Add flour, cook and stir until smooth.
Add tomatoes (or tomato sauce) to the soup and simmer it covered for 1/4 hour longer.
Add salt and pepper to taste before serving.
notes: Vary the vegetables if you like, keeping about the same proportions of liquid and solids. I usually triple the recipe.

title: Melon Snowball
directions: Dissolve 1 pkg. lemon jello in 1 c. boiling H2O.
Stir in 1 T. lemon juice and 1 c. cocktail juice.
Chill till slightly thickened.
Stir in 1 c. drained fruit cocktail.
Cut off end of cantaloupe, scoop out seeds, fill with jello mixture, and chill till firm.
Remove rind from melon and dry with paper towels.
Frost with softened cream cheese.
Chill till serving time.
Slice and arrange on greens; garnish with more fruit cocktail.
notes: The recipe calls for a cantaloupe to be used as a mold for the gelatin mixture.

title: Melon in Rum Lime Sauce
directions: In saucepan, mix sugar and H2O. Bring to boil.
Simmer for 5 mins.
Add lime rind - let cool to room temp.
Add lime juice and rum.
Pour over fruit - chill for several hours.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Jackie Pfrang, 1976.

title: Mint Julep - Churchill Downs
directions: Boil 1 cup sugar and 1 cup water for 5 minutes.
Cool and place in a container.
Add 3 sprigs of mint and cover.
Refrigerate overnight.
To serve, add 1 tablespoon of syrup and 2 ounces of Kentucky bourbon to a crushed ice-filled julep cup.
Stir and garnish with mint.
notes: Recipe yields enough syrup for 16 drinks.

title: Minted Pineapple Mold
ingredients: 1/2 cup syrup from a 20 ounce. can crushed pineapple
Remaining pineapple juice (from the 20 ounce. can)
directions: Place 1 envelope of unflavored gelatine and 1/2 cup syrup from a 20 oz. can of crushed pineapple in a saucepan.
Place over low heat, stirring constantly until the gelatine is completely dissolved.
Remove from heat, add 1/3 cup mint flavored apple jelly, and stir until melted.
Add the crushed pineapple and the remaining juice.
Chill until the mixture mounds slightly when dropped from a spoon.
Add 1 teaspoon of confectioners' sugar to 1 cup of heavy cream; beat until stiff.
Fold the whipped cream into the gelatine mixture.
Turn into a 5-cup mold; chill until firm.
Unmold to serve and garnish with fresh mint.
notes: The recipe specifies using the syrup and juice from a 20 ounce. can of crushed pineapple.

title: Mixed Greens with Raspberries & Walnuts
directions: Whisk tog. 1st - 6 ingredients.
Toss c salad greens, rasp & walnuts.
notes: 6 servings

title: Molded Peach Surprise
ingredients: 1 cup thinly sliced fresh peaches, sweetened
directions: Dissolve gelatin in hot water. Add cold water and lemon juice.
Chill until slightly thickened.
Reserve one cup of mixture.
Fold peaches into remaining gelatin and spoon into 8x8x2 inch pan. Chill until almost firm.
Place bowl of reserved gelatin in bowl of ice and water. Beat with egg beater until fluffy and thick.
Whip cream and fold into whipped gelatin and spoon over other layer.
Chill until firm.
To serve, cut into squares and garnish with slice of fresh lime and sprig of mint, if desired.
notes: 8-10 servings.

title: Morning Glory Muffins
directions: Sift together sugar, flour, cinnamon & baking soda, salt in lg. bowl.
Add fruit, carrots & nuts & stir to combine.
In a bowl whisk eggs & oil & vanilla.
Pour this mixture into cupcake tins lined with muffin paper.
Fill each cup to brim.
Bake at 350° for 35 mins.
notes: Need 24 hrs. for ripening to develop full flavor. Also freezes well.

title: Mulligatawny
directions: In a large saucepan, cook onion and curry powder in vegetable oil until onion is tender.
Stir in chopped carrots, celery, and green pepper.
Cook, stirring occasionally, until vegetables are crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Sprinkle flour over vegetable mixture, stirring well to mix.
Add broth, undrained tomatoes, parsley, lemon juice, sugar, cloves, salt, and pepper.
Bring to boil, then add chicken.
Simmer for 30 minutes.
notes: Recipe from Cheryl Burgin. Serves 6.

title: Myrana's Salsa
directions: Mix together.
Let sit for at least 1 hour.
notes: Recipe by Julia Dawson, 2003.

title: Nana Trilett's Doughnuts
ingredients: 2 eggs, beaten together with 1 cup sugar
directions: Mix the eggs, sugar, sour milk, and cream.
Add the flour, nutmeg, cinnamon, soda, and salt.
If not thick enough to roll, add more flour.
Put into ice box to chill overnight.
Bake in hot fat.
notes: The recipe specifies adding the dry ingredients (nutmeg, cinnamon, soda, salt) to the flour, then combining everything. 'Bake in hot fat' refers to deep-frying the doughnuts.

title: Nana Trilletts's America's Original Egg Nog
ingredients: Two fifths Puerto Rican Rum (1 white label & 1 gold label)
directions: Dissolve sugar in rum in a large jar.
Beat eggs to light froth, add to rum mix, beating to foam.
Chill in refrig. 3 hrs.
Beat cream in another bowl stiff, add to rum mix beating constantly.
Pour into punch bowl.
Place in refrig. for 1 hr.
Remove & grate nutmeg over eggnog.
notes: Serves 40
pdfLink: pdfs/Nana Trilletts's America's Original Egg Nog.pdf

title: Nana's Boiled Salad Dressing
ingredients: 1 cup vinegar (If vinegar is very strong, use 1/3 water)
directions: Melt butter.
Mix ingredients and cook until thick.
When cool, thin with cream.
Add sugar to taste.
Add cream as you use it, as it keeps good before cream is added.
notes: For potato salad: I use baked cold potato, onions, and hard boiled eggs chopped.

title: Nathalie Dupree's Killer Pasta Salad
ingredients: 1/4 cup chopped green onions (both white and green parts)
1/4 pound fresh snow peas, strings removed
1 large red bell pepper, seeded and cut into thin strips
1 pound short pasta, such as rotelle OR fusilli OR penne
directions: In a jar, combine mustard, garlic, wine vinegar, oil, onions, salt and pepper, to taste shake until creamy. Set aside.

Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil. Cook snow peas in water for 1 minute; remove with a long-handled strainer and immediately drench with cold water to stop cooking process and brighten color.
Repeat with broccoli and zucchini, cooking for 3 minutes each. In a bowl, combine cooked vegetables with red bell pepper and toss with half the dressing.

Cook pasta in vegetable water for 8 to 10 minutes. Drain, rinse with cold water and drain again. Toss with remaining dressing. Combine vegetables and pasta. Sprinkle with cheese. Add more salt and pepper to taste. Refrigerate until ready to serve, at least 1 hour or up to 2 days, covered.
notes: Makes 8 to 10 servings. Nutrients per serving (for 10): 340 calories, 18 grams fat (47 percent total calories), 2 milligrams cholesterol, 122 milligrams sodium.

title: New England Fish Chowder
ingredients: Leftover baked fish, cut into 1" sq. pieces
Salt pork, diced into small pieces
Baked fish (for the secondary recipe, likely Haddock)
directions: Fry salt pork until brown and crisp.
Add sliced onions to salt pork and brown slightly.
Add water to cover, then add cubed potatoes.
Boil until potatoes are just tender.
Add milk and cream.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Bring to a boil, add fish, and then let stand overnight in the refrigerator to bring out the best flavor.
Reheat to serve.
For baked fish: Place fish in a dish, pour cream over just to cover, season with salt, pepper, paprika, and butter. Bake uncovered at 350° until tender.
notes: The recipe suggests letting the chowder stand overnight to improve flavor. There is also a secondary, separate short recipe included for 'Baked Fish - Haddock'.

title: New Potato & Asparagus Salad
ingredients: 3 medium red new potatoes, halved lengthwise
directions: Cook potatoes in large pot of boiling H2O until just tender (20 minutes).
Cook asparagus just crisp-tender. Drain.
Cut asparagus into 1 1/2 inch pieces.
Toss vegetables together with sauce.
Serve salad warm or at room temperature.
notes: Makes 2 servings - double or triple as needed. The mustard, lemon juice, olive oil, chives, and salt/pepper form the sauce.

title: Olé! Olé! a Hearty Mexican Dip!
ingredients: 2 large bags corn chips or taco-style chips for dipping
directions: Brown meat and chopped onion in large skillet; add ketchup and spices.
Mash beans with their liquid; add to meat mixture.
Place meat mixture in bottom of chafing dish or other serving dish that can be kept heated.
Top meat mixture with an outer ring of grated cheese, an inner ring of onions and a center of sliced olives.
Keep hot and serve with chips.
notes: Prepare meat sauce and toppings ahead of time. Heat sauce when ready to serve! "A man's dish! Popular with the football crowd!"
pdfLink: pdfs/OLÉ! OLÉ! A hearty Mexican dip!.pdf

title: Oatmeal Coffee Cake
directions: Mix all liquid ingredients.
Pour into jelly roll pan.
Top with crumb topping (oatmeal, cracker meal, sugar, salt, Spry, flour mixed well).
Bake at 350° for 20-25 minutes.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Aunt Lydia. 'Spry' is a vintage brand of vegetable shortening.

title: Oliva
directions: Sauté the onion, red pepper, and garlic slowly.
Add the rosemary, olives, carrots, and pepperoncini peppers.

title: Olive Crostini
ingredients: 1 (4 1/4 ounce) can chopped black olives, drained
3/4 cup (3 ounce) shredded Monterey Jack cheese
1 (8 ounce) French baguette, cut into 1/4" slices
directions: Combine the first 7 ingredients.
Top each bread slice with the olive mixture and arrange on baking sheets.
Broil with the oven door partially open for 3-4 minutes, or until topping is bubbly and golden.
notes: Yields 42 appetizers. Recipe by Sue Downer.

title: Onion Cheese Supper Bread
directions: Mix ingredients, adding only 1 cup of the cheese into the batter.
Spread into a 13x9x2 inch pan.
Sprinkle remaining cup of cheese on top.
Melt 4 tablespoons of margarine and pour over top.
Bake at 400°F for 20 minutes.
notes: Recipe specifies a 13x9x2 inch pan.

title: Onion Roasted Potatoes
ingredients: 2-3 lbs all-purpose potatoes, cut into lg. chunks
directions: Preheat oven to 450°.
Mix soup and olive oil in lg. bowl or plastic bag.
Add potatoes and coat potatoes.
Bake, stirring occasionally, 40 mins. or until tender.
Garnish w/ chopped parsley.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Makes about 6-8 servings.

title: Orange Bread
ingredients: 2 (11-ounce) cans refrigerated buttermilk biscuits (we used 1869 brand)
1 (3-ounce) package cream cheese, cut into 20 squares
directions: Combine first 3 ingredients in a small bowl; set aside.

Separate biscuit dough into individual biscuits; gently separate individual biscuits in half. Place a cream cheese square between the 2 halves, and pinch sides to seal each back together. Dip in butter, and dredge in reserved sugar mixture. Stand biscuits on edge in a lightly greased 12-cup Bundt pan, spacing evenly. Drizzle with remaining butter, and sprinkle with remaining sugar mixture.
Bake at 350° for 45 minutes or until golden. Immediately invert onto a serving plate.
Combine powdered sugar and orange juice; stir well. Drizzle over warm bread. Serve immediately.
notes: Pockets of cream cheese await inside this sugar-crusted pull-apart bread. Yield: one 10-inch coffee cake.

title: Orange Sherbet Salad
directions: Pour jello into a medium bowl and add water.
Stir to dissolve.
Add sherbet and mix well.
Cool in refrigerator until it is as thick as unbeaten egg whites.
notes: IT WON'T TAKE LONG!

title: Pasta with Tomato Sauce and Roasted Vegetables
ingredients: 1/3 cup oil cured black olives, halved
1 pound penne or rigatoni pasta, cooked until just tender and drained
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Cut first 5 ingredients into 1 1/2 inch chunks.
Spread vegetables in large roasting pan; sprinkle with garlic and olive oil and toss to cover evenly.
Season with salt and pepper.
Roast vegetables until soft and brown for 20-25 minutes stirring halfway through.
Scrape the vegetable mixture into a saucepan; add tomato sauce and olives and heat.
Add roasted vegetable sauce to pasta and mix to combine.
Sprinkle with basil and grated cheese and serve hot. Serves 4-6 depending on menu.
notes: Use any combination of your favorite veggies. Serve with a fresh green salad and finish with a fruit sorbet!
pdfLink: pdfs/PASTA WITH TOMATO SAUCE AND ROASTED VEGETABLES.pdf

title: Peach and Melon Fruit Bowl
directions: Mix peaches, juice and sugar.
Toss and let stand for at least 15 minutes.
Combine cantaloupe and peaches.
Divide the fruit and juice into 4 dessert bowls and top with almonds.
Make a fresh fruit sundae by placing a scoop of ice cream in the bowls before adding the fruit.
Serves 4.
notes: Be sure all fruits are good and ripe! Be creative and add cherries, fresh pineapple or blueberries. Add vanilla ice cream for a fruit sundae!

title: Président Brie Tourte with Pesto Cream Cheese
directions: Cut 15 oz. Président Mini Brie in half into 2 layers.
Spread 3 oz. of cream cheese in middle of Brie.
Lay 2 1/2 oz. of salmon slices on top of the cream cheese.
Garnish with 1/2 oz. of salmon and sprigs of baby dill.
notes: Ripened (soft) Brie provides the best flavor for these tourtes, but the ripened Brie should be well chilled before cutting. Cut horizontally into layers using a cheese hand wire. Recipes are for the 15 ounce. Mini Brie. For the 8 ounce. Brie, use 1/2 of the ingredients.
pdfLink: pdfs/PRÉSIDENT Brie Tourte with Pesto Cream Cheese.pdf

title: Pumpkin Waffles
directions: Stir together pumpkin, eggs, milk and butter.
In a separate bowl, combine flour, baking powder, salt, sugar and nutmeg.
Add dry ingredients to pumpkin mixture. Stir until thoroughly combined.
Cook according to the directions for your waffle maker.
Serve immediately with berry or maple syrup, fresh berries or ginger whipped cream.
notes: Makes 6 classic waffles or 8 Belgian waffles. Adapted from The Joy of Cooking.

title: Pasta Salad
ingredients: 8 ounce pasta noodles (corp, screw, tomato, spinach and egg)
4 cups zucchini, yellow squash, broccoli, red peppers
2 cups basil leaves (when in season) or fresh spinach
directions: Cook pasta according to pkg. directions.
Steam vegetables (zucchini, yellow squash, broccoli, red peppers) for 3-5 mins.
Grind basil leaves or spinach fine.
Brown the pine nuts.
Toss all together - chill.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Julia Devalier.

title: Pasta with Creamy Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 3# fresh plum tomatoes or 1 lg can peeled drained tomatoes
directions: Melt butter - sauté onions (brown around 10 mins).
Add wine & bring to boil - reduce to 3 T.
Add chicken stock - reduce to 1/2 cup.
Meantime, process tomatoes - add and bring to boil - simmer 1/2 hr.
Add cream and simmer for 10 m.
notes: May add shrimp (1#) - and a little basil.

title: Pasta
directions: Put a small amount of oil in a pan.
Stir in garlic powder and parsley.
Add 2 large cans of tomato paste.
Add 2 cans of water.
Optionally add 1 can of tomato sauce.
Simmer, adding water as needed.
Add salt to taste.
Add the can of White Northern beans about 30-45 minutes before serving.
notes: Increase for more sauce.

title: Pecan Crunch Coffee Cake
directions: Combine biscuit mix, brown sugar, and spices.
Cut in butter.
Set aside 2/3 cup of this mixture.
To the remaining mixture, add buttermilk and egg.
Mix well.
Spread in a greased 9" x 1 1/2" round pan.
Combine the remaining ingredients (apple, raisins, and pecans) and sprinkle over the batter.
Top with the reserved crumb mixture.
Bake at 350° for 40-45 minutes.
notes: Recipe attributed to Jerri.

title: Phyllis Salad
directions: Mix ingredients together
Toss with Wishbone 'Italian' dressing

title: Pines French Dressing
directions: Put in jar and shake
notes: Recipe explicitly states 'NO blender'

title: Pink Punch
directions: Combine all ingredients and serve chilled.
notes: Jen Fagan, Dec. 1969. Note reads: 'very good'.

title: Pizza - Egg Dish
directions: Saute crumbled sausage with mushrooms, then drain.
Blend 6-8 eggs and 4T sour cream for 1 minute.
Pour eggs into a greased pan.
Bake at 450° for 5-10 minutes until set.
Spread a thin layer of salsa over the eggs.
Add sausage and mushrooms.
Layer with 3 cheeses, starting with Velveeta, then Cheddar and Mozzarella.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes at 300°.
Let stand 5-10 minutes.

title: Pizza Pie
ingredients: 4 cups sifted flour (plus additional flour for kneading)
directions: Measure water into a bowl, add yeast, and stir until dissolved.
Stir in sugar, 1/4 cup olive oil, salt, and 4 cups of sifted flour.
Beat until smooth.
Stir in more cups of sifted flour.
Turn out onto a lightly floured board and knead until smooth and elastic.
Place in a large greased bowl; cover and let rise in a warm place until doubled in bulk (approx. 45 minutes).
Prepare sauce by mixing tomato paste, water, 2 teaspoons salt, oregano, and pepper.
Once dough has risen, punch down and divide into quarters.
Form each into a ball and place on greased baking sheets or 12" pizza pans.
Press and pull with fingers into circles until very thin with edges about 1/4" thick.
Arrange on dough 1/4 of the tomato paste mixture, 2 tablespoons each of olive oil and grated cheese.
Place sliced mozzarella cheese on top.
Bake at 400° for 25 minutes.
notes: Dough might set in a container of warm water.

title: Poppy Seed Loaf
directions: Grease and flour 2 medium loaf pans.
Combine all bread ingredients and pour into prepared pans.
Bake at 350° for 1 hour.
Prepare glaze by combining 1 tablespoon melted butter, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, 1/2 teaspoon almond extract, 1/4 cup orange juice, and 3/4 cup sugar in a small bowl.
Prick hot loaf with a toothpick and pour on glaze.
Let stand 15-20 minutes before removing from pans to cool.
notes: Recipe from Nancy Dawson. Note at top reads: 'Anne Luther '92, 2 sm loafs'.

title: Potato Salad W Cherry Tomatoes, Bacon & Avocado
ingredients: 2 slices of bacon - cooked and crumbled
2 T. finely chopped fresh basil leaves
directions: In a steamer, steam potatoes - cut into 1" pieces - cool.
Combine potatoes, bacon, tomatoes, avocado, scallions, and the basil.
In small bowl, whisk together vinegar and oil.
S/p [salt/pepper] to taste - pour dressing over - toss and serve.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson.
pdfLink: pdfs/Potato Salad w Cherry Tomatoes, Bacon & Avocado.pdf

title: Potatoes
ingredients: 2 lb bag frozen Ore-Ida hash brown potatoes
directions: Bake 1 hr. at 350°
notes: Serves 10

title: Prune & Apricot Coffee Cake
ingredients: 3/4 cup dry prunes, chopped fine first
3/4 cup dry apricots, chopped fine first
Hot H2O (for soaking prunes and apricots, approx. 5 mins)
directions: Soak chopped prunes and apricots in hot water for 5 minutes.
Mix butter, brown sugar, 1 T. flour, and 1 T. cinnamon together and let stand.
Cream shortening and sugar. Add eggs one at a time and beat well.
Add dry ingredients with vanilla and milk, alternating, 1/3 at a time.
Fold in prunes and apricots.
Grease and flour a 9" tube pan.
Layer 1/3 of the cake mixture in the pan, then add 1/3 of the cinnamon mixture. Repeat this process three times.
Place chopped nuts on top of cake.
May place in refrigerator for 3 hours covered.
Before baking, let stand at room temperature for 15 minutes.
Bake at 350°F for 55 minutes.
Cool for 25 minutes.
notes: May be served with a sherry sauce.

title: Puffed Pancake with Strawberries
directions: Mix eggs, milk, orange juice, sugar, flour & salt.
Preheat oven to 425°.
In 13x9 pan, melt butter in oven till sizzling.
Pour batter into sizzling pan.
Bake in middle of oven for 20 min, till puffy & brown.
Serve immediately.
For Strawberry Sauce: Heat 2-10 oz pkgs frozen strawberries with 2 tbl of orange marmalade.
Serve warm or cold over pancake.
Serve sour cream if desired.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Ann King, '94. Serves 8.

title: Pumpkin Bread
directions: Mix oil & sugar, add eggs & then combine remaining ingredients.
Bake approx 1 hr @ 325°.
notes: Makes 3 loaves. Recipe from Nancy Dawson.

title: Punch
notes: May add rum or leave plain

title: Quiche
directions: Preheat oven to 350°F.
Bake for 45 minutes.
notes: Change your cheeses in any combination you may want; more cheddar than swiss, but I used this combination. Makes two 9" pans.

title: Roasted Potatoes with Red Onions
ingredients: 6-8 garlic cloves, unpeeled and left whole
directions: Preheat the oven to 400 degrees.
Peel and quarter the potatoes; rinse well and pat thoroughly dry with paper toweling.
Place butter and oil in a shallow roasting pan; place in oven to heat.
When butter has melted, add potatoes, red onions and garlic. Toss well, then spread out into one layer.
Place pan in the oven and roast for 10 minutes.
Stir gently; add rosemary and cook an additional 10-15 minutes or until golden brown and tender.
Season with salt and pepper when removing from oven. Garnish with rosemary sprigs. Serves 4.
notes: Remove garlic cloves or allow guests to peel and enjoy. 'The whole house smells good!'

title: Roasted Vegetables
ingredients: 2 medium zucchini, sliced in ½ inch slices
2 yellow bell peppers, seeded and cut in large squares
¼ teaspoon freshly cracked black pepper
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Place all vegetables in a shallow baking dish; drizzle with oil.
Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Shake during baking time and bake for 35 to 40 minutes or until edges brown and vegetables are tender.
Place in serving dish and drizzle with all topping ingredients.
Serves 4 to 6.
notes: Drizzled with olive oil and seasoned with fresh lemon zest! Wonderful with grilled seafood!

title: Raisin Bran Muffins
directions: Mix all of the dry ingredients in a lg bowl, add beaten eggs, oil & milk
Mix well and fold in fruit.
Let batter refrigerate over night, well covered, before baking.
Drop batter in greased muffin tins & bake @ 400 for 12-15 min.
notes: This batter may be kept in the refrigerator (well covered) for 3-4 weeks. DO NOT stir batter per use.

title: Raisin Sauce for Ham
directions: Mix all ingredients.
Cook over low heat, stirring until sauce comes to a boil and is thickened.
Add raisins.
Set top of dbl. boiler over hot H2O.
Cook about 30 mins until raisins plump.
notes: Recipe signed by Elsa Morrison.

title: Raspberry Champagne Punch
ingredients: 2 pkgs (10 ounce each) frozen raspberries, thawed
directions: Combine raspberries, brandies, and orange liqueur in a large punch bowl.
Place ice mold in punch just before serving.
Stir in soda and champagne gently.
notes: Excellent.

title: Raspberry Muffins
directions: For the topping, mix the brown sugar and cinnamon and set aside. Cut the chilled butter in 16 thin shavings and set aside.
Preheat the oven to 400 degrees. Butter 16 muffin cups.
In a mixing bowl, stir together the flour, baking powder, salt, sugar and baking soda.
In another bowl, stir together the egg, buttermilk, melted butter and raspberries, including the juice.
Stir the liquid ingredients into the dry. Mix until the batter is combined — barely 15 seconds or so — the batter will be slightly lumpy.
Fill the muffin cups 2/3 full. Rapidly sprinkle some topping mixture over each muffin and dot each with a piece of butter.
Bake for 25 minutes. Serve warm.
notes: Makes 16 muffins.

title: Ratatouille À La Niçoise
ingredients: 3 medium green peppers, cut into 1-inch pieces
2 medium eggplants, cut into chunks without peeling
3 medium zucchini, cut into chunks without peeling
1 can (about 1 lb.) Italian peeled plum tomatoes with juice
1 1/2 teaspoons whole coriander, coarsely ground with mortar and pestle
Small handful fresh basil, chopped, or 1 teaspoon dried basil
directions: Pour oil into flame-proof casserole or Dutch oven.
Sauté onions in hot oil until just transparent.
Add green peppers, eggplant, zucchini and garlic, stir to coat with oil.
Lower heat to simmer; cover; cook 40 minutes in their own juices, stirring occasionally.
Add tomatoes with juice, coriander, salt and pepper; mix well.
Boil gently, uncovered, for about 10 minutes, stirring often to reduce excess liquid.
Blend in parsley and basil.
Refrigerate overnight. Serve slightly chilled but not ice cold.
notes: Makes four servings. TESTED IN PARADE'S KITCHEN

title: Refrigerator Rolls
directions: Pour boiling water over Crisco.
Add sugar and salt, let cool.
Add beaten egg and beat well.
Dissolve yeast in lukewarm water.
Add to mixture.
Add flour, 1 cup at the time.
Let rise until double its size, work down and store in refrigerator.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mary Faye Long

title: Relish for Steak
directions: Mix.

title: Roasted Fennel and Potatoes
ingredients: 8 red potatoes (about 1 pound), cut in half
directions: Heat oven to 425°. Set a heavy roasting pan in the oven and preheat for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile, cut each fennel bulb lengthwise into six wedges. Season fennel and potatoes with salt and pepper and toss with olive oil.

Remove roasting pan from oven and place fennel and potatoes, cut side down, in hot pan. Return pan to oven and roast vegetables for 30 minutes, without turning, until tender and golden brown. Serve immediately.
notes: Preheat the roasting pan to give the vegetables a crisp, golden crust.

title: Rosemary Potatoes
directions: In a 9x13 pan heat oil and garlic in oven at 375 degrees.
Remove from oven and toss in remaining ingredients.
Stir to coat well with hot garlic oil.
Bake at 375 for 1 hour stirring occasionally.
notes: Serves 6 to 8. ©1995 Shenandoah Growers — Harrisonburg, Virginia

title: Rosemary-brown Butter Pecans
directions: Preheat oven to 300 F - line lg. baking sheet w/ parchment paper.
Melt butter med heat - cook until butter starts to foam & turns brown (4-5 mins).
Stir in brown sugar & rosemary.
Place pecans on baking sheet.
Pour browned butter over pecans.
Toss until coated.
Bake in preheated oven 20-25 mins - stir.
Garnish w/ flaky sea salt.
notes: 10 mins prep - 50 mins total

title: Spinach with Pine Nuts
ingredients: Freshly ground black pepper to taste
directions: Over medium low heat, pour oil in a large skillet and sauté garlic until softened, about 2 minutes.
Increase heat slightly, add spinach and cook while stirring until leaves are limp.
Add pine nuts and season with pepper; serve.
notes: Delicious with fettuccini Alfredo! To toast pine nuts, place in a single layer in a small skillet; heat over medium low heat; shake and stir constantly until golden brown. Also great with seafood!

title: Split Pea Soup
directions: Combine the first 8 ingredients; bring to boil.
Cover and simmer for one hour.
Pour the soup and all seasonings into a blender or food processor to puree.
Add half and half and gently reheat.
Serves 6.
notes: A ham bone may be used in place of the diced ham. If you desire pieces of ham in the soup, remove a few cubes before pureeing. Return ham to soup when the half and half is added. If a thinner consistency is desired, add more half and half. Top with your favorite croutons and serve with sandwiches for a winter taste treat!

title: Summer Zucchini Casserole
ingredients: 3 tablespoons freshly grated Parmesano Reggiano (Parmesan) cheese
directions: Sauté onions and pepper strips in olive oil.
When vegetables begin to soften add zucchini and sauté 3-5 minutes longer.
Add tomatoes and cook until tomatoes are softened (about 3 minutes).
Season with salt and pepper.
Place mixture in a shallow casserole dish and sprinkle with cheese.
Just before serving time, bake the casserole in a preheated 375 degree oven until topping browns and vegetables are hot.
Serves 6-8.
notes: To speed browning of the cheese, run under broiler for a couple of minutes. Serve with grilled fish or a crabmeat casserole!

title: Sunday Brunch Pizza
ingredients: 1/2 cup mixed dried fruits (cranberries, cherries, raisins, etc.); replump in warm water and blot with paper towel
1/2 cup Stonewall Kitchen Blackberry Sage Tea Jam
directions: Preheat oven to 425°.
Beat ricotta, egg and egg yolk together until smooth. Stir in dried fruits, amaretti, pine nuts and lemon zest.
Roll or stretch pizza dough to a diameter of about 16 inches, leaving edges a little thicker.

Transfer to a large pizza pan or flat cookie sheet dusted with cornmeal. Spread mixture over crust, leaving a 1-inch border free of filling. Dribble about half of the Blackberry Sage Tea Jam over cheese filling in a random pattern.
Bake on lowest shelf in oven until cheese is set and crust is golden brown, about 14 to 16 minutes.
Remove, dribble remaining Blackberry Sage Tea Jam over first layer of jam and let stand for at least 10 minutes. Cut into wedges and serve.
notes: Serves 6 to 8. A novel treat to celebrate a leisurely late morning meal or afternoon snack.

title: Sweet Potato Waffles
ingredients: 1 cup cooked and mashed sweet potato
directions: Use a mixer to mix first seven ingredients.
Combine flour and baking powder and add to sweet potato mixture alternately with milk.
Allow batter to stand in refrigerator for 15 minutes before preparing waffles.
Keep batter chilled while preparing waffles.
When ready to bake, follow manufacturer's directions for your waffle iron.
Yields 6-8 waffles depending on size of waffle iron used.
notes: For breakfast or dinner! Top with cinnamon sugar or maple syrup!

title: Salad - Frappé
directions: Dissolve jello in hot water and chill until set.
Add cottage cheese, whipping cream, cherries, crushed pineapple, and nuts.

title: Salad - Mom Skillett's
ingredients: 1 cup sour cream (or 1 cup whipping cream if a sweeter taste is desired)
directions: Combine all ingredients in a bowl and mix until well incorporated.
notes: Excellent

title: Salad Dressing - Roquefort
directions: Combine ingredients in blender.
Blend on speed #10 for 1 minute.
Add Roquefort or blue cheese to mixture.
Blend only until cheese is chopped.

title: Salmon Party Log
directions: Mix well
Chill
Roll in nuts
Serve with crackers
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Dawson

title: Sandy D'amato's - Salad Dressing
directions: Thinly slice the shallot and chop fine.
Chop garlic finely.
Whisk together all ingredients except the olive oil.
Whisk in the olive oil in a steady stream.
Serve with your choice of salad greens.
notes: Makes 1 cup. Original recipe noted 3/4 teaspoon of salt, but includes an annotation to use 1/2 teaspoon.

title: Goat Cheese Torta
ingredients: Garnishes: fresh basil sprigs, pecans, pine nuts
directions: PROCESS first 5 ingredients in a blender or food processor until smooth, stopping to scrape down sides.
LINE a 2- or 3-cup glass bowl with plastic wrap, allowing 3 inches to hang over sides.
SPREAD half of cheese mixture into bowl; top evenly with 1/2 to 3/4 cup Garden Pesto.
Top with remaining half of cheese mixture. Cover and chill 8 hours.
INVERT chilled torta onto a serving platter; remove plastic wrap. Garnish, if desired. Serve with baguette slices.
notes: Imported from archive

title: Goat Cheese Torta
directions: PROCESS first 5 ingredients in a blender or food processor until smooth, stopping to scrape down sides.
LINE a 2- or 3-cup glass bowl with plastic wrap, allowing 3 inches to hang over sides.
SPREAD half of cheese mixture into bowl; top evenly with 1/2 to 3/4 cup Garden Pesto.
Top with remaining half of cheese mixture. Cover and chill 8 hours.
INVERT chilled torta onto a serving platter; remove plastic wrap. Garnish, if desired. Serve with baguette slices.
notes: Imported from archive

title: Scramble
ingredients: 1 12 ounce. pkg. bite size shredded wheat
1 10 1/2 ounce. pkg. crisp doughnut shaped oat cereal
1 6 1/2 ounce. pkg. bite size crisp rice
directions: Mix all ingredients in very large roaster.
Bake in slow oven 250° for 2 hrs., stirring mixture with wooden spoon every 15 minutes.
Add nuts at end of cooking period.
notes: Yields 8 qts. Scramble will keep well in tightly sealed jars.

title: Sesame Asparagus
ingredients: 2 lbs. fresh asparagus or 20 ounce. frozen spears
directions: Slice cleaned asparagus into 1/4-inch thick diagonal slices (for frozen spears, cut into 2-inch pieces).
Heat sesame seeds in skillet over medium-high heat until golden brown, shaking pan frequently. Remove to bowl.
Add oil to pan. Heat over high heat. Add onion. Fry 1 minute, stirring constantly.
Add asparagus. Fry 3 minutes or until just tender, stirring frequently.
Stir in salt, pepper, soy sauce, and sesame seeds.
Serves 8.
notes: Distributed by Lee Brands, Inc., Calexico CA 92232

title: Sherried Mushrooms and Eggs
ingredients: 4 teaspoon dry sherry (I used dry vermouth and added a little more than called for)
directions: Drain mushrooms.
Heat 2 Tbsp margarine in skillet. Add mushrooms and onion; sauté 4-5 min. Set aside.
Heat 4 Tbsp margarine in saucepan. Remove from heat. Stir in flour, salt, and red pepper.
Gradually stir in cream. Bring to boiling, stirring constantly, until sauce is smooth and thickened.
Dice 5 eggs and slice remaining egg into wedges for garnish.
Stir eggs, mushroom mix, and sherry into sauce. Heat (do not boil).
Spoon into patty shells.
notes: Makes 6 portions. Recipe by Jackie Prang, 1-21-71.

title: Ship's Cabin Mimosa
directions: Place orange juice in tulip-shaped champagne glass.
Fill with champagne.
Float Grand Marnier on top.
notes: At the Ship's Cabin in Norfolk, the champagne cocktail has replaced the martini for many people, says Scott McWhinney. 'Champagne is such a showy and atmospheric drink,' he says, 'many people don't want to wait for a celebration to drink it.'

title: Shrimp Bisque
ingredients: 1 pound uncooked shrimp, shelled and deveined (Do not cook!)
directions: Mince uncooked shrimp and set aside.
Place butter in a heavy pot; add onion and cook on low until onion is golden.
Add half and half, fish seasoning cube and uncooked shrimp.
Cook on low for 15-20 minutes. DO NOT BOIL!
When ready to serve, stir in vinegar, parsley or chives, salt, pepper and nutmeg.
Yields 6 cups.
notes: This bisque is best made ahead of time and allowed to sit for at least 30 minutes before serving. It can be made a day ahead. Do not add last five ingredients until ready to serve. "Wonderfully rich!"

title: Shrimp Grits
ingredients: 1 1/3 cups quick grits or reg (NOT INSTANT)
1 1/2 c. parmesan cheese - shredded - less if using grated
directions: Bring water to boil & salt & chicken bouillon.
Add grits & bring to a second boil & stir constantly for 3 mins.
Add cream & boil again for 1 min.
Add shrimp & lemon pepper to cooked grits & stir in shrimp.
Bring to a boil & then turn off heat & cover.
Let stand for 20 mins. (shrimp will cook during this time).
When ready to serve, boil once again & add cheese stirring until melted - Serve
notes: Makes: 10-12

title: Shrimp Mold - Lg Size
ingredients: 2 T gelatin (or 1 pkg 3 ounce lemon jello)
1 c cold water (omit water if using jello)
directions: Boil soup, add cream cheese, stir till smooth.
Add gelatin.
Cool, add rest and stir.
Chill to set.
notes: Recipe notes indicate an alternative for the gelatin: using 1 package of 3 ounce lemon gelatin instead of 2 tablespoons of plain gelatin, in which case the cold water should be omitted.

title: Smoked Salmon Tartar
directions: Mince all ingredients and combine.
notes: Optional: serve with cucumber rounds, sliced avocados, and bread rounds.

title: Sour Kraut Salad
ingredients: 1 qt. Old Fashioned Krout (wash krout & chop fine)
directions: Mix all.

title: Spaghetti with Asparagus
ingredients: 1 chicken bouillon or 1 t. chicken stock base
directions: Heat butter & oil in 1 qt. saucepan over med-high.
Add onion & sauté until golden (don't brown).
Add ham & sauté briefly.
Add asparagus, water, & bouillon.
Reduce heat & simmer about 15 min.
Add spaghetti to lg. pot of rapidly boiling salted water & cook until al dente, about 5-6 min.
Drain well.
Return spaghetti to pot.
Add asparagus mixture & half & half & cook over med-low until warmed through.
Top w/ parmesan & pepper before serving.
notes: good; Laura 6/85

title: Sparkling Champagne Punch
ingredients: 4 (6 ounce.) cans frozen lemonade, thawed & undiluted
4 (6 ounce.) cans frozen pineapple juice, thawed & undiluted
directions: Combine first 3 ingredients; chill well.
To serve punch, pour juice over ice mold.
Gently stir in ginger ale, tonic water, & champagne.
notes: Yield: 7 qts.

title: Spicy Stir-fried Asparagus
directions: Wash and trim asparagus; cut into diagonal slices.
Heat oil in wok or large skillet; add asparagus and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Remove from pan.
Stir ginger and garlic into skillet; add red pepper and stir-fry one minute.
Add soy sauce, broth, Szechwan sauce and sugar.
Return asparagus to skillet; heat through.
Place on serving plate and sprinkle with walnuts.
Serves 6.
notes: The spicy flavor of this dish can be varied by the amount of Szechwan sauce used. Serve with grilled lamb and fresh fruit!

title: Spinach Salad
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mary Sue Marchese. Serves 6.

title: Spinach Savay
directions: Drain uncooked spinach.
Combine with sour cream and soup mix.
Top with cheese and bacon crumbles.
Bake at 350° for 20 min.
Serves 6
notes: Can be made early in the day.

title: Split Pea Soup
ingredients: 1 package dried onion soup mix (preferably Lipton)
1½ cups baby carrots, rinsed and sliced
1 large or 2 small leeks, stripped of their outer leaves, rinsed, and chopped
3 or 4 tablespoon tamari or soy sauce
directions: In a large pot, combine peas, broth, water, and soup mix. Stir well. Add carrots, onions, celery, leeks, garlic, mustard, tamari, and balsamic vinegar. If mixture seems too thick, pour in a little more water.
Bring to a full boil over medium, reduce heat to a simmer, and cook for about 2 hours, stirring and skimming surface occasionally.
Remove from heat and let sit for an hour at room temperature.
Puree, in several batches, in a food processor or blender until smooth. Add salt and pepper to taste.
notes: SERVES: 10 | PER SERVING: 170 calories, 30g carbs, 11g protein, 1.5g fat, 0mg cholesterol, 1,060mg sodium, 9g fiber

title: Split Pea Soup
ingredients: 16-ounce. pkg. Jack Rabbit Green Split Peas
2 chicken bouillon cubes or 2 tablespoons instant chicken bouillon
directions: In large deep pot, combine peas, water, ham shank, onion, chicken bouillon and seasonings.
Simmer, uncovered, 1 1/2 hours.
Remove ham shank; trim meat off bone and return meat to pot.
Stir in carrots and celery.
Simmer, uncovered, an additional 2 to 2 1/2 hours or until soup reaches desired thickness.
notes: Makes 6 (1 1/2-cup) servings.

title: Springtime Asparagus
ingredients: ⅛ teaspoon freshly ground black pepper
directions: Starting 2 inches below the tip, use a vegetables peeler to remove outer covering from stalks; cut off tough ends.
In a large skillet add asparagus and just enough water to cover; bring to a boil and simmer 2-4 minutes or until just tender; drain and place on a warmed platter.
Put egg through a fine sieve or strainer and sprinkle over asparagus.
Melt butter in small skillet; allow to brown slightly; add parsley, salt and pepper and spoon over asparagus.
Sprinkle lightly with nutmeg.
Serves 4.
notes: Delicious with a grilled butterflied leg of lamb!

title: Squash Souffle
directions: Combine squash, salt, syrup, brown sugar & cornstarch. Beat until fluffy.
Add egg yolks, cream & butter. Mix thoroughly.
Beat egg whites till stiff. Fold into squash mixture.
Put in 1 1/2 qt buttered casserole.
Bake @ 350° for 1 hr.
Sprinkle almonds on top.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson; Ann Luther 1993

title: Steamed Asparagus with Pistachio Butter
ingredients: 2 pounds of asparagus spears, trimmed of tough ends
directions: Steam asparagus until fork tender; drain well and keep warm.
Melt butter or margarine in a small skillet; add marjoram and nuts and stir for 1 minute.
Spoon pistachio butter over warm asparagus.
Serves 4-6.
notes: Delicious with crab imperial or a seafood casserole.

title: Steamed Green Beans Almond Dill
directions: Tip green beans on both ends and place in a steamer over boiling water.
Top with garlic, pepper and fresh dill.
Steam until just tender.
Move to a serving dish and dot with butter.
Toss in toasted almonds.
Serve immediately.
notes: Serves 4 to 6. ©1995 Shenandoah Growers — Harrisonburg, Virginia

title: Stein Eriksen's Classic Fondue
ingredients: FOR DIPPING: Country Italian bread cubes, apple and pear sections
directions: Rub bottom of heavy medium saucepan with garlic.
Discard garlic; add wine and cream; bring to boil.
Stir together cornstarch and water; stir into cream mixture.
Cook and stir until slightly thickened and bubbling.
Gradually add cheese; stir until melted.
Stir in nutmeg, salt, and white pepper to taste.
Stir in Kirschwasser.
Pour into fondue pot; place over fondue burner.
Fondue will thicken as it holds over burner.
Serve with dippers.
notes: Makes 3 1/2 cups or 10 to 12 appetizer servings. Regional contributor: Sally Mauer. Tabletop stylist: Susan Victoria. For more information, see the Reader's Resource on page 138.

title: Strawberry Jam Muffins
ingredients: 12 teaspoons strawberry jam or strawberry preserves
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees.
Grease 12 muffin tins.
Sift flour, sugar, baking powder and salt into a mixing bowl; add lemon peel.
Combine milk, oil and egg; beat with a fork until well mixed.
Make a well in the center of the flour; add milk mixture all at one time and stir ONLY until ingredients are moistened. DO NOT OVER MIX!
Place 1 tablespoon batter in bottom of each tin, top with 1 teaspoon strawberry jam or preserves and top with an additional tablespoon of batter.
Sprinkle muffin tops with sugar and cinnamon.
Bake approximately 18-20 minutes or until the center springs back when touched gently.
Yields 12 large muffins.
notes: Work quickly when putting the batter and jam in the muffin tins; bake immediately. Measurement for baking powder is correct. Homemade preserves can be used in this recipe. The strawberry center provides a delicious surprise. Serve hot with soft butter!

title: Strawberry Romaine Salad
directions: Mix the first 7 ingredients and shake vigorously.
Pour over lettuce mixture.
notes: Recipe by Nancy Dawson. Makes 12 servings.

title: Strawberry Salad W Pretzel Crust
directions: Layer #1: Mix crushed pretzels and melted butter. Press into the bottom of a 9x13 pan. Bake for 10 minutes at 300°F. Let cool.
Layer #2: Mix cream cheese and sugar. Fold in Cool Whip. Spread over Layer #1.
Layer #3: Mix Jell-O and boiling water until Jell-O is dissolved. Add strawberries and stir until thickened. Spread over Layer #2.
Chill before serving.
notes: Recipe attributed to Brenda Owens, 1990.

title: Strawberry Salad
directions: Dissolve jello in water.
Add strawberries, pineapple, bananas, and nuts.
Place mixture in mold until set firm.
Spread on sour cream.
Spoon on rest of salad mix and let all set firm.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mary Faye Long.

title: Strawberry Soup
directions: Clean strawberries and puree in blender.
Add all ingredients.
Mix well.
Chill.
Top with whip cream and fresh strawberry.
notes: Excellent. Enjoy!

title: Strawberry-orange Cooler - Jerri Buell
ingredients: 1 pkg (10 ounce) frozen strawberries, partially thawed
directions: Put 1st 2 ingredients in blender - turn high
Then add ice cream - blend until smooth.
notes: 2 servings

title: Strawberry-red Leaf Salad
ingredients: 1 cup sliced celery, cut on diagonal
directions: For the dressing: Combine all ingredients except poppy seeds in a blender. Slowly add oil. Stir in poppy seeds. Refrigerate.
For the caramelized pecans: Combine sugar and pecans in a heavy pan. Slowly cook until all sugar has melted onto pecans and they are browned. Immediately place on waxed paper. Cool.
Combine all ingredients for salad with dressing and toss.
notes: Recipe from Nancy Dawson, transcribed by Anne Luther '92.

title: String Beans Amandine
directions: Remove ends from fresh green beans.
Cut beans French-fashion in long strips.
Tie into portion-size bundles with string.
Cook in salted water as usual.
Lift bundles to a serving dish and remove the string.
Heat butter with shaved almonds until the almonds are lightly browned.
Pour over beans.
notes: 4-5 servings

title: Stuffed Green Peppers Dip
directions: Blend all ingredients.
Fill green pepper.
Chill.
Serve.
notes: Recipe dated Sept 1971; includes a reference to 'c Fritos' on the reverse side.

title: Summer Squash and Corn
ingredients: 1-2 ears of corn (cut corn from the cob)
directions: Fry bacon; remove from pan and save.
Saute onion in bacon grease until it begins to become transparent.
Add squash and saute 3-4 minutes.
Add water and sugar; cover and cook over low heat approximately 15 minutes.
Remove top; add cut corn, cover and continue to cook for 5 additional minutes.
Garnish with bacon.
Serves 4.
notes: This recipe can easily be halved or doubled. You will be amazed how delicious the corn is when added to the squash!

title: Summer Tomato Pasta
ingredients: 1 lb very ripe vine-ripened tomatoes, diced (skin on)
Pinch of crushed red pepper flakes
directions: Place tomatoes in a bowl and add the remaining ingredients except linguine.
Mix well and set aside for 3 hours at room temperature.
Cook linguine until al dente.
Remove and add to the tomato sauce.
notes: Variations include balsamic vinegar (good Italian), shallots, bell peppers, fresh sage, or jalapeño peppers.

title: Summer Tomato Salsa
ingredients: 1-2 tablespoons canned green chilies, chopped (hot or mild)
1 teaspoon dried fresh cilantro OR 1 tablespoon dried cilantro
directions: Spray a large teflon-coated skillet; sauté garlic and onion over medium heat until light golden.
Add next five ingredients; bring to boil.
Add all remaining salsa ingredients; stir to mix well.
Allow to simmer for 30 minutes.
Serve hot or chill until ready to use.
notes: Serving suggestions: Top grilled chicken, fish or grilled vegetables with salsa. Serve with rice and a fresh fruit salad. Use on grilled meat, seafood or vegetables!

title: Summer Tomato Soup
directions: Place all soup ingredients in blender and blend well.
Peel, seed and dice tomato.
Place tomato and all remaining vegetables in 1-quart container.
Pour soup mixture over vegetables.
Chill well.
When ready to serve, place gazpacho in bowls and top with croutons, parsley and pepper.
Serve with hot bread.
notes: Yields 3 cups or 6 half-cup servings. When serving, be sure to evenly distribute vegetables in each bowl.

title: Sunday Morning Sausage Biscuits
directions: Crumble and fry sausage until golden brown.
Remove sausage from pan and set aside.
Add flour to hot pan drippings and allow to bubble 1-2 minutes.
Remove from heat and slowly add milk.
Blend until smooth; cook over low heat until thickened.
Add sausage and seasonings.
Serve over hot biscuits.
Serves 8.
notes: This dish can be prepared ahead of time and kept in the refrigerator for a day or two. Reheat over low heat when ready to serve. Great for a crowd! Delicious with fried or escalloped apples!

title: Super Slaw
ingredients: 2 large red or yellow bell peppers, cut into matchstick-size strips
2 medium carrots, peeled, cut into matchstick-size strips
8 large green onions, cut into matchstick-size strips
directions: Whisk first 7 ingredients in small bowl to blend.
Combine remaining ingredients in large bowl.
Add dressing and toss to coat.
Season with salt and pepper and serve.
notes: Dressing can be made 1 day ahead. Cover and chill. Let stand at room temperature 30 minutes before continuing.

title: Sweet & Sour Bean Salad - Palmer
ingredients: 1 cup each green beans, wax beans, kidney beans (washed & drained)
Salt & Lawry's seasoned salt to taste
directions: Mix sugar, vinegar, and water until sugar is dissolved.
Mix all together.
Let stand overnight.

title: Sweet Potato Casserole
ingredients: 3 cups sweet potatoes, cooked and mashed
directions: Mix the sweet potato ingredients together and put in an 8x8 dish.
For the topping, mix the butter, brown sugar, flour, and pecans together.
Crumble topping over the potato mixture.
Bake 30 minutes at 350°.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Laurie Dawson. Serves 6-8.

title: Sweet Potato Souffle W. Sherry & Walnuts
ingredients: 1/2 cup black walnuts or reg. walnuts
directions: Whip in machine till light.
Fold in pan and bake @ 350° for 30 mins.
Sprinkle c walnuts.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson; Olney Inn recipe.
pdfLink: pdfs/Sweet Potato Souffle w. Sherry & Walnuts.pdf

title: Sweet Potato Souffle
ingredients: 1/2 cup hot milk (or more according to size of potatoes)
directions: Boil yams until soft.
Mash yams and add hot milk, butter, brown sugar, egg yolks, pecans, cinnamon, cloves, and nutmeg.
Beat 2 egg whites until stiff.
Fold egg whites into the potato mixture.
Pour into a buttered baking dish.
Put marshmallows on top.
Bake at 325°–350° for 15–20 minutes until browned.
notes: Recipe attributed to Marje Palmer, March '62.

title: Taco Salad
ingredients: 1 15 ounce can red kidney beans, drained well
directions: Shred lettuce and set aside.
Combine avocado, sour cream, Italian dressing, green onions, chili powder and salt.
Place lettuce in the bottom of a flat bowl; top with beans, olives and tomatoes.
Spoon avocado dressing over the salad and top with cracked pepper, cheese and chips.
Toss and serve.
notes: Serve as a main dish on a hot night! If serving this salad from a buffet, it can be assembled as described but the chips should be placed around the edge. Do not toss until ready to serve. Well-drained cooked ground beef can be added if desired. The delicious avocado dressing can be used as a dip! Serves 6-8.

title: Tropical Fruit Salad
ingredients: 2 15 1/2 ounce cans unsweetened pineapple chunks, drained
2 large navel oranges, peeled and diced
1 large (or 2 medium) red delicious apple, diced (do not peel)
1/8 cup lemon juice (fresh or Minute Maid frozen)
directions: Combine all ingredients except the lettuce, sherbet and cherries.
Toss gently; do not bruise the fruit.
Chill and serve on lettuce; top with sherbet and garnish with a cherry.
Serves 8-10.
notes: This is extremely easy to prepare and makes a beautiful salad plate. Popular with everybody! Other sherbet flavors are also delicious!

title: Tuscan White Bean Salad
ingredients: 16-20 ounces canned white cannellini beans, drained
1/4 - 1/2 cup sliced Nicoise or Kalamata olives, drained
4 tablespoons Chianti red wine vinegar or red wine vinegar
2 anchovies, finely chopped or 1 teaspoon anchovy paste
directions: Combine all salad ingredients and toss gently with dressing.
Chill several hours or overnight.
To serve: Spoon salad into shallow platter and garnish with fresh oregano and parsley.
notes: The dressing is the secret! Serves 6-8. This salad is also delicious with 1 can water-packed (well-drained) tuna added. Great to make ahead and take to fall picnics or tailgates!

title: Taco Beef Soup
directions: Brown beef with onion & drain.
Add next 5 ingredients & simmer about 45 minutes.
Add avocado.
Serve w/ cheese, chips & sour cream.
notes: Recipe from Jeri

title: Tangy Tomato Soup
ingredients: 3 cans Campbell's cream of tomato soup
directions: Mix & whisk
Add more tomato soup or milk to taste
Serve hot or cold
Sprinkle chives on top
notes: Serves 12

title: Tasty Multi-bean Soup
ingredients: 2 C. Cubed Ham (or 2 t. Bouillon granules)
directions: Cover the beans with water and sprinkle on salt.
Soak the beans overnight.
Add Ham, Tomatoes, Red Pepper Pod, Garlic then simmer for three (3) hours.
Add the lemon juice and simmer 30 minutes longer.
Enjoy!
notes: Recipe source: In Good Taste, 1124 Sam Rittenberg Blvd., Charleston, S.C. 29407 (803) 763-5597

title: Tavern Cheese Spread
directions: Blend
Refrigerate
notes: Served best at room temp.

title: Tex Mex Dip
ingredients: Sour cream mixed with taco seasoning
directions: Layer ingredients in order.
Serve with tostadas.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson.

title: Thanksgiving Salad - Good
directions: Mix raspberry or cherry Jello as directed; chill to consistency of jelly (use orange juice and lemon juice instead of the cold H2O).
Have round mold well greased with butter.
Take 1 or 2 packages cream cheese, mix with juice of lemon and orange to soften, roll into little balls and roll them in ground nuts.
Place all around in the bottom of mold and maraschino cherries between each ball.
Pour Jello over this and chill.
Unmold and fill the middle with cottage cheese, garnish with frosted grapes and lettuce.
notes: Good.

title: The 2-minute Hot Buttered Rum
ingredients: 1 1/2 ounces dark rum (or rum flavoring to taste) (per serving)
directions: Cream 1/4 lb. of butter with 1 lb. of dark brown sugar.
Sprinkle and mix thoroughly into batter 1/4 tsp. each of ground cinnamon, ground nutmeg and ground cloves.
Store in a covered container in the refrigerator.
To serve: place one heaping tbsp. of batter into each cup or mug.
Add 1 1/2 ounces dark rum (or rum flavoring to taste).
Fill with boiling hot water, stir and serve.
notes: The batter can be made ahead of time and kept refrigerated. The total preparation time to serve is two minutes.

title: Three Vegetable Sauté
directions: Slice zucchini and summer squash thinly.
Sauté in olive oil with garlic for 15 minutes or until tender.
Remove and discard garlic.
Add drained preserved beans.
Heat vegetable mixture for 3 minutes.
Season with salt, pepper, oregano, and lemon pepper.

title: Tiropites (cheese Puffs)
directions: Beat eggs and mix in cheeses.
Cut layers of phyllo dough into four strips.
Separate the layers one at a time—if it is difficult to separate, then use 2 or 3 layers.
Spread a strip of phyllo on countertop and brush with melted butter.
Place a teaspoon of filling at the left end and fold over a triangle (A to A').
Continue folding in triangles until it's all folded up, tucking end under.
Bake at 300-325° until golden brown (about 20 mins).
notes: The recipe includes a diagram showing the 'A to A'' triangular folding technique.

title: Toast Crispies
ingredients: 1 loaf Pepperidge Farm thin sliced white bread
directions: Trim crust from bread, cut each slice into 3 strips.
Spray 2 medium jelly roll pans with Pam.
Arrange strips close together on pans.
Mix sugar, butter & zest together & beat until dissolved.
Spread evenly over strips.
Bake @ 250° for 1 hr.
Cool on wire rack & store in airtight containers.
notes: From the kitchen of Bev Taylor.

title: Toasted Almond Sauce
ingredients: 1 1/3 cups toasted sliced or slivered almonds
directions: In a large saucepan melt butter; stir in sugars, cream, and water.
Bring to boiling; reduce heat.
Boil gently, stirring frequently, till mixture thickens slightly, about 15 minutes.
Remove from heat.
Stir in vanilla and almonds.
Cover and chill until needed; reheat to serve warm or at room temperature.
notes: Makes 4 cups (sixteen 1/4-cup servings.) Note: To make more sauce, it's best to make the basic recipe as many times as needed rather than double or triple the recipe.

title: Tomato Aspic
directions: Pour 1 cup of the tomato juice into a measuring cup. Sprinkle gelatin over juice; stir for a couple of seconds. Set aside.
Pour remaining 3 cups tomato juice into a 2-quart saucepan. Set saucepan on a burner, but do NOT turn on heat yet.

Rinse and dry celery. Cut celery rib into 1/8-inch-thick lengthwise strips. Holding strips together, cut them into 3-inch pieces. Holding each bundle of strips together, cut crosswise into tiny pieces. You need to have at least 1 cup chopped celery.
Slice off and discard fuzzy brownish root end and stem top of onion. Peel off and discard papery outer brownish-yellow skin of onion.
Put onion half cut-side down on a cutting board. Cut slices crosswise from stem top to root end. Then holding the onion together, chop lengthwise into tiny pieces. You'll need 1 cup of chopped onion.
Add chopped celery, onion, bay leaf, sugar, salt and pepper to the 3 cups tomato juice in the saucepan. Stir in tomato juice/dissolved gelatin mixture.
Turn heat to medium. Gently warm juice mixture, stirring now and then, until it is hot. Do NOT let it boil.
Select a 1 1/2-quart bowl, dish or mold.
Remove bay leaf, then pour the warm mixture into the desired bowl or pan; let cool. Cover with plastic wrap and refrigerate until aspic jells and you are ready to serve.
To turn the aspic out, put container in hot water for a few seconds to soften the outer surface and allow you to slide it out onto a platter.
notes: Must be made ahead of time because it takes 2 or more hours to chill and set up. It stores well in the refrigerator for 4 or 5 days. Nutrients per serving: 85 calories, 6 grams protein, 18 grams carbohydrate, no fat, no cholesterol, 3 grams fiber, 1,445 milligrams sodium.

title: Tomato and Zucchini Salad with Caper Vinaigrette
directions: Halve tomato slices.
Line plates w/ lettuce.
Mound zucchini in center.
Arrange tomatoes in ring around zucchini.
Sprinkle onion over zucchini.
Mix vinegar, capers, chives, & parsley in small bowl.
Slowly whisk in oil in thin stream.
Season w/ salt & pepper.
Spoon over salads & serve.
notes: Recipe yields enough for 2 and servings. Contributed by Lama Hodge, 6/85.
pdfLink: pdfs/Tomato and Zucchini Salad with Caper Vinaigrette.pdf

title: Tortellini Salad
ingredients: 4 cups vegetables, blanched (red peppers, yellow squash, zucchini, broccoli)
1 orange (optional, white membrane removed and cut up)
directions: Cook tortellini for 8 minutes.
Blanch the vegetables.
Mix sauce ingredients together (lemon juice, Dijon, veg oil, olive oil, thyme).
Toss all together.
Chill before serving.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Julia Desgalier.

title: Toss Salad for a Crowd
directions: Layer the lettuce, celery, onion, green pepper, and cooked peas in a large salad bowl.
Combine the sour cream and mayonnaise.
Spread the sour cream and mayonnaise mixture over all the layered ingredients.
Top with the crumbled bacon and shredded Cheddar cheese.
Cover and place in the refrigerator for 8 hours.
notes: Very good.

title: Trappes Hot Potato Salad
directions: Fry out the bacon to get the grease.
While hot, mix the flour into the bacon grease.
Add sugar and vinegar.
Cook until thickened.
Pour over hot potatoes and serve.
notes: Recipe dated 1970 by Jerry Bierl. Note on card emphasizes to "Do while hot."

title: Tropical Relish
directions: Put cranberries through food chopper.
Quarter lemon, remove seeds, and put through food chopper (or cut lemon into 6 or 8 pieces and grind with the berries).
Add pineapple and blend all with sugar.
notes: Will keep several weeks in refrigerator.

title: Tuna Dip - Jerri Burd
notes: Recipe attributed to Jerri Burd.

title: Twin Loaf Cheese Salad
directions: Combine cottage cheese, sour cream, and milk.
In saucepan, sprinkle gelatin on H2O to soften.
Place over low heat, stir until gelatin is dissolved.
Remove from heat, stir in onion juice and salt.
Gradually add cottage cheese mixture.
Fold in remaining ingredients.
Pour into molds; chill until firm.
Grease mold before filling.
notes: 12 servings

title: U.s. Senate Bean Soup
ingredients: Ham bone with some meat on it
1 small bunch of celery including the tops, finely chopped
directions: Soak 1 pound white beans overnight in cold water and cover.
Drain the beans and put them in a soup kettle with a ham bone that still has some meat on it and 3 quarts water.
Bring the water to a boil and simmer the mixture for about 2 hours.
Stir in 1 cup cooked mashed potatoes and add 3 onions, 1 small bunch of celery including the tops, and 2 garlic cloves, all finely chopped, and 1/4 cup chopped parsley.
Simmer the soup for 1 hour longer, until the beans are thoroughly cooked.
Remove the ham bone from the kettle, dice the meat on it, and return the meat to the soup.
notes: Serves 6. As served daily in the U.S. Senate Cafeteria.

title: Ukrop's Words Worth Eating Blueberry Bread (from Ukrops Words Worth Eating)
directions: Preheat oven to 350.
Have all ingredients at room temperature.
Use electric mixer on medium to cream sugar and butter until light and fluffy.
Beat in eggs, one at a time.
In a separate bowl, combine all dry ingredients and stir well.
Add dry ingredients to batter alternately with milk; end with flour.
Fold in blueberries.
Pour batter into 3 (9 x 5 x 3) greased and floured loaf pans.
Combine topping and sprinkle on each loaf.
Bake 45-50 minutes or until center springs back when pressed lightly. Do not overbake.
