Combine mustard, paprika, brown sugar, salt, Worcestershire sauce, vinegar, ketchup; add to mustard mixture; add to meat; add 1 cup of water; stir; cover cook over low heat 2 1/2 hours.
Blend flour with remaining 1/2 cup water, add to meat mixture; stir until thickened.
Boil noodles in salt water - drain.
Serve meat over noodles.
notes: 8 servings
pdfLink: Hearty Hungarian Beef Goulash and Noodles.pdf

title: Hearty Onion and Soy Marinated Round Steak Casserole with Mushrooms and Vegetables
ingredients: Round steak (slivered, easier when partially frozen)
1 package onion soup mix (or mushroom onion)
Japanese vegetables or broccoli (added in the last 30 minutes, optional)
directions: Dissolve 2 cups of hot water with 2 bouillon cubes and 1 package of onion soup mix (or mushroom onion). Add 2 tablespoons of soy sauce.
Pour over meat and add celery, pepper, and mushrooms if desired.
Cover and bake at 325 degrees Fahrenheit for about 1.5 hours.
For the last 30 minutes, add Japanese vegetables or broccoli if desired.
notes: Good served with rice and fruit. Recipe from Anne Luther and Irene Kennedy.
pdfLink: Hearty Onion and Soy Marinated Round Steak Casserole with Mushrooms and Vegetables.pdf

title: Jumbo Deluxe Surprise Burgers with Melted Cheese and Bacon
ingredients: 6 tablespoons Oscar Mayer real bacon bits
6 large sandwich rolls or hamburger rolls
directions: Divide the beef into twelve 3-ounce patties.
Brown the bacon bits lightly on foil in a toaster oven or broiler.
Arrange 6 patties on a tray.
Top each patty with: 1 tablespoon bacon bits, 1 slice of cheese which has been folded in quarters, 1/2 teaspoon mustard, 1/8 teaspoon pepper and 1/8 teaspoon salt.
Place the 6 remaining patties on top and seal the edges of the two patties by pressing firmly with your fingertips.
Grill over a medium-hot charcoal fire for approximately 6-7 minutes on the first side and 5 minutes on the second.
This produces a burger with a pink center.
Since fires vary greatly, the cooking time may have to be adjusted.
Serve in a roll with lettuce, tomato and mayonnaise.
Serves 6.
notes: You only need one of these jumbo burgers per person. "Best served in a large deli-style roll!"
pdfLink: Jumbo Deluxe Surprise Burgers with Melted Cheese and Bacon.pdf

title: Greek Eggplant and Beef Moussaka with Bechamel
ingredients: 1 bay leaf and 1 hot dried red pepper
directions: Trim eggplant peel, cut into 3/4 inch cubes, toss with 1 teaspoon salt. Set aside.
Brown meat, add onion, garlic, cinnamon, bay leaf, and cook.
Add eggplant, cook 5 minutes.
Add tomatoes, hot pepper, salt, and pepper. Cook 30 minutes. Stir.
Melt butter, add flour, milk, salt, and pepper.
Stir cornstarch and water into sauce, cook 1 minute, remove, and add yolks.
Cook noodles, add to meat, spread sauce over, and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 400 degrees for 20 to 30 minutes.
notes: Jackie Pfrang 1978
pdfLink: Greek Eggplant and Beef Moussaka with Bechamel.pdf

title: Sherry Beef with Mushrooms
ingredients: 1 package Lipton onion or mushroom soup
directions: Mix and cover
Bake at 300 degrees for 3 hours
Serve over rice or noodles
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Anne King. Serves 6-8.
pdfLink: No Peeky Sherry Beef with Mushrooms.pdf

title: Sauerbraten Patties with Ginger Snaps and Egg Noodles
directions: Soak bread in a little warm H2O; crumble. Add meat, onion, egg, and salt; mix well. Shape into 4 patties.
Brown on both sides in margarine. Add the next 5 ingredients, cover and simmer about 1 hour.
Serve on hot cooked noodles.
4 servings
pdfLink: Sauerbraten Patties with Ginger Snaps and Egg Noodles.pdf

title: Beef in Burgundy
ingredients: 4 pounds chuck, trimmed, cut in 2-inch cubes
2 1/2 tablespoons potato flour; or 1/4 cup unsifted all-purpose flour
directions: meat-extract paste, and tomato to paste until smooth.
Gradually add Burgundy, stirring until smooth.
Then add beef, pepper, herbs, parsley sprigs, and mushrooms, stirring until well mixed; bake, covered, 1 1/2 hours.
Add onions; bake 1 hour longer, or until meat is tender.
Sprinkle with chopped parsley.
Serve with Gnocchi, page 170.
Makes 8 servings.
notes: Marked as "Very Good"

title: Epicurean Spiced Pot Roast with Marinade
directions: Slit eye-of-the-round beef in several places.
Rub into slits mixture of: 1 cup flour, 0.5 teaspoon freshly ground pepper, 1 tablespoon salt, 0.5 teaspoon allspice, 0.5 teaspoon ground cloves.
Place meat in deep bowl, marinate overnight in refrigerator in: 2 tablespoons vinegar, 1 tablespoon lemon juice, 0.25 cup oil, 1 large onion, chopped, 1 clove garlic, minced.
Drain and brown in 0.25 cup oil.
Add marinade and 1.5 cups tomato juice.
Roast uncovered, in oven and baste frequently for 3 hours.
Remove and slice thinly.
Serves 8.
pdfLink: Epicurean Spiced Pot Roast with Marinade.pdf

title: Weber Grill Stuffed Meatloaf with Celery and Bacon
directions: Remove celery leaves and cut celery heart to about 8 to 9 inches long—wash and dry. (Keep bottom of celery intact—do not remove root.) Gently pull branches apart and sprinkle with salt.
Combine cheese and pimiento, spread generously between celery branches. Wrap heart tightly in foil and chill while preparing meat loaf.
Combine all remaining ingredients except bacon and mix.
Turn meat mixture onto large sheet of waxed paper and pat out to an oval of about 11 x 12 x 3/4 inches.
Cut off only the very bottom of root of celery heart—place on center of meat.
Fold meat up and over celery—pat into roll shape, completely enclosing celery.
Lay bacon slices in chevron pattern over top of roll (overlap slices slightly). Gently lift roll on one side and tuck bacon underneath. Repeat on other side (use picks if necessary).
Tie roll securely with string—wrap in foil—seal top with drugstore fold—do not close ends.
Using indirect method—place meat loaf over drip pan and cook 1 1/4 hours (drain grease into drip pan occasionally by pushing foil down and letting it run in pan).
Remove foil and cook 20 minutes longer.
Bake potatoes at same time on grill!
notes: 10 to 12 servings.
pdfLink: Weber Grill Stuffed Meatloaf with Celery and Bacon.pdf

title: Grilled Foil Pot Roast with Lipton Onion Soup
directions: Brown one side of a round bone roast on the grill.
Have some heavy aluminum foil ready and sprinkle most of a package of Lipton's onion soup in foil.
Place raw side of meat in dehydrated soup.
Sprinkle remainder of package on browned side of meat and wrap securely in foil.
Grill over low heat for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, raw side down.
pdfLink: Grilled Foil Pot Roast with Lipton Onion Soup.pdf

title: Baked Teriyaki Meatballs
ingredients: 3 pounds extra-lean or lean ground beef
1 1/2 to 2 cloves garlic, minced very fine
directions: Form meat into approximately 100 one-inch meatballs.
Place compactly in a 9 x 13 baking pan.
Combine marinade from soy sauce, water, ginger and garlic.
Pour over meat and allow to marinate for one hour at room temperature.
Preheat oven to 275; bake uncovered for 35 to 40 minutes or until meatballs are firm.
Do not overcook since they are kept warm while serving and continue to cook.
Serve in sauce from a heated dish or chafing dish.
notes: Meatballs can be formed a day ahead or early in the day. Place in baking pan and wrap tightly; add marinade as directed in recipe. "Extra easy since there's no browning involved!"

title: Grilled Marinated Chuck Steak
ingredients: 2 1/2 to 3 pound chuck steak, trimmed of excess fat
directions: Place steak on cutting board; use sharp fork to pierce meat all over on both sides.
Combine all marinade ingredients and mix well.
Place chuck steak and marinade in a large, heavy-duty, sealed plastic bag; seal securely.
Marinate overnight in refrigerator, turning bag several times.
Remove steak from bag when ready to cook; reserve marinade to use while grilling.
Cook on a hot grill for 4 to 8 minutes per side, depending on thickness of steak.
Brush continually with marinade.
Do not over cook.
Discard any unused marinade.
Slice on the diagonal in thin slices.
Serves 4 to 6.
notes: Everyone always wants a good recipe for chuck steak!

title: Geri's "you'll Never Believe It" Slow-roasted Prime Rib
directions: Place roast in roasting pan uncovered and put in 375 degree oven for 1 hour.
Turn off the oven, but do not open the oven door at all.
For rare roast beef: 45 minutes before serving time turn oven to 300 degrees.
For medium roast beef: 50 minutes before serving time turn oven to 300 degrees.
For medium well roast beef: 55 minutes before serving time turn oven to 300 degrees.
That's all - and don't peek!
notes: Recipe from: Geri. This can be started in mid-afternoon... and it works!
pdfLink: Geri's You'll Never Believe It Slow-Roasted Prime Rib.pdf

title: Chicken with Shallots and Mushrooms
ingredients: 4 boneless chicken breasts, all skin removed
1 cup shredded part-skim milk mozzarella cheese
1 teaspoon minced green onion tops, for garnish
directions: Sauté chicken in butter or margarine in uncovered skillet over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes; turn once. Add mushrooms and shallots and season with salt and pepper; continue cooking for 8 to 10 additional minutes or until chicken is tender.
Place chicken on serving dish; top with mushrooms and shallots. Sprinkle cheese over chicken and cover tightly with foil. Let stand 5 minutes or until cheese melts. Sprinkle with green onions.
Serves 4.
notes: Serve with steamed vegetables marinara! Marked as "Very Good"

title: Chicken and Rice Casserole with Veggies and Toasted Almonds
ingredients: 1 10½ ounce can cream of mushroom soup, regular or reduced calorie
½ cup chopped sweet red pepper
¼ - ½ cup sliced canned mushrooms
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Combine all casserole ingredients and spoon into a shallow 2-quart casserole.
Combine topping ingredients and spoon on casserole.
Bake uncovered for 30-40 minutes or until casserole is heated through and top is golden brown.
Serves 6.
notes: Serve with a fresh fruit salad!
pdfLink: Chicken and Rice Casserole with Veggies and Toasted Almonds.pdf

title: Skillet Chicken Tetrazzini
directions: Melt butter in skillet, add onion and celery and cook until clear.
Arrange chicken in layers, add spaghetti.
Mix salt, pepper, soup and broth. Pour over spaghetti.
Place mushrooms over top.
Sprinkle parmesan cheese and paprika.
Cover and cook until steam escapes.
Turn to simmer and cook 30 minutes.
4-6 servings.

title: Crispy Chicken Chimichangas with Spicy Tomatillo Salsa
ingredients: 1 3-4 pound chicken, cut into pieces or 3 cups cooked chicken, boned, skin removed
1/4 cup fresh cilantro leaves, coarsely chopped
directions: Cover chicken with cold water, bring to boil, cover, reduce heat and simmer for 45 minutes until very tender. Allow chicken to cool in broth. Remove chicken from bones, discard skin and bones. Save broth if desired for another recipe. Shred chicken; set aside.
In a medium skillet, saute onion and garlic in oil until onions are transparent.
Add tomatillo salsa and salt. Bring to boil, reduce heat and simmer 5-8 minutes to reduce liquid.
Add chicken and cilantro, cook 10 minutes.

Fill each tortilla with several spoonfuls of filling. Roll one side of tortilla toward center, folding in a small portion of each end toward center. Continue rolling tortilla and secure with a toothpick.
Heat oil in skillet to 400 degrees; fry rolled tortilla until golden crisp, turning once.
Drain on paper toweling. Remove toothpicks and add toppings. Makes 8 chimichangas.
notes:
*If tomatillo salsa is not available, 2 8-ounce cans diced tomatoes with chilies, drained slightly can be substituted.
NOTE: Chimichangas are great with any leftover meat. Shred leftover beef, pork or chicken and saute with onions and garlic. Add chopped green chilies or salsa of your choice and cook, assemble and fry as above.
"Tomatillos and cilantro give this dish authentic Mexican flavor!"
The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
pdfLink: Crispy Chicken Chimichangas with Spicy Tomatillo Salsa.pdf

title: Chicken with Many Flavor Sauce
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken, cut in thin strips
1 sweet red or green pepper, seeded and sliced
1 cup sliced fresh mushrooms or canned straw mushrooms
directions: Prepare marinade and pour over chicken; toss and marinate 1 hour.
Place 1/2 tablespoon oil in heated wok or large frying pan and add garlic, ginger and green onions; stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add next 4 ingredients; mix well and set aside.
Place 1 1/2 tablespoons oil in wok; stir-fry undrained chicken for 2-3 minutes; drain and set aside.
Place remaining 1 tablespoon oil in wok; add all remaining ingredients and stir-fry for 1-2 minutes.
Add cooked chicken and sauce; stir until heated through.
Serve with hot rice.
Serves 4-6.
notes: Turkey or pork can be used in this recipe! Add hot pepper flakes according to personal taste. Pre-sliced, stir-fry chicken can be found in Ukrop's meat department. Garnish with minced green onions!

title: Bombay Chicken Salad with Fresh Peaches and Chutney
ingredients: 1/4 cup sliced green onions, including tops
directions: Combine sour cream, mayonnaise, and curry powder.
Toss gently with remaining ingredients, except peaches, almonds, lemon juice, and lettuce.
Chill several hours before serving.
Dip peaches in lemon juice to prevent turning brown.
Mound chicken salad on lettuce leaves and surround with drained peach slices; top with almonds.
Serves 8-10.
notes: Note: Canned sliced peaches can be substituted for fresh peaches. Could be served in pineapple halves. Marked as "Very Good". "Best served the day it is made!"
pdfLink: Bombay Chicken Salad with Fresh Peaches and Chutney.pdf

title: Bacon-wrapped Chicken Breast Casserole with Chipped Beef and Mushroom Cream Sauce
directions: Line long pan with chipped beef.
Place chicken on top.
Pour mixture over it.
Sprinkle almonds.
Bake 2 hours at 250 degrees covered.
Bake 1 hour at 250 degrees uncovered.
notes: Serves 5 or 6. Recipe from the kitchen of Anne Guthrie, dated 5/13/68. Marked at the top as 'excellent'.
pdfLink: Bacon-Wrapped Chicken Breast Casserole with Chipped Beef and Mushroom Cream Sauce.pdf

title: Hot Chicken Salad with Water Chestnuts and Potato Chip Crust
directions: Stir together first 7 ingredients in a large bowl.
Stir together 1 cup cheese, sour cream, 1 cup mayonnaise, and lemon juice until blended.
Stir into chicken mixture.
Spoon into a lightly greased 9x13 baking dish.
Sprinkle with remaining 1 cup cheese, crushed potato chips, and Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 350° for 30 minutes or until thoroughly heated.
Serves 8
pdfLink: Hot Chicken Salad with Water Chestnuts and Potato Chip Crust.pdf

title: Chicken Saltimbocca with Swiss Cheese and Ham
ingredients: 3 whole large chicken breasts - boned (1 1/2 pounds)
directions: Place chicken bone side up on cutting board - cover with plastic wrap - pound lightly to (6 inches x 5 inches).
Place ham and half slice of cheese on each cutlet.
Top with some tomato and dash of sage. Tuck in sides, roll up - jelly roll fashion - pressing to seal well.
Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese and parsley.
In 12 inches x 7 1/2 inches x 2 inches baking dish - heat butter at High for 30 seconds. Dip chicken in butter then roll in crumbs.
Arrange chicken rolls - seam side down in baking dish - do not touch each other.
Cook covered at Medium High for 10 minutes. Turn - cook Medium High 10 minutes till done.
Place rolls on serving platter - stir blend mixture - spoon over chicken.
6 servings
pdfLink: Chicken Saltimbocca with Swiss Cheese and Ham.pdf

title: Crispy Parmesan Chicken Parmigiana with Butter and Lemon
ingredients: 3/4 cup bread crumbs (2 slices white bread)
directions: Combine flour, salt and pepper; set aside.
Do the same with the eggs and milk and finally combine the bread crumbs and cheese in a flat dish.
Place chicken breasts between 2 sheets of waxed paper and flatten with a wooden mallet.
Dredge the chicken in the flour and shake off excess, dip in egg mixture and then in the bread crumbs.
Be sure to coat well.
Allow chicken breasts to stand for a minimum of 30 minutes before cooking.
Heat butter and oil in a skillet; sauté breasts until golden brown. (Approximately 3 minutes on each side.)
Serve with lemon slices.
Be sure to squeeze a little lemon over each serving.
Serves 4.
notes: If the chicken is to stand longer than 30 minutes, refrigerate. "Too easy for words and yet deliciously fork-tender!"
pdfLink: Crispy Parmesan Chicken Parmigiana with Butter and Lemon.pdf

title: Company Chicken and Artichoke Bake
ingredients: 1-14 ounces can artichoke hearts, drained and halved
directions: Melt butter in skillet, brown chicken breasts. Remove chicken.
Place in 2 quarts casserole. Top with drippings.
Sauté onions and garlic until tender. Then stir in flour and salt.
Cook 1 minute. Slowly add wine and broth.
Cook over medium heat until thick and bubbly. Then add cream cheese. Stir until melted.
Pour over chicken.
Bake at 350 degrees for 40-45 minutes.
Add almonds at end.
notes: May be refrigerated for 24 hours before final baking, and then baked. Recipe Phyllis Mille March 2000

title: Lunch Chicken Salad Patties in Crescent Dough
ingredients: 4 to 6 chicken breasts, cubed, diced to 2 cups
directions: Wrap salad mixture in 2 triangles of roll dough, pinch together.
Bake 20 minutes at 350 degrees
notes: Recipe from: Judy Danuson. Serves: 4.
pdfLink: Lunch Chicken Salad Patties in Crescent Dough.pdf

title: Imperial Chicken Rolls with Parmesan and Lemon Butter Sauce
ingredients: 1 whole chicken, deboned and cut in half
directions: Blend bread crumbs, cheese, parsley, salt, and pepper.
Combine melted butter and garlic.
Dip chicken into butter and then into crumb mixture, coating thoroughly.
Roll each piece into a firm roll, skewer with a toothpick, and arrange in a flat pan.
Squeeze the juice of one lemon over the chicken and drizzle any remaining butter over the chicken.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake 1 hour at 350 degrees.
notes: Susan Dawson
pdfLink: Imperial Chicken Rolls with Parmesan and Lemon Butter Sauce.pdf

title: Pistachio Chicken Breasts with Herb-garlic Cheese Filling
ingredients: 1-2 tablespoons minced fresh basil or 0.5 teaspoon dried
0.5 cup flour combined with 1 teaspoon each salt and pepper
1.5 cups finely ground pistachio nuts (about 7 ounces shelled)
0.25 cup clarified butter (see p. 124 for how to make)
directions: Combine the cream cheese with the garlic, herbs, and seasonings.
Chill until firm and then form into eight 2-inch-long cylinders.
Keep refrigerated until ready to use.
Preheat the oven to 350 degrees.
Gently pound chicken breasts between wax paper until each is 0.25 inch thick.
For each portion, put 1 portion of the filling along 1 edge of a pounded chicken breast and fold and roll the chicken over the filling to completely and securely enclose it.
Repeat with each piece of chicken.

Roll each piece sequentially in the seasoned flour, the beaten eggs, and finally the ground pistachios and sauté in the clarified butter over medium heat for 1-2 minutes on each side or until lightly browned.
Transfer the chicken to a baking pan and put in the preheated oven for 15-20 minutes.
Serve hot.
notes: FROM BETH'S KITCHEN
pdfLink: Pistachio Chicken Breasts with Herb-Garlic Cheese Filling.pdf

title: Chicken a La Maria with Broccoli, Ham, and Parmesan Bread Crumbs
ingredients: 6 whole chicken breasts, split, boned and skirned
1-10 ounce package chopped broccoli, thawed and drained
1-4 ounce package boiled ham slices, diced
directions: Combine bread crumbs and cheese, dip chicken halves in crumb mixture to coat lightly, and arrange in 13x9 pan.
In saucepan, cook onion in butter till tender, blend in soup and milk, stir until bubbly.
Cook 1 minute longer, then add broccoli and ham.
Spoon mixture over chicken and sprinkle with remaining bread crumbs.
Bake uncovered, in 350 degree oven for 45 minutes.
notes: Serves 8-10
pdfLink: Chicken a la Maria with Broccoli, Ham, and Parmesan Bread Crumbs.pdf

title: Baked Chicken Breasts with Swiss Cheese and Sherry
directions: Grease a 2 quart baking dish.
Layer chicken, cheese, soup mixed with wine, and croutons, then dot with butter.
Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 1 hour uncovered.
notes: From: Jeri. Marked with a circled G.
pdfLink: Baked Chicken Breasts with Swiss Cheese and Sherry.pdf

title: Baked Chicken Salad with Potato Chip Crust and Almonds
directions: Grease 2 quart casserole.
Crumb potato chips and set aside.
Put chicken and celery in casserole.
Put Miracle Whip, cheese, lemon, and onion in blender and blend until smooth.
Remove top, add almonds, pour over chicken and celery, and mix.
Sprinkle potato chips on top.
Bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
(Add milk if too thick)
notes: Good. Jerre.
pdfLink: Baked Chicken Salad with Potato Chip Crust and Almonds.pdf

title: Grilled Chicken with Basil Butter
ingredients: 4 chicken breast halves, skinned and deboned
directions: To prepare chicken, mix melted butter, basil, and pepper.
Baste chicken with butter mixture and grill over medium high coals approximately 10 minutes or until done.
As chicken cooks, turn occasionally and baste until all butter is used.
While chicken cooks prepare basil butter.
Blend together all ingredients for basil butter.
Refrigerate for 5 minutes.
Serve chicken topped with cooled basil butter mixture.
Serves 4.
notes: 1995 Shenandoah Growers - Harrisonburg, Virginia

title: Barbeque Chicken Dry Rub Blend by Julia Hodge
directions: Blend all seasoning ingredients together.
Take chicken skin off and wash chicken.
Grease chicken with oil.
Shake on seasoning 2 hours early.
To cook: grill for 30 to 40 minutes, or bake in the oven at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 45 minutes.
notes: Recipe by Julia Hodge. Blend the seasoning mix thoroughly and let the seasoned chicken rest for 2 hours before cooking.
pdfLink: Barbeque Chicken Dry Rub Blend by Julia Hodge.pdf

title: Grilled Huli-huli Chicken with Caramelized Pineapple and Sweet and Sour Rice
directions: Marinate chicken breasts, then grill.
Grill chicken and pineapple on grill.
notes: From the kitchen of Doug Allen
pdfLink: Grilled Huli-Huli Chicken with Caramelized Pineapple and Sweet and Sour Rice.pdf

title: Tarragon Chicken Salad Sandwiches with Crème Fraîche
ingredients: boneless whole chicken breast - about 3 pounds
1 cup crème fraîche or heavy cream
2 loaves Pepperidge Farm white bread (for sandwiches)
directions: Arrange chicken breasts in a single layer in a large jelly roll pan.
Spread evenly with crème fraîche or cream - bake in preheated 350 degree oven for 20 to 25 minutes or until done - cool.
Shred meat into small pieces.
Whisk sour cream and mayonnaise together - pour over chicken mixture.
Add celery, walnuts, tarragon, salt, and pepper - toss well.
Refrigerate covered for at least 4 hours.
Use Pepperidge Farm white bread - spread both sides touching the filling with butter.
Cut diagonally into 4s after removing crust - about 50 triangles.

To make Crème Fraîche: Whisk cream and sour cream together. Cover loosely with plastic wrap and let stand in kitchen or other warm spot overnight or until thickened. In cold weather this may take as long as 24 hours.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 4 hours after which the crème fraîche will be quite thick. The tart flavor will continue to develop as the crème fraîche sits in the refrigerator. Makes 2 cups.
notes: Makes about 50 triangular sandwiches.
pdfLink: Tarragon Chicken Salad Sandwiches with Crème Fraîche.pdf

title: Cheesy Chicken and Asparagus Au Gratin
directions: Mix bread crumbs, cheese and 0.25 cup of butter.
Line 11x7.5 inch baking dish with half the crumb mixture.
Arrange asparagus in dish.
Blend remaining butter, flour, salt and pepper; add milk.
Cook, stirring, until thick; add chicken.
Pour over asparagus; sprinkle with remaining crumb mixture.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes, until crumbs are browned.
May be prepared and frozen, then baked for the 30 minutes.
notes: Yield: 6 servings. From Favorite Recipes of Episcopal Churchwomen - Casseroles Cookbook.

title: Fine Ground Chicken Salad with Celery and Onion
directions: Boil boneless, skinless chicken until very tender, then chill overnight.
Use a food processor to grind the chicken fine.
Grind in the processor celery and onion.
Season with salt and pepper.
Use Wish-Bone Italian salad dressing and mayonnaise until the right consistency.
notes: Recipe by Mary Pinkham.
pdfLink: Fine Ground Chicken Salad with Celery and Onion.pdf

title: Stuffed Chicken Breasts with Wine Sauce
ingredients: 1 1/2 cups drained pineapple, crushed - 1 1/2 ounce can
directions: Cook bacon crisp - add celery and onion.
Sauté until soft. Stir in rice and pineapple.
Flatten chicken breast - skin side down.
Place 1/3 cup stuffing in center - roll and secure with picks. Dip in egg, then cracker crumbs - place in shallow pan - sprinkle with thyme.
Bake 350 degrees - 1 hour.
Serve sauce over chicken when done.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Joan Eisele. Serves 6-8.
pdfLink: Stuffed Chicken Breasts with Wine Sauce.pdf

title: Baked Chicken Breasts with Crab Cream Sauce
directions: Make sauce, then add crab and egg.
Line casserole with foil. Then skin chicken breast and place in foil.
Pour sauce over and cover.
Bake in 350 degrees for 1 and 1/2 hours or until done.
notes: Sauce may be used over rice.

title: Hearty Curried Chicken with Tomatoes and Raisins
directions: Put all in large pan and cover and simmer - about 40 minutes.
notes: This is enough for 1 to 2 chickens or 8 chicken breasts.

title: Chicken and Broccoli Casserole with Sour Cream
ingredients: 6 to 8 chicken breasts cooked and cubed
directions: Mix all ingredients together.
Bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Sprinkle with slivered almonds.

title: Wild Rice and Chicken Casserole with Sausage and Mushrooms
ingredients: 2 pounds fresh mushrooms, sliced and sautéed in butter
directions: Brown sausage, cook wild rice 20 minutes and drain.
Mix sausage, soup, mushrooms and rice together.
Add salt and pepper to taste.
Layer of rice and layer of chicken.
End with layer of rice.
Top with buttered bread crumbs.
Bake 45 minutes or longer at 375 degrees.
Serves 12.

title: Warm Spiced Fruit Casserole with Curry and Brown Sugar
ingredients: 2 cans fruit (pineapple, peaches, pears and 1 orange sliced)
1/3 cup melted butter and 1/2 cup brown sugar
directions: Drain fruit well.
Mix butter and sugar.
Pour over fruit and let stand 2 hours.
Bake 1/2 hour at 375 oven.
pdfLink: Warm Spiced Fruit Casserole with Curry and Brown Sugar.pdf

title: Classic Chicken Almond Stir Fry with Assorted Vegetables
ingredients: 2 packages chicken breast - slice very thin and long (raw)
3 cups chicken stock (or Spice Island chicken stock)
1 1/2 cups chopped fresh tomatoes (skin and seedy pulp removed)
2 cups edible snow peas (cut into 1-inch pieces or leave whole)
1 cup almonds - blanched - split into 2 and fry in deep fat or butter until golden brown
directions: Preheat cooking utensil and add 5 tablespoons salad oil, let it sizzle a bit and then add raw sliced chicken breast.
Cook 2 minutes, stirring often, and add 3 cups chicken broth, which should be boiling hot.
Add vegetables, 2 tablespoons soy sauce, and 1 tablespoon MSG. Mix thoroughly.
Cover and cook 8 minutes.
Stir in cornstarch and water and cook another minute or two, stirring gently as the mixture thickens.
Taste for seasoning and add a little salt if needed.
Transfer to serving dish and sprinkle with almonds.
Serves 8-10 with other dishes.
notes: Marked as "Very Good" (Harriet Doddaige, 1963, Ft. Bliss). Make day before - may be frozen.
pdfLink: Classic Chicken Almond Stir Fry with Assorted Vegetables.pdf

title: Holiday Buffet Chicken and Ham Casserole
ingredients: 1/4 pound Smithfield or country ham, sliced thin
1 10 1/2 ounce can cream of mushroom soup
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Line the bottom of a 9 x 13 baking dish with ham; position chicken breasts over ham.
Combine soup, half and half and pepper; pour over chicken.
Top with cheese.
Cover with aluminum foil and bake 1 1/2 hours.
Remove from oven and allow to cool slightly before serving.
Sauce thickens as the dish cools.
Serve with a rice casserole or rice.
Serves 6-10 depending on the size of the chicken breasts.
notes: Note: If country ham is used, do not add salt. This dish can be prepared ahead of time and baked when ready. Be sure to have dish at room temperature before baking. "The sauce is sensational!"

title: Crispy Chicken Cutlets with Mozzarella and Spaghetti
ingredients: 1 jar (15 1/2 ounces) marinara sauce (use more sauce)
directions: Dip cutlets in egg, then in bread crumbs.
Heat butter in skillet and sauté cutlets until golden.
Pour half the sauce into 13x9x2-inch baking pan, add cutlets and top with remaining sauce.
Bake in preheated 350° oven 15 to 20 minutes or until hot and bubbly.
Sprinkle with cheese and bake a few minutes longer to melt.
Serve with spaghetti.
notes: Susan Dawson
pdfLink: Crispy Chicken Cutlets with Mozzarella and Spaghetti.pdf

title: Baked Chicken with Brie and Vegetables
ingredients: 1 large triangular wedge of brie, cut in chunks (do not remove rind)
herbs of Provence (combination of rosemary, thyme, marjoram, oregano, and basil)
6 medium carrots, peeled and cut into 2-inch pieces
6 small to medium zucchini, cut into 2-inch pieces
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees Fahrenheit. Remove giblets and neck from cavity if necessary.
Rinse chicken in cold water and pat dry. Stuff hen with celery, peeled onion and brie; place in an oven-to-table roasting pan that has been lightly sprayed with cooking oil.
Rub hen with olive oil and pat all over with herbs.
Place the vegetables around the hen in the roasting pan: cover with heavy-duty aluminum foil, and bake for 2 1/2 hours.
Remove foil and bake an additional 30 minutes. Serve immediately. Serves 6-8 depending on appetites of guests and remaining menu.
notes: Easy to prepare and forget until time to serve! Serving Note: Leave chicken in roasting dish to carve; surround each portion of chicken with vegetables and spoon melted brie over chicken or vegetables.
pdfLink: Baked Chicken with Brie and Vegetables.pdf

title: Crockpot Chicken with Mushroom Sauce
directions: Dip chicken into melted butter.
Place in crockpot and sprinkle dry dressing mix over breasts.
Cook on low setting for 6 hours.
Combine soup, wine, and cream cheese in saucepan and heat until smooth and heated through.
Add sautéed mushrooms and pour all over chicken in pot.
Cook 30 minutes or more until ready to serve over rice or noodles.
Makes enough sauce for 6 chicken breasts.
notes: From the kitchen of Patty Jellison. Serves 6.

title: Nancy Dawson's Chicken Divan with Stuffing
ingredients: 1 package Pepperidge Farm stuffing mixed with 1/2 cup melted butter
directions: Chopped broccoli in lasagna size casserole - top with cooked chicken - cut up.
Mix remaining (not stuffing). Pour about 1/2 over chicken - then add stuffing and cover with remaining sauce.
Save a little of stuffing for top!!
Bake 350 degrees for 20-30 minutes.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Makes 6 servings.
pdfLink: Nancy Dawson's Chicken Divan with Stuffing.pdf

title: Classic Herb-stuffed Chicken Kiev with Creamy Mushroom Sauce
ingredients: 6 whole chicken breasts, boned and skinned
1 package (8 ounces) fine noodles, cooked and drained
directions: Prepare chicken: Mix softened butter, parsley, chives, shallots or onions, salt, and pepper. Shape into 6 sticks. Chill.
Slice 1 chicken breast between 2 pieces of wax paper. Pound it slightly with a mallet.
Place 1 stick of herbed butter on each breast. Roll breast so butter is completely enclosed. Close edges with wooden picks.
Sprinkle lightly with salt and pepper.
Heat oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Beat egg and water in pan. Dredge breast in flour, dip in egg mixture, and roll in crumbs to coat well.
Heat butter in a skillet over medium heat. Sauté breast until golden on all sides, turning gently with 2 forks.
Put chicken in a shallow baking pan. Bake 15 to 20 minutes or until tender.
Prepare Mushroom Sauce: Melt butter, add onion, cook 2 minutes. Add mushrooms, cook 5 minutes or until tender. Remove from heat.
Sprinkle with lemon juice, salt, and pepper. Stir in sour cream.
Mix half of sauce with noodles. Place chicken on noodles and serve remaining sauce.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Nancy Hodge.
pdfLink: Classic Herb-Stuffed Chicken Kiev with Creamy Mushroom Sauce.pdf

title: Honey Pecan Chicken Breasts
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees. Rinse chicken and pat dry.
Combine salt and next 5 ingredients; mix well. Brush on each side of chicken breasts and set aside.
Combine cornflake crumbs and pecans in a flat dish. Dip each breast in pecan mixture and place in a lightly sprayed shallow baking pan.
Spray tops of each breast lightly, with cooking spray, and bake for 18-25 minutes depending on size and thickness of breasts.
Serves 6-8.
notes: Serve with brown rice and steamed spinach!

title: Williams-sonoma Lemon-thyme Roasted Chicken
ingredients: 1 chicken, 6 to 7 pounds (3 to 3.5kg), giblets and neck removed from cavity
Kosher salt and freshly ground pepper, to taste
2 tablespoons unsalted butter, at room temperature
2 carrots, peeled and cut into 1/2-inch (12mm) pieces
1 1/2 cups (375ml) reduced-sodium chicken stock, plus more if needed
directions: About 30 minutes before roasting, remove the chicken from the refrigerator. Preheat an oven to 450°F (230°C). Oil a V-shaped roasting rack and place it in a roasting pan. Remove and discard any pockets of fat from the chicken cavity. Rinse the chicken and pat dry with paper towels. With the chicken placed breast side up and starting at the neck cavity, slip your fingers under the skin and gently separate the skin from the breast meat on both sides, being careful not to tear the skin. Carefully slide 4 or 5 lemon slices and half of the thyme sprigs under the skin, spacing them evenly. Season the cavity with salt and pepper, and place the remaining lemon slices and thyme in the cavity. Tuck the wing tips under the back. Tie the legs together with kitchen string. Rub the chicken all over with the butter. Place the chicken, breast side up, on the rack.

Roast the chicken for 30 minutes. Reduce the oven temperature to 325°F (165°C). Add the carrots, celery, onion and the 1 1/2 cups (375ml) stock to the pan. Continue to roast until an instant-read thermometer inserted into the thickest part of a thigh, away from the bone, registers 170° to 175°F (77° to 80°C), 1 to 1 1/2 hours more. Remove from the oven. Slip a pair of tongs in the chicken cavity and carefully tip the bird, draining the liquid from the cavity into the pan. Transfer the chicken to a carving board and tent with aluminum foil. Let rest for 15 to 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, scrape up any browned bits from the pan bottom and pour the contents of the pan through a medium-mesh sieve into a large measuring pitcher. Using a spoon, press on the contents of the sieve to extract as much liquid as possible. Skim off and reserve 3 tablespoons fat, discarding the remainder. Add stock if needed to the pitcher to total 2 cups (500ml). In a saucepan over medium heat, warm the reserved fat. Add the flour and cook, stirring, until well blended, 2 to 3 minutes. Slowly stir in the 2 cups liquid. Add any juices from the carving board. Cook, stirring constantly, until the gravy is smooth and thickens slightly, 3 to 4 minutes. Season generously with salt and pepper. Carve the chicken. Pour the gravy into a warmed bowl and pass at the table. Serves 8.
notes:
Adapted from Williams-Sonoma Essentials of Roasting, by Rick Rodgers (Oxmoor House, 2004).
© Williams-Sonoma, Inc., 2005

title: Grilled Chicken with Honeydew Salsa
ingredients: 1/2 honeydew melon, peeled and seeded and cut into quarter-inch cubes
1/2 - 1 jalapeno chile pepper, seeded and diced (see note)
6 boneless, skinless chicken breasts, flattened slightly
directions: Rub flattened breasts with oil, salt and pepper; grill over a medium hot fire for 3-5 minutes per side depending on thickness of chicken and heat of grill.
Combine all salsa ingredients and chill 30 minutes before grilling chicken. Spoon salsa over warm chicken.
Serves 6.
notes: Use kitchen gloves when handling jalapenos. Adjust amount of spices and peppers to personal taste. A nice little kick in the salsa adds to the grilled chicken! A great combination of summer flavors!

title: Szechwan Chicken with Peanuts and Green Onions
directions: Remove skin and bones from chicken breasts; save for later use or discard. Cut breasts into square pieces about 3/4 to 1 inch.

Beat egg white with 1 tablespoon cornstarch, 1 tablespoon light soy sauce, and sherry until mixture is frothy. Marinate chicken in this mixture for at least 30 minutes, turning occasionally so that chicken is well coated.
In a small bowl, combine salt, monosodium glutamate, sugar, mashed garlic, vinegar, molasses, water, remaining cornstarch, and remaining soy sauce.
Blend until perfectly smooth, then add green onions.
Heat oil in skillet, stir fry chicken in hot oil until each piece turns white. Remove to absorbent paper and keep warm.
Discard oil and wipe skillet with paper towel.
Heat sesame oil over medium heat. Add dried red peppers and cook until they turn black.
Add chicken, peanuts, and vinegar-molasses-onion mixture. Mix well and cook for 2-3 minutes.
notes: Serves 4-6. Marked as "Very Good".
pdfLink: Szechwan Chicken with Peanuts and Green Onions.pdf

title: Overnight Savory Chicken Strata Casserole
ingredients: 12 slices bread, toasted and lightly buttered on both sides
1 10-1/2 ounce can cream of chicken soup
directions: Lightly butter a 9 x 13 glass baking dish.
Place 6 slices of bread on the bottom; top with celery, onion and chicken.
Place remaining bread on top.
Combine eggs, Miracle Whip, milk and salt; pour over bread.
Cover with plastic wrap and allow to sit in refrigerator overnight.
When ready to bake, spread soup over top and cover with cheese.
Preheat oven to 325 and bake uncovered for 1 hour.
Serves 8-10.
notes: Serve with a green vegetable, salad or aspic. "Perfect for a crowd since it has to be fixed ahead!"

title: Garlic Lemon Chicken on the Grill
ingredients: 1/2 cup extra virgin olive oil, divided
directions: Chicken: Place breasts in storage bag; squeeze lemons over chicken and place lemon pieces in bag with chicken. Add 1/4 cup olive oil, garlic, salt and pepper to bag; close bag and place in refrigerator to marinate for a minimum of 8 hours or overnight.

To Grill: Remove chicken from bag; discard bag and contents. Place chicken over hot fire and sear both sides quickly; reduce heat and cook over a medium fire for 8 - 10 minutes depending on size and thickness of breasts. Brush with remaining virgin olive oil twice while grilling. Do not overcook.
To Serve: Arrange on serving plate; garnish with sliced lemon and fresh rosemary sprigs. Serves 6 - 8 depending on rest of menu.
notes:
Serve with one of the many new gourmet mustards as an optional sauce. Key lime or a whole grain mustard would be delicious
The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: St. Louis Grilled Cornish Game Hens with Zesty Vinegar Sauce
ingredients: 4 Cornish game hens, split for grilling
directions: Preheat grill. Rub Cornish hens with salt, pepper and oil.
Combine all sauce ingredients and mix well.
Place hens, skin side down on grill and brush frequently with sauce. Cook, uncovered 10-12 minutes over medium heat.
Turn and repeat process; cook second side for 10-12 minutes or until fork tender.
Serves 4-8 depending on rest of the menu and appetites of guests.
notes: "Serve with leafy green salad tossed with mandarin oranges and diced red onions in a citrus vinaigrette!"
pdfLink: St. Louis Grilled Cornish Game Hens with Zesty Vinegar Sauce.pdf

title: John's Barbecue Chicken with Mesquite and Lemon Pepper
directions: Sprinkle seasoning on both sides of chicken.
Then use KC Masterpiece barbecue sauce.
Pour over chicken and let sit in refrigerator for about 1 hour.
notes: Best if cooked on grill.
pdfLink: John's Barbecue Chicken with Mesquite and Lemon Pepper.pdf

title: Jerri's Baked Chicken and Minute Rice Casserole
directions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees Fahrenheit.
Grease a 9x13 inch baking pan.
Sprinkle 2 cups minute rice on the bottom of the pan.
Warm 1 can cream of mushroom soup and 1 can cream of celery soup with 0.5 cup milk and mix.
Pour over rice.
Place chicken pieces over mixture.
Sprinkle 1 package dry onion soup mix over chicken.
Cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 2.5 hours.
pdfLink: Jerri's Baked Chicken and Minute Rice Casserole.pdf

title: Chicken, Broccoli, and Cauliflower Casserole
directions: Bake chicken at 350 degrees for 1 hour. While cooling, steam broccoli and cauliflower.
Debone chicken and cut into bite-size pieces.
Mix with soup, mayonnaise, broccoli, and cauliflower. Add curry powder, salt, and pepper to taste.
Top with cheese slices.
Bake at 300 degrees for 45 minutes.
Add fresh squeezed lemon to taste.
notes: Donna Dawson, serves 4-6

title: Rich Brown Turkey Giblet Gravy
directions: Combine giblets, neck pieces, onions, carrots, celery, and 1/2 cup water, and 1/2 cup broth. Bring to a boil uncovered and stir often.
Cook until giblets and vegetables are browned and browned bits stick to pan, 15 to 20 minutes.
Add remaining ingredients.
Simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours.
Strain - use broth for gravy.

title: Thanksgiving Herb and Mustard Roasted Turkey
directions: Blend Dijon mustard, soy sauce, and olive oil using wire whisk.
Add juice of lemons.
Mix in fresh herbs.
Add garlic using garlic press.
Rub turkey with marinade.
Sprinkle with pepper and salt.
Bake at 350 degrees for 15-20 minutes per pound.
After 1.5 hours, remove foil and baste every 15 minutes until done.
notes: Thanksgiving Feast from the kitchen of Patty Jellison.
pdfLink: Thanksgiving Herb and Mustard Roasted Turkey.pdf

title: Nancy Dawson's Roasted Chicken with Orange, Rosemary, and Dijon Glaze
ingredients: 3 tablespoons Grand Marnier or orange liqueur
directions: Preheat oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Rinse chicken.
Squeeze the juice of orange over the bird.
Place orange and onion inside.
Tie legs together.
Sprinkle salt and pepper all over and rosemary.
Pour water into pan.
Roast for 20 minutes.
Reduce to 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 1 hour.
Heat glaze until smooth, then add Grand Marnier.
Spoon over chicken.
Continue to roast.
May add potatoes, carrots, and onions to pan.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Makes 4 to 6 servings.
pdfLink: Nancy Dawson's Roasted Chicken with Orange, Rosemary, and Dijon Glaze.pdf

title: Nigerian Chicken with Spiced Tomato Vegetable Gravy Over Rice
directions: Fries-flour and brown chicken lightly. Cover skillet with 1/2 inch cooking oil. Remove chicken.
To oil add: 2 medium chopped onions, 1/2 or 3/4 cup diced green pepper, 1 cup grated carrot, quarter 3 or 4 small tomatoes. Cook these until slightly tender.
Put chicken back into pan with vegetables and add 1 cup water.
Cover and cook for about 1 hour. You'll need to add water occasionally. When this is finished you will have a gravy out of the vegetables (keep enough water in it to make a small bowl of gravy).
Serve over rice.
Salt and pepper as preferred.
pdfLink: Nigerian Chicken with Spiced Tomato Vegetable Gravy over Rice.pdf

title: Classic Chicken Chow Mein with Mushrooms and Almonds
ingredients: 1/2 cup sliced mushrooms, fresh or canned
2 green peppers or 1 1/2 cups diced green peppers
3 to 4 cups chicken cut in pieces
directions: Put all in sauce pan and cook until limp: mushrooms, butter, green peppers, and sliced onions.
Cook celery in 1 quart chicken stock.
Add chicken cut in pieces.
Put in broth and add 4 teaspoons soy sauce.
Stir in 1/3 cup cornstarch mixed in 2 tablespoons water to thicken.
Add 1/4 cup toasted almonds.
Serve over Chinese noodles.
May add sliced water chestnuts.
pdfLink: Classic Chicken Chow Mein with Mushrooms and Almonds.pdf

title: Cambridge Chicken with Ham and Red Wine
ingredients: flour mixed with salt and pepper
directions: Shake chicken in paper bag with flour.
Brown chicken in butter and place in casserole.
Mix remaining ingredients and pour over chicken.
Bake, covered in 350 degree oven for 1 hour.
Remove and cool a short time before placing in refrigerator overnight.
The next day, when ready to bake, again spoon the liquid over the chicken and place, covered, in a 300 degree oven for 1 hour.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of: Jerri. Serves: 4.
pdfLink: Cambridge Chicken with Ham and Red Wine.pdf

title: Classic Chicken Hash “21” with Wild Rice and Mornay Sauce
ingredients: Additional grated Parmesan cheese for topping
directions: Poach a 2.5 pound chicken in chicken broth for 1 hour or until tender.
Remove chicken from broth, let cool, cut meat from bones, dice it, and reserve it.
In a saucepan, cook 1 cup wild rice in 4 cups boiling water, stirring frequently for 20 minutes, or until tender, and drain it.
In a skillet, sauté the rice briefly in 2 tablespoons butter, blend in 0.5 cup sherry and salt and pepper to taste. Keep rice warm.
In a skillet, melt 0.5 stick or 0.25 cup butter, blend 2 tablespoons flour and stir slowly in 2 cups scalded milk.
Cook the sauce until it is smooth and thick, simmer gently for 10 to 15 minutes, add 0.5 cup light cream, salt and pepper to taste, stir in chicken. Keep creamed chicken warm.
Prepare a Mornay sauce: In a skillet, melt 0.5 stick or 0.25 cup butter, blend in 2 tablespoons flour, slowly stir in 2 cups scalded milk. Cook sauce until smooth and thickened.
Add a little sauce to 3 egg yolks, beaten, blend mixture thoroughly, stir it into rest of sauce. Do not let it boil.
Let sauce cool, add 2 tablespoons whipped cream, 0.5 cup grated Parmesan cheese and salt and pepper to taste. Cook sauce until cheese melts and sauce is blended and thickened.
In a shallow flameproof serving dish, arrange a border of wild rice and keep the creamed chicken in center.
Pour Mornay sauce over the chicken and rice, sprinkle top with grated Parmesan cheese, place under broiler for a few minutes to brown top.
Serves 4 to 6.
notes: Marked as "Very Good"
pdfLink: Classic Chicken Hash “21” with Wild Rice and Mornay Sauce.pdf

title: Baked Monterey Jack and Green Chile Stuffed Chicken Breasts with Homemade Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 8 large whole chicken breasts, skinned and boned
1 can (7 ounces) chopped mild green chilies
0.5 pound Monterey Jack cheese, cut into 8 strips
Optional: hot pepper sauce to taste
directions: Pound chicken breasts between 2 sheets of waxed paper until thin.
Spread each breast with 1 tablespoon of green chilies. Place one cheese strip on top of each portion of chili.
Roll up each chicken breast and tuck ends under.
Combine bread crumbs, Parmesan cheese, chili powder, salt, cumin, and pepper in a shallow dish.
Dip each stuffed breast into the melted butter and roll in the bread crumb mixture.
Place breast in a baking dish, seam side down. Drizzle with remaining butter.
Cover and chill 4 hours or overnight.
Preheat oven to 400 degrees Fahrenheit.
Bake for 25 to 40 minutes, or until done.
Serve with the tomato sauce and garnish with sour cream and fresh limes.
In small saucepan combine tomato sauce, cumin, green onion, salt, pepper, and hot pepper sauce, if desired.
Bring to a boil and cook, stir constantly, until thickened.
notes: Laura Gough 11/88
pdfLink: Baked Monterey Jack and Green Chile Stuffed Chicken Breasts with Homemade Tomato Sauce.pdf

title: Creamy Chicken Oriental with Mushrooms and Water Chestnuts
directions: Coat chicken with flour, 1 teaspoon salt, and a dash of pepper.
In a 5-quart dutch oven, brown 4 chicken pieces at a time in hot oil.
Remove to platter.
Cook onion, celery, and garlic until tender.
Blend soup, sherry, and soy sauce.
Drain mushrooms and chestnuts (thinly slice).
Combine with soup and add to cooked vegetables and bring to boil.
Place chicken in sauce, cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Add pea pods, cover and simmer until chicken is done (10 to 15 minutes).
Spoon sauce over chicken and pass remainder.
Serves 12
notes: Over -
pdfLink: Creamy Chicken Oriental with Mushrooms and Water Chestnuts.pdf

title: Sour Cream Marinated Baked Chicken
directions: Make a mixture of all ingredients except chicken, bread crumbs and margarine.
Marinate chicken in the mixture overnight.
Turn once or twice while marinating.
When ready to bake, preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Roll chicken in bread crumbs and bake in an 8-inch square glass baking dish in which the margarine has been melted.
Bake 1 hour uncovered.
Do not turn while baking.
Remove from oven and drain on a heavy brown bag.
Serves 4-6.
notes: This recipe can easily be doubled and baked in a 9 x 13 pan. Bake the same length of time. "A nice dish for entertaining since the work is done the day before!"

title: Baked Chicken Breasts on a Mushroom Bed with Port Wine Cream Sauce
ingredients: 3/4 cup chicken stock or canned chicken broth
salt and freshly ground black pepper to taste
3 boneless chicken breasts, skinned and halved
directions: Melt butter in skillet. Add shallots and sauté gently for 5 minutes without browning.
Add sliced mushrooms to skillet, season with salt and pepper, sauté over medium heat, stirring occasionally, for 10 minutes.
Preheat oven to 325 degrees Fahrenheit.
Add chicken broth, Port, and heavy cream to skillet with mushrooms and simmer for another 5 minutes, or until slightly thickened.
Spoon mushroom mixture into shallow baking dish.
Arrange chicken breast halves in single layer on top of mushrooms.
Season with salt and pepper and cover tightly with foil.
Bake for 20 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley.
notes: Laura Hodge 6-17-85
pdfLink: Baked Chicken Breasts on a Mushroom Bed with Port Wine Cream Sauce.pdf

title: Crispy Sesame Chicken with Fresh Citrus Sauce
ingredients: 1/2 cup red currant jelly or currant jelly
directions: Remove skin from chicken and place each breast between 2 sheets of waxed paper.
Use a wooden mallet to pound to 1/4-inch thickness.
Combine next 5 ingredients to make cornflake mixture.
Dip each breast into melted butter or margarine and then into cornflake mixture.
Place chicken on lightly greased baking sheet; bake uncovered in a preheated 425-degree oven for 20 minutes.
Transfer to serving plate and garnish with sliced fruit. Top each serving with sauce. Serves 4-6.
SAUCE: Heat first 6 ingredients until warm; set aside.
Melt butter and add cornstarch; stir to blend.
Gradually add warm fruit juice mixture and cook on low heat until thickened; stir constantly.
notes: Serve with a baked rice casserole and buttered broccoli! The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
pdfLink: Crispy Sesame Chicken with Fresh Citrus Sauce.pdf

title: Pat's Artichoke Chicken Casserole
ingredients: 1-16 ounce can artichoke hearts, drained and chopped
1-2 ounce jar pimientos (chopped) or 1/2 cup sliced green olives
directions: Saute chicken in oil.
Add mushrooms and artichokes, cook briefly.
Arrange in a 9"x13" buttered baking dish.
Add water chestnuts and pimientos or olives.
Combine remaining ingredients to make a sauce; pour over casserole.
Bake uncovered at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.
Serve over rice or noodles.
notes: Serves 6. Recipe from Jeri.

title: Irish Lamb Stew
ingredients: 2-3 pound lamb shoulder, cut into 1-1 1/2 inch cubes (Yields approximately 1 1/2 pounds of lamb cubes. Save meaty bones.)
6 medium white onions, quartered or 18 small whole white onions, peeled
4-5 carrots, peeled and cut into eighths
6-8 medium red-skinned potatoes, unpared and quartered
directions: Trim ALL fat from lamb.
Melt 2 tablespoons butter in a Dutch oven; add meat and brown.
Sprinkle flour over lamb; add water, salt, pepper and meaty lamb bones.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce heat and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Discard meat bones.
Sauté garlic, onions, turnips and carrots in 2 tablespoons butter until light golden.
Add vegetables and potatoes to lamb; cook uncovered for 20 minutes.
Add Kitchen Bouquet, peas and Krazy Salt.
Cook 10-15 minutes or until potatoes are tender.
Serve with cracked pepper, parsley and bacon.
Serves 4-6.
notes: Note: Do not stir more than necessary; overstirring breaks up vegetables! 'Serve hot with crusty bread for a hearty and delicious main dish!' The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Veal Chops with Belgian Endive
ingredients: 4 loin veal chops, about 1/2 pound each
4 firm-white, unblemished heads of Belgian endive
directions: Salt and pepper chops. Dredge in flour.
Heat 3 tablespoons butter in heavy skillet.
Cook chops over medium heat 8 to 10 minutes and turn. Cook uncovered 15 minutes longer.
Cook endives in heavy saucepan with 1 tablespoon butter, salt, and pepper. Cover, simmer 25 minutes.
When chops done, place on platter and cover with foil.
Add shallots to skillet and cook.
Add cognac and flame it. Stir with wooden spoon to dissolve brown particles that cling to the bottom and sides.
Add cream and cook, stirring over high heat. Cook 5 minutes until thick.
Strain and add salt and pepper.
Preheat oven 400 degrees.
Chops in baking dish. Press endive gently to remove water. Arrange around chops. Spoon sauce over all and sprinkle with cheese.
Bake 15 minutes.
notes: 4 servings

title: Veal Scallopini with Lemon and Parsley
ingredients: 1 pound veal scallopini, thinly sliced and pounded to 1/4-inch thickness
directions: Preheat oven to 200 degrees; place an ovenproof platter in oven for later use.
Heat oil and butter or margarine in a heavy-bottom large skillet, uncovered over medium-high heat.
Place flour, salt and pepper on flat plate.
When oil is hot, quickly dip veal pieces in flour and shake off excess flour.
Sauté as many pieces as fit comfortably in a single layer.
Cook 2 minutes per side; remove from pan and place on heated platter and keep warm.
Continue cooking remaining veal.
When all veal has been cooked, deglaze skillet with lemon juice and spoon over veal.
Garnish with sliced lemon and parsley.
Serves 6.
notes: Quick and elegant! ...from our collection of family favorites. Serve with fettuccine and steamed broccoli. The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
pdfLink: Veal Scallopini with Lemon and Parsley.pdf

title: Veal with Sour Cream and Wine Sauce Healy
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boned shoulder of veal, cut into 1 inch cubes
directions: In a heavy skillet, sauté medium onion, diced, in 1/2 stick or 1/4 cup butter until it is soft.
Add 1 1/2 pounds boned shoulder of veal, cut into 1 inch cubes, and brown the veal on all sides.
Add 1 cup white wine, the juice of 1 garlic clove, 1 tablespoon dried basil, 1 teaspoon salt, and simmer the mixture gently, covered, for 15 minutes, or until the veal is tender.
Add 1 cup sour cream, 1/3 cup evaporated milk, and 1/4 cup grated Cheddar cheese and cook the mixture slowly, stirring, until the sauce is blended and thickened.
Add salt and pepper to taste and serve the veal and sauce over rice.
notes: Serves 4.
pdfLink: Veal with Sour Cream and Wine Sauce Healy.pdf

title: Grandmother's Veal Stew
ingredients: 3 pounds veal roast, cut into 2-inch cubes
8 ounces canned tomatoes, undrained and mashed
directions: Combine flour, salt and pepper; dust veal cubes in flour. Reserve remaining flour.
Heat oil in Dutch oven; add meat and brown on all sides. (Brown half of the meat at a time.)
Add next 8 ingredients and bring to boil. Cover and reduce heat.
Cook on low for 2 hours. Add lemon peel during last 10 minutes of cooking.
Remove veal and place in serving dish; skim fat from cooking broth.
Blend 1/2 cup broth with reserved flour; gradually stir into cooking broth.
Cook on medium high heat for 6-7 minutes; stir occasionally.
Pour over meat. Serves 6 over cooked noodles. Garnish with parsley.
notes:
Note: Can be prepared one day ahead!
"Easy to prepare and so good!"
The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Weiner Schnitzel
ingredients: 1 pound veal steak or veal cutlet (approximately 1/2-inch thick)
directions: Cut the veal into serving pieces; pound very lightly with a wooden mallet to flatten slightly.
Place veal in a flat dish, cover with milk and marinate for one hour at room temperature.
Drain milk and reserve.
Season flour with salt, pepper and garlic powder; place in flat dish.
Combine egg and 4 tablespoons reserved milk.
Dip veal into flour, then egg mixture, and then bread crumbs.
Fry in vegetable oil until golden brown or approximately 5 minutes per side (Do not have the heat too high!).
Drain well on paper towels.
Serve with lemon slices and parsley.
Serves 3-4.
notes:
Note: Do not omit lemon! Squeeze a little over each serving! Can be prepared early in the day and refrigerated until ready to cook.
"Easy and sensational!

title: Marinated Lamb Kabobs
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds lean boneless lamb, cut into 1 1/2-inch cubes
1/2 cup reduced calorie Caesar salad dressing
directions: Place lamb in a shallow dish; combine remaining ingredients, and pour over lamb.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Remove meat from marinade; thread onto skewers.
Broil 7 to 8 inches from heat for 18 to 20 minutes, turning a quarter turn every 4 to 5 minutes.
Baste with marinade while cooking.
Discard remaining marinade.
Yield: 4 servings.
notes: Note: Serve with fresh parslied potatoes and spring peas. Garnish with fresh mint or mint jelly. The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Medallions of Pork with Pear Sauce
ingredients: 2 pears, peeled, cored, thinly sliced (about 1 pound)
directions: Heat oil in heavy large skillet over medium heat. Season pork with dried sage, salt and pepper. Coat pork with flour; shake off excess. Add pork to skillet and sauté until brown, about 3 minutes per side. Transfer to plate.

Drain fat from skillet. Add pears and sauté over medium heat 2 minutes. Stir in wine, sugar and ginger, scraping up any browned bits. Increase heat to high and boil until pears are tender and syrup is thick, about 5 minutes. Return pork and any accumulated juices to skillet. Simmer just until cooked through, about 1 minute. Season to taste with salt and pepper. Arrange pork on plates. Spoon sauce over and serve.
4 servings; can be doubled
notes: Ready in under fifteen minutes, pork chops are transformed by this simple yet sensational sauce into an entrée good enough for company. Add sautéed cabbage and roasted potatoes to complete the meal. Finish with old-fashioned Chocolate Pudding. Marked as "Very Good"
pdfLink: Medallions of Pork with Pear Sauce.pdf

title: English Country Pork Chops
ingredients: 6 center-cut boneless pork chops (approximately 3/4 - 1 inch thick)
1/4 cup cranberry chutney or mango chutney
1-1 1/2 teaspoons hot and sweet mustard or Dijon mustard
directions: Mix chutney and mustard in small bowl; set aside until ready to use.
Spray a heavy, covered skillet that is just large enough to hold chops in a single layer.
Season chops with salt and pepper; place in heated pan and quickly brown on both sides.
Reduce heat to medium low and spoon sauce over chops; cover and cook 18 - 22 minutes or until fork tender.
Place chops on serving plate and set aside.
Add vinegar to skillet and bring to boil; stir sauce and spoon over chops.
Garnish with sprigs of watercress or sprigs of fresh sage.
Serves 4 - 6.
notes: Marked as "Very Good". ...from our quick & easy collection. "Serve with savory long grain and wild rice and creamed spinach."

title: Sweet and Sour Pork
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds lean pork, cut into 1-inch cubes
2/3 cup pineapple chunks, fresh or canned
4 cups steamed vegetables (use red, green and yellow peppers, zucchini or yellow squash)
directions: Place pork and next 4 ingredients in a medium covered sauce pan. Bring to a boil; reduce heat to low and cook 45-50 minutes or until pork is tender. Strain broth and reserve.

Sauce: Place all sauce ingredients, except pineapple chunks and water, in saucepan. Heat over medium heat; bring to a boil and slowly add reserved pork cooking broth. Stir constantly until thickened and smooth. Add pineapple chunks and water.
To serve: Add pork to sauce and heat well. Arrange rice and veggies on plates; top with pork and sauce. Garnish with green onions. Serves 6.
notes: Marked as "Very Good", from our collection of family favorites, Words Worth Eating, The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Saucy Baked Pork Chops
directions: Trim fat from chops and heat fat in skillet (2 tablespoons fat - remove trimmings).
Brown chops in fat - season with salt and pepper.
Drain off fat.
Combine remaining ingredients - pour over chops.
Cover; bake in moderate oven 350 degrees 45 - 60 minutes or till chops are done.
notes: 6 servings

title: Polynesian Pork Chops
directions: Trim fat from chops. Heat fat in skillet to have 2 tablespoons melted fat, remove trimmings.
Brown chops in fat, season with salt and pepper. Pour off fat.
Peel and section oranges, reserving any juice.
Add water to juice to measure 1/2 cup, add to chops with onion and soy sauce.
Cover and simmer 30 minutes.
Add celery and simmer 5 minutes.
Remove chops.
Blend cornstarch and water, stir into sauce. Cook and stir till mixture thickens.
Return chops to skillet, top with orange sections. Cover, simmer until hot.
Serve on rice.
notes: 6 servings

title: Peppered Rack of Pork
ingredients: 3-4 pound Pork Rib Roast, with at least 6 ribs, chine bone cracked
directions: Heat oven to 375 degrees.
Trim rib bones down 1-1 1/2 inches and between each one so that they stick out and are clean of meat. (This is known as Frenching).
Coat roast on all surfaces with peppered seasoning.
Place roast, bones up, in shallow roasting pan.
Roast for 1-1 1/2 hours, until internal temperature reaches 150-155 degrees with a meat thermometer.
Remove roast from oven; let rest until temperature reaches 160 degrees, about 10 minutes.
Cut between rib bones to serve.
notes: Great alternative for Holiday Turkey! Serve with Duchess Potatoes and Green Beans and Almonds from Ukrop's Kitchen. Recipe from the National Pork Producers Council and National Pork Board.

title: Baked Pork Chops with Potatoes and Onions
directions: Heat oven to 350 degrees.
Trim fat from chops and roll in flour.
Brown chops and garlic in fat over medium heat.
Season with salt and pepper.
Place potatoes in baking dish, top and brown chops.
Separate onion slices into rings and lay over chops.
Blend sour cream, salt, and mustard; pour over casserole.
Bake 1 1/2 hours.
Servings 4
pdfLink: Baked Pork Chops with Potatoes and Onions.pdf

title: Stuffed Pork Chops
directions: Toss first 4 ingredients together, add rest.
Bake at 350 degrees for 1 1/2 hours.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Jackie Strong, Serves 6

title: 2-4-6-8 Pork Chops with Minute Rice
ingredients: Minute rice (1/4 cup for 2 chops, 1/2 cup for 4 chops, etc.)
directions: Trim pork chops.
Layer on top of chops in order: onion slice, tomato slice, American cheese slice, and bacon.
Bake 45 minutes at 350 degrees Fahrenheit.
Add minute rice (1/4 cup for 2, 1/2 cup for 4, etc.).
Continue to bake for 20 minutes, covered.
notes: Jerre Buech, 11/88

title: Barbecued Spareribs with Homemade Barbecue Sauce
directions: Simmer for 20 minutes.
Ribs: place in a pan. Cover with aluminum foil.
Bake in a hot oven 450 degrees for 15 minutes.
Reduce heat to 350 degrees, bake 1 hour longer with sauce.
pdfLink: Barbecued Spareribs with Homemade Barbecue Sauce.pdf

title: Savory Sausage Casserole
ingredients: 2 packages (2 ounces each) dehydrated chicken noodle soup
directions: Break apart sausage and brown in ungreased skillet; pour off excess fat.
Remove from burner.
Mix together sausage, rice, soup, onion, and celery in a 3-quart casserole.
Refrigerate.
When ready to bake, mix soy sauce with water and add this with the almonds, to the casserole.
Mix all gently.
Cover and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of: Jerri

title: Festive Holiday Ham
ingredients: 1 6 ounce can frozen orange juice concentrate, thawed
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Score top of ham and stud with cloves.
Line a 9x13 pan with heavy duty aluminum foil.
Bake ham uncovered for 30 minutes.
While ham is baking, prepare glaze: Combine water, orange juice, honey and spices in medium saucepan.
Mix 1/2 cup of orange juice mixture with cornstarch; stir mixture into remaining orange juice in saucepan and cook over medium heat until mixtures comes to a boil.
Boil 1-2 minutes and remove from heat.
At the end of 30 minutes, spoon glaze on top of ham and bake an additional 30 minutes.
Add additional glaze every 10 minutes.
Transfer to serving platter; surround with sliced oranges and parsley.
Decorate ham with cherries.
Server warm or cold.
Serves 10-15.
notes: Note: The remaining glaze may be heated and served with sliced ham. A large canned ham can be used in this recipe. "Serve with pleasure; the ham looks sensational and has spicy, orange taste!" The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Ham and Pork Loaf
directions: Combine brown sugar, dry mustard, and vinegar to make the sauce.
Pour over ham loaf and bake at 350 degrees for 1 hour.

title: Mustard Sauce by Jan Dachtler
directions: Mix, try, and chill.
notes: Jan Dachtler, Aug. 2002

title: Baked Fresh Ham in Beer by Jerri Burd
directions: Spread a boiled ham lightly with prepared mustard, then cover with a thick paste of corn syrup and brown sugar.
Stud with cloves.
Place in a baking pan and pour in a bottle of beer.
Bake in a very hot oven (450 degrees) basting often with the beer for 1.5 hours or until crust forms.
notes: Jerri Burd
pdfLink: Baked Fresh Ham in Beer by Jerri Burd.pdf

title: Grilled Bratwurst with Sauerkraut
ingredients: 1 32-ounce jar fresh sauerkraut, rinsed and drained
2 golden delicious apples, peeled and diced
directions: Prepare sauerkraut before grilling bratwurst.
Place sauerkraut, apples, chicken broth, vinegar, Worcestershire sauce and brown sugar in a covered saucepan; cook over low heat for 30-40 minutes.
During last 15 minutes of cooking time, prepare bratwurst. (See below.)
Place drained sauerkraut on a platter.
Top with grilled bratwurst.
Spoon a dollop of mustard on top of each sausage.
Garnish with apple slices and serve with dark bread.
Serves 4-6.
TO COOK BRATWURST: Place bratwurst and milk in heavy saucepan; bring to boil, cover and cook on lowest heat for 10 minutes.
Remove sausages from pan and grill on a lightly greased griddle or frying pan until golden brown on all sides.
notes:
Note: Sauerkraut can be prepared ahead.
"Serve with German potato salad!"
The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Eggs Fu Yung
ingredients: 1 cup finely chopped cooked ham or pork
directions: In top of double boiler, combine 1 teaspoon soy sauce, molasses, vinegar, and cornstarch, stirring until smooth.
Then gradually stir in chicken broth; over direct heat, bring to boiling, stirring. Reduce heat, and simmer 10 minutes. Sauce will be thickened and translucent. Keep warm over hot water.
In large bowl, combine ham, bean sprouts, and onion. Add eggs, salt, and 1 tablespoon soy sauce, stirring just until combined.

Slowly heat a little oil in small skillet. Add egg mixture, about 2 tablespoons at a time (as for pancakes). Sauté, turning once, just until browned on both sides. Remove, and keep warm. Repeat until egg mixture is used. Arrange "pancakes" on hot platter. Pour the hot sauce over them.
Makes 4 to 5 servings.

title: Baked Fresh Fillet of Cod with Lemon Butter and Parsley
ingredients: 1/4-1/2 teaspoon fresh lemon juice, for topping
1-2 teaspoons fresh minced parsley, for topping
directions: Preheat oven to 450 degrees.
Rinse fillets and pat dry.
Sprinkle fillets generously with lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Dip fillets in melted butter and then into crumbs.
Pat fillets to coat well.
Place fillets in a shallow glass baking dish.
Bake approximately 10 minutes or until fish flakes easily when touched with a fork.
Combine remaining lemon juice, melted butter and parsley; spoon over fillets and garnish with sliced lemon.
Serves 3-4.
notes:
Note: Fillets of haddock or pollock can also be used in this recipe.
PRESERVING FRESHNESS AT HOME: For superb seafood enjoyment, prepare fillets on the day of purchase. Maintain fresh flavor by placing fillets in a covered glass dish in the coldest section of your refrigerator. Do not allow fillets to rest on ice or in water.
THE 10-MINUTE RULE: A 1-inch thick fillet bakes in 10 minutes at 400-450 degrees. When done, the fish flakes easily. Do not overbake; fish continues to cook after removal from oven.
"This extra-easy recipe is perfect for today's busy cook!"
The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
pdfLink: Baked Fresh Fillet of Cod with Lemon Butter and Parsley.pdf

title: Lemon Linguini with Shrimp and Asparagus
ingredients: 1/2 pound asparagus, cut in 2" pieces and cooked
directions: Toss linguini with olive oil, lemon zest, lemon juice and all remaining ingredients except cheese and pine nuts.
Arrange on serving plates; top with cheese and pine nuts.
Serves 4.
notes: What a refreshing dish!, Equally delicious with grilled chicken!, Marked as "Very Good", ...from our collection of family favorites, Words Worth Eating is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
pdfLink: Lemon Linguini with Shrimp and Asparagus.pdf

title: Shrimp and Feta Pasta Salad
directions: Combine shrimp, feta, and spring onions.
Mix dressing ingredients.
Add to shrimp mixture.
Cover and refrigerate at least one hour.
Cook pasta, drain, and toss with above mixture.
Serve at room temperature.
Yields 6 pounds.
notes: Great Picnic Pasta!

title: Broiled Scallops in Garlic Butter
ingredients: ¼ - ½ teaspoon fresh lemon juice
1 tablespoon chopped fresh parsley, for garnish
directions: Soak scallops in cold salted water for 10 minutes. Drain and pat dry.
Butter a glass-baking dish; arrange scallops in the dish.
Combine garlic, lemon juice, butter, salt and pepper and drizzle over scallops; reserve some for use when serving.
Broil on highest rack for 4-5 minutes; turn and broil an additional 2-3 minutes or until scallops are tender.
If additional browning is desired, place bits of butter on top of scallops and return to broiler.
Garnish with lemon slices and parsley.
Serves 4.
Serve with steamed green beans and new potatoes!
notes: Marked as "Very Good", Ready in 10 minutes!, from our quick and easy collection

title: Coquilles St. Jacques
ingredients: 1 pint scallops (1 pound), cleaned and cut in pieces if large
directions: Melt 3 tablespoons butter in saucepan.
Add scallops, cook and stir 5 minutes.
Stir in 3 tablespoons flour and blend well.
Add 1 cup cream and 3/4 cup milk a little at a time.
Cook and stir until slightly thick.
Add 1/2 cup sautéed sliced mushrooms.
Season to taste with sherry.
Divide into shells and sprinkle with 1/2 cup buttered bread crumbs and with grated Parmesan cheese.
Bake at 400 degrees until crumbs are brown (about 10 minutes).
notes: Serves 4-6 large shells or 14 small shells

title: Shrimp Amandine
ingredients: 1 pound medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1/4 cup finely chopped shallots or green onions
1/3 to 1/2 cup sliced almonds, lightly toasted
2 to 3 cups cooked rice, to serve with shrimp
directions: Combine olive oil, corn oil, lemon juice and garlic and pour over shrimp; allow to marinate for 1 1/2 hours.
Drain shrimp and reserve marinade.
Melt margarine in a sauté pan and sauté shrimp and shallots until shrimp turn pink, about 4 to 6 minutes.
Place drained shrimp and shallots on a heated plate.
To pan drippings, add reserved marinade, almonds, Tabasco, white wine vinegar, chicken broth and salt.
Let cook over low heat for 2 to 4 minutes or until reduced to half its original volume; pour over shrimp.
Arrange shrimp on a platter with hot rice. Garnish with parsley.
Serves 2 to 3.
notes: For ease of preparation, marinate shrimp and cook rice early in the day. The actual cooking time of the shrimp is only 8 to 10 minutes. Cooked rice can be warmed in the microwave. In place of the corn oil margarine, a butter-margarine blend can be substituted. Serve with green peas and mushrooms and a fruit salad! Ukrop's Words Worth Eating is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Scallops Provençale
ingredients: 1 stick butter or corn oil margarine
1 pound sea scallops or 1 pound uncooked medium shrimp, peeled and cleaned
1 large green pepper, seeded and cut into 1-inch squares
2-3 tomatoes, cut into quarters or eighths
directions: Preheat oven to 400.
Place butter in a 9x13 glass baking dish; place in oven only until butter melts. Do not brown butter.
Place scallops or shrimp and vegetables in dish; stir to coat with butter.
Sprinkle with seasonings.
Bake 10-12 minutes or until seafood is done. Do not overcook.
Serves 4.
notes: Note: Cut extra-large scallops in half before cooking. Do not overcook seafood. A combination of scallops and shrimp can be used in this recipe. "Serve with rice, a green salad and hot bread for a delicious and easy seafood dinner!" The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Seared Scallops and Asparagus with Creamy Herbed Butter Sauce
ingredients: 1 pound green asparagus, trimmed and cut into slices on the diagonal
2 tablespoons TFM Roasted Garlic and Herb Finishing Butter
directions: Heat 1 tablespoon olive oil in a large skillet over medium high heat until hot, but not smoking. Sauté asparagus until tender, stirring occasionally; about 5 to 6 minutes. Transfer asparagus to plate with slotted spoon and return skillet to stove.

Pat scallops dry and sprinkle with pepper and 1/2 teaspoon salt. Add remaining olive oil to skillet. Sauté scallops until browned on both sides and cooked through, about 4 to 6 minutes, and transfer to a clean plate.

Return skillet to stove and add Nobilo Sauvignon Blanc, bring to a boil. Deglaze by scraping up any browned bits from the bottom of the skillet, boiling until liquid is reduced to about 2 tablespoons. Reduce heat to low and whisk in finishing butter, 1 tablespoon at a time until incorporated. Repeat with mascarpone cheese. Once fully incorporated, add tarragon, asparagus and remaining salt and cook until heated. Plate scallops and top with sauce. Garnish with lemon zest before serving.
pdfLink: Seared Scallops and Asparagus with Creamy Herbed Butter Sauce.pdf

title: Olney Crab Imperial
directions: Blend seasonings into mayonnaise, pour over the crab meat and toss together lightly.
Place the crab meat on scallop shells and top off with an additional tablespoon of mayonnaise.
Sprinkle with paprika.
Bake for 20 minutes in 375 degree F. oven.
Serve at once.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson; Serves 6.

title: Imperial Crab
directions: Combine above; fold in white sauce (4 tablespoons butter and 3 tablespoons flour and 1 cup milk. Melt butter in saucepan, add flour, stir until smooth, add milk, stir until smooth and thick).
Place in crab shells.
Dot with butter, pinch of paprika.
Bake at 400 degrees until brown and heated through.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Donna Dawson. Serves 6-8.

title: Crab Casserole - Teresa Brown
directions: Sauté onion and green pepper in butter.
Heat and melt mushroom soup and sharp cheese together.
Mix onion, green pepper, and soup together.
Butter a casserole dish and place crab in it.
Pour mixture over the crab.
Sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Bake in a 325 degree oven for 30 minutes or until bubbling.
notes: Marked as "Excellent". Serves 4; double recipe to serve 6 or 8.

title: Crabmeat Cherboug Curry
directions: Cut crabmeat into 1-inch cubes. Saute lightly in 1/2 cup butter over low heat; sprinkle with paprika. Add sherry and lemon juice.
In small, flat pan roast pistachio nuts with 1 tablespoon butter in 350 degree oven for 20 minutes.
Make basic cream sauce (1/2 cup). Add cayenne, mushrooms, curry, salt, MSG and nuts; add crabmeat last. Serve on fluffy rice mixed with peas. Makes 6 servings.
notes: ...from the Captain's Table

title: Crab Mornay
ingredients: 1 1/3 cups rich chicken broth (or concentrated canned chicken broth)
directions: Add 5 tablespoons flour to 1/3 cup melted butter.
Add 1 1/3 cups rich chicken broth.
Stir constantly. Cook, stirring over medium heat until sauce thickens.
Remove from heat, add 1/2 cup light cream.
Meanwhile, heat 1 1/2 pounds crab meat in top of double boiler. Fold in sauce.
Pour into casserole, and sprinkle lightly with grated cheese.
Run under broiler to brown.
Serve on rice or toast with sliced cucumber and tomato salad. Or serve in small shells as appetizer.
notes: 5-6 luncheon servings, 10-15 appetizer shells.

title: Shrimp Scampi a La 2010
ingredients: 2-3 pounds jumbo shrimp, peeled and deveined
directions: Melt butter in a hot skillet.
Add wine, shrimp, garlic, Parmesan cheese and juice of a lemon.
Shrimp are done when they turn pink and are firm.
Sprinkle with parsley before serving.
notes: Serves 4-6, Donna Dawson '85

title: Shrimp and Scallop Fettucini
ingredients: 3/4 pound fettucini noodles, cooked and drained
directions: Melt margarine in large skillet and sauté garlic. Add asparagus, peas and green onion; stir-fry until vegetables are crisp-tender, about 5 minutes.
Stir in shrimp, scallops, parsley, basil, chicken broth and wine vinegar. Cook over high heat for 2-4 minutes, stirring constantly, until seafood is thoroughly cooked. (Do not overcook.)
Add salt and pepper. Serve over hot fettucini and sprinkle with Parmesan cheese.
Serves 6.
notes: Ukrop's - Words Worth Eating. Seafood and fresh vegetables atop hot fettucini! Serve with a fresh tomato salad and hot Italian bread! The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Happy Accident Shrimp Casserole
ingredients: sherry and curry to taste (1/4 cup sherry)
directions: Combine all ingredients except dressing and butter.
Spoon mixture into 1 1/2 quart ungreased casserole dish.
Sprinkle over casserole dressing and margarine.
Bake uncovered 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Conne Luther. Serves 4-6.

title: Shrimp Jambalaya
directions: Melt butter, add onion and green pepper.
Sauté until brown, add shrimp, cook until pink.
Drain tomatoes, measuring juice. Add water to juice to equal 1 1/2 cups.
Add liquid, tomatoes, and spices and sugar to skillet.
Cover and simmer 5 minutes.
Stir in rice, simmer 5 minutes.
notes: Donna Dawson, serves 4

title: Baked Shrimp and Cheese
directions: Saute onions, garlic and bay leaves in butter until onions are lightly browned. Remove bay leaves and strain butter into saucepan, reserving onion mixture.
Add flour to butter and cook over low heat until bubbly. Slowly stir in cream and cook until medium thick. Add curry, wine, stir in onion mixture.
Divide shrimp among 6 buttered ramekins or baking shells - cover with sauce and sprinkle cheese. Bake at 350 degrees until cheese is melted (5 minutes) - broil until cheese is lightly browned.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson; From Anne Lusher '92

title: Creamy Shrimp and Egg Dish with Chinese Noodles
directions: Toast baskets and lemon slices.
Saute onion and pepper in butter in saucepan over low heat, do not brown.
Blend in flour and seasonings.
