directions: Mix all dry ingredients, add apples, eggs, salad oil, and vanilla.
Pour into greased 9x12-inch pan.
Bake 350 degrees for 50 minutes.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mary Kaye Long. May add nuts to batter. Also may ice with brown sugar icing.

title: Fresh Apple Cake
directions: Combine sugar, oil, vanilla, eggs, lemon juice and salt in mixing bowl.
Beat well.
Mix dry ingredients and add to sugar mixture, beating well again.
Add apples and nuts, mix well by hand.
Bake in greased and floured tube pan for 1 1/2 hours at 325 degrees.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson; Birdie Lightner; Oct '94

title: Apple Pecan Cake with Caramel Glaze
ingredients: 3 1/2 cups cooking apples, peeled and diced (3-4 large apples)
directions: Preheat oven to 325.
Grease and flour a 10-inch tube pan; set aside.
Mix oil and sugars in a large mixing bowl, beat in eggs, one at a time.
Mix all dry ingredients together with a fork and blend into creamed mixture.
Stir in all remaining ingredients.
Spoon into pan and bake for 1 1/2 hours or until cake springs back when pressed lightly near the center.
Cool in pan for 15 minutes; remove cake from pan and place on rimmed cake plate.
Set cake aside and prepare glaze.
GLAZE: Place all glaze ingredients in a saucepan and bring to boil while stirring constantly.
Boil one minute and slowly spoon over cake.
Decorate top with pecan halves.
Yields 20 slices.
notes: Freezes nicely. For a fresh baked appearance, glaze and decorate cake after thawing. LOW CHOLESTEROL VARIATION: Use no-stick cooking spray to grease cake pan; use Egg Beaters for eggs and use evaporated skim milk. Cut pecans to 1/2 cup or omit. No one would ever guess this is a low cholesterol cake. "Wonderful flavor!"
pdfLink: Apple Pecan Cake with Caramel Glaze.pdf

title: Key Lime Cake with Key Lime Cream
ingredients: 1 2-layer size butter flavored cake mix with pudding included
2 tablespoons Nellie and Joe's Key Lime juice
1/2 cup Nellie and Joe's Key Lime juice
directions: Cake: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease and flour two 8 or 9-inch round cake pans. In large bowl, combine all cake ingredients at low speed until moistened; beat 2 minutes at high speed. Pour batter into greased and floured pans. Bake 9-inch layers for 30 to 40 minutes, bake 8-inch layers for 35 to 45 minutes or until toothpick inserted in center comes out clean. Cool 15 minutes; remove from pans. Cool completely.

Key Lime Cream: In small bowl, combine sweetened condensed milk and 1/2 cup lime juice; mix well. In large bowl, beat whipping cream until stiff peaks form. Reserve 1 cup of whipped cream for garnish. Gently fold remaining whipped cream into condensed milk mixture just until blended.

To assemble: To assemble cake, slice each layer in half horizontally to make 4 layers. Place 1 cake layer cut side up on serving plate; spread with 1/3 of key lime cream mixture. Repeat with second and third layers. Top with remaining cake layer. Spread with reserved whipped cream. Refrigerate 2 to 3 hours before serving. Garnish with fresh lime slices. Serves 12-14.
Serve with fresh raspberries and a sprig of mint!
notes: From our collection of family favorites. The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
pdfLink: Key Lime Cake with Key Lime Cream.pdf

title: Two-egg Cake (cottage Pudding)
directions: Cream shortening and sugar at number 8 speed.
Add eggs one at a time and beat.
Add sifted dry ingredients alternately with milk on number 1 speed.
Bake in loaf pan (greased and floured) at 375 degrees.
Serve with lemon or chocolate sauce.

title: Hot Fudge Cake
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Melt chocolate and butter over low heat and set aside.
Place sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Measure flour and then sift with baking powder and salt.
Combine flour mixture with sugar; add chocolate mixture.
Slowly add milk and vanilla.
Pour batter into a lightly greased 9 x 13 baking pan.
Combine the first four topping ingredients and spread over the batter.
DO NOT MIX THE BATTER AND TOPPING TOGETHER!
Bake approximately 45 minutes or until the cake is done.
Allow to cool 15 minutes before serving.
Spoon into bowls and top with vanilla ice cream.
Serves 12-14.
notes: Makes its own fudge sauce as it bakes! When testing for doneness of the cake, press cake lightly with finger. If your finger does not leave an imprint, the cake is done. Do not test by sticking something through to the bottom of the dish since the sauce is on the bottom. Best warm, but it's also good when cold!

title: Raspberry Fudge Cake
ingredients: 1/4 cup cherry liqueur or maraschino cherry juice
Garnish: fresh mint sprigs, fresh raspberries
directions: Grease a 9-inch springform pan, and dust with cocoa; set aside.
Combine flour, baking powder, and salt; set aside.
Melt 3 semisweet chocolate squares, 4 unsweetened chocolate squares, and 3/4 cup butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly.
Whisk together sugar, 3/4 cup jam, liqueur, and eggs in a large bowl; whisk in melted chocolate mixture and flour mixture. Pour into prepared pan.

Bake at 350 degrees for 40 to 45 minutes or until set. Cool in pan on a wire rack 10 minutes; remove sides of pan, and cool cake completely on wire rack. If desired, wrap cake airtight, and store at room temperature until ready to serve.

To serve, melt remaining 1 semisweet chocolate square and 1 tablespoon butter in a heavy saucepan over low heat, stirring constantly. Let stand 15 to 20 minutes or until a good consistency for drizzling.
Meanwhile, spread remaining 1/4 cup jam over top of cake. Slice cake, and place on individual dessert plates. Drizzle chocolate glaze over slices. Garnish, if desired. Yield: 8 servings.
notes: Yield: 8 servings.

title: Applesauce Cake or Muffins
directions: Cream 0.5 cup soft shortening or butter and 2 cups sugar.
Beat in 2 eggs (about 0.33 cup).
Beat in 0.5 cup applesauce.
Sift together 2.875 cups sifted softasilk, 1.5 teaspoons soda, 1.5 teaspoons salt, 0.75 teaspoon cinnamon, 0.5 teaspoon cloves, and 0.5 teaspoon allspice, and beat into batter.
Mix in 0.5 cup water.
Stir in 0.5 cup nuts and 1 cup raisins (if desired).
Bake for cake at 350 degrees for 45 to 50 minutes.
Bake for cupcakes at 400 degrees for 20 to 30 minutes or even less.
Sprinkle regular or confectioners sugar on top.
For a fancy cake, lay a paper doily over cake, then sift confectioners sugar on it while cake is still hot.
Remove paper easily for a lacy design.
Let paper set about 10 minutes to let sugar soak into cake.

title: Lemon-raspberry Cake
directions: Grease 3 (9-inch) round cakepans; line with wax paper. Grease and flour wax paper. Set pans aside.
Beat shortening at medium speed of an electric mixer until creamy; gradually add sugar, beating well. Add eggs, one at a time, beating well after each addition.
Combine flour, baking powder, and salt; add to shortening mixture alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour mixture. Mix after each addition. Stir in flavorings.
Pour batter into prepared pans. Bake at 375 degrees for 18 to 20 minutes or until a wooden pick inserted in center comes out clean.
Cool in pans on wire racks 10 minutes; remove from pans, and let cool completely on wire racks.

Slice cake layers in half horizontally to make 6 layers. Place 1 layer, cut side up, on a cake plate; spread with 3 tablespoons preserves. Repeat procedure with remaining 5 layers and preserves, omitting preserves on top of last layer.

Reserve 1 cup Lemon Buttercream Frosting; spread remaining 1 3/4 cups frosting on top and sides of cake. Using a star tip, pipe reserved frosting on top of cake. Garnish, if desired. Store in an air-tight container in refrigerator.

Beat first 3 ingredients (butter or margarine, lemon rind, lemon juice) at medium speed of an electric mixer until creamy. Gradually add powdered sugar, beating until frosting is of spreading consistency.
notes: Yield: one 6-layer cake. Yield for frosting: 2 3/4 cups.

title: Lemon Filling for Cake
directions: Beat all together and boil until consistency of jelly.

title: Pineapple Filling for Cake
directions: Combine sugar, salt and cornstarch and mix well, then add pineapple, corn syrup and water, cook, until thick and clear, stirring constantly

title: Bourbon or Rum Balls
directions: Grind wafers and nuts finely in food chopper. Mix with remaining ingredients.
Roll into balls size of large cherry and dust with confectioners' sugar.
notes: This recipe makes from 30-35 balls, which will keep indefinitely.

title: Walnut Horns - Mom Willett
directions: Mix together, chill, and roll into balls size of walnuts.
Bake 12 minutes at 300 to 325 degrees.
Roll in powdered sugar.
notes: Mom Willett

title: Peanut Blossoms
directions: Sift together flour, soda, and salt.
Cream butter and peanut butter.
Add sugar and brown sugar.
Add egg and vanilla. Beat well.
Blend in dry ingredients gradually - mix.
Shape dough into small balls and roll in sugar and place on greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350 degrees for 10 minutes. - Take out of oven and top with chocolate candy kisses, pressing firmly but gently down - return to oven for 2 to 5 minutes.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Mary Ellen Hodge. 47 cookies.

title: Hello Dolly Bars
ingredients: 1 can Eagle Brand sweetened condensed milk
directions: Melt butter in 8x8-inch pan.
Layer crumbs, then coconut, chocolate chips, and nuts. Do not mix.
Pour Eagle Brand over ingredients.
Bake 30 minutes at 350 degrees.
Cool, then cut into small squares.
notes: A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson. Very rich.

title: Lemon Squares
directions: Heat oven to 350 degrees.
Measure flour after sifting.
Blend flour, butter, and confectioners' sugar thoroughly.
Press evenly in square pan, 8x8x2 inches.
Bake 20 minutes.
Beat rest of ingredients together.
Pour on crust and bake 20 to 25 minutes more.
Do not overbake!
Makes 16 squares.
notes: (The filling puffs during baking but flattens when cooled.)

title: Lemon Hazelnut Squares
ingredients: 6 tablespoons (3/4 stick) CHILLED UNSALTED BUTTER CUT INTO PIECES
directions: FOR CRUST: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F. Line 8-inch square baking pan with foil; butter foil. Mix flour, sugar and salt in processor. Add butter and nuts and blend until fine meal forms. Press onto bottom of prepared pan. Bake until light brown around edges, about 18 minutes.

MEANWHILE, PREPARE FILLING: Blend first 6 ingredients in processor. Pour filling onto hot crust. Bake until filling begins to brown at edges and is just springy to touch, about 20 minutes. Cool completely in pan on rack. Lift foil and dessert from pan. Gently peel foil from edges. Cut dessert into 16 squares.
(Can be made 1 day ahead. Wrap tightly; chill.)
Sift powdered sugar over lemon squares; serve at room temperature.
notes: makes 16

title: Toffee Cookies with Pecans
directions: Pat mixture out on cookie sheet.
Bake 20 minutes at 325 degrees.
Melt bar of German sweet chocolate with 3 tablespoons butter in double boiler.
Spread on dough while hot and sprinkle 1/2 cup pecans over top.

title: Birdie Lighthiser Toffee Cookies
ingredients: 6 plain 1.05 ounce milk chocolate Hershey bars
directions: Preheat oven 350 degrees
In large bowl, cream butter and sugar mixture.
Add egg yolk and beat until well blended.
Gradually add flour, stirring until well blended.
Spread mixture in a greased 15 1/2 x 10 1/2 jelly roll pan and bake till golden.
Remove from oven and arrange the chocolate bars over the top.
When the bars are melted, spread them evenly over cookie and sprinkle pecans on top.
When cool cut into small bars.
Bake 20 minutes?
notes: Birdie Lighthiser

title: Toffee Bars
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Crust - blend ingredients together - then press into ungreased 9x13 pan.
Then arrange pecans over crust.
Melt brown sugar and butter in saucepan - until it boils - Boil 1 minute (only) - stir constantly.
Pour over pecans and crust - Bake 20 minutes.
Cool 1 minute - Sprinkle with chocolate chips. Then spread around. Chill - then cut.
notes: Phyllis Miles, Dec. 1999. These freeze well.

title: Toffee Bars
directions: Press and flatten in jelly roll pan.
Bake 10 minutes at 350 degrees.
Then spread with topping.
Beat well 2 eggs, 1 cup brown sugar, and 1 teaspoon vanilla.
Mix and stir in 2 tablespoons flour, 1 teaspoon baking powder, 1 can coconut, and 1 cup nuts.
Return to oven and bake 25 minutes more or until golden brown.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Aunt Lydia

title: Peanut Butter Cookies by Susan Dawson
directions: Melt chocolate chips and wax.
Roll balls in chocolate.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Susan Dawson
pdfLink: Peanut Butter Cookies by Susan Dawson.pdf

title: Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Cookies
directions: Mix all together.
Bake at 325 degrees.
notes: Serves 6 dozen.

title: Nana's Icebox Cookies
ingredients: 1 cup melted butter (1/2 pint measuring cup)
directions: Sift flour, soda, and salt well together.
Place in buttered bread pan in refrigerator.
Next day warm sides on electric plate enough to just leave the pan on parafine paper.
Slice down centre in half.
Wrap each half in parafine paper and leave in refrigerator 3 or 4 days until set very hard.
Slice with sharp thin knife and bake in 325 oven.
Watch as cooking.

title: Saltine Cracker Toffee with Chocolate and Nuts
directions: Line cookie sheet with sides with parchment paper.
Line sheet with Saltine crackers.
Mix butter and sugar together, bring to boil for 3 minutes, stirring often.
Pour mixture over crackers.
Bake for 15 minutes at 350 degrees.
Take out of oven, place chocolate chips over top, and spread evenly.
May use slivered almonds or chopped pecans over top.
Cool overnight, then break into pieces.
notes: Written on Marriott Vacation Club stationery. Includes a To-Do list on the top: Relax, Have fun.
pdfLink: Saltine Cracker Toffee with Chocolate and Nuts.pdf

title: 5 Star Ghirardelli Chocolate Chip Bars
directions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
In large bowl, cream butter and brown sugar on medium speed until light and fluffy.
Add vanilla and eggs one at a time, mix.
Combine flour, baking powder, and salt.
Add dry ingredients gradually.
Fold in chocolate chips and nuts.
Spread batter into a greased 13-inch by 9-inch pan.
Bake at 325 degrees for 25 to 30 minutes.
Cool completely.
Cut into squares, 16 to 18 bars.

title: Chocolate Chip-peanut Butter Brownies
ingredients: 1 cup of flour (right out of the bag)
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Mix flour, baking powder and salt; set aside.
In a small mixing bowl, cream the peanut butter, butter or margarine and both sugars until light and fluffy.
Beat in the eggs just until blended.
Stir in the flour mixture just until blended.
Add chocolate chips and vanilla.
Spread batter in a greased 8-inch baking pan.
Bake 30-35 minutes.
Do not overbake.
Cool and cut into squares.
Yields 25-30 squares.
notes: Note: If using a glass dish, reduce heat to 325. \"Great for lunches and after school treats!\"

title: Chocolate Snowballs
directions: Blend butter or margarine and sugar. Beat in egg and vanilla. Set aside.
Sift flour and salt. Add to butter and sugar mixture.
Add chocolate morsels and chopped nuts.
Form into 1-inch balls.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes in 350° oven on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Cool slightly, then roll in confectioners sugar.
notes: Yield: 6 dozen. Recipe by liz tafel.

title: Holiday Sugar Cookies
ingredients: Red or green sugar crystals, optional (see note)
directions: Preheat oven to 325 degrees.
Use an electric mixer on low speed to cream margarine or butter with 1 1/2 cups sugar; add egg yolks.
Sift dry ingredients; mix with creamed sugar mixture.
Add almond extract; mix well.
Form into 1-inch balls and roll in remaining 1/2 cup sugar.
Space balls 2 inches apart on an ungreased cookie sheet.
Do not flatten cookies.
Bake 10-12 minutes.
Remove from baking sheet while warm.
Yields 4 dozen.
notes: Note: Do not crowd cookies together since they spread while baking. Cookies will be soft when removed from oven but will firm as they cool. Can be made ahead and frozen. Festive Touch: Use decorative sugar to sprinkle tops after baking. "Crisp on the outside and slightly chewy inside!" The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Soft Sugar Cookies - Jerri Byrd
directions: Cinnamon-sugar
Cream butter and sugar.
Add eggs 1 at a time. Add vanilla. Beat until light and fluffy.
Mix and sift flour, salt, baking powder, and soda. Add to cream mixture alternately with sour cream.
For 3" cookies, drop by heaping teaspoons on well greased sheet - well apart.
With spatula flatten into circles about 3" in diameter.
Sprinkle with sugar.
Bake at 400° for 10-12 minutes.
30 cookies
notes: Jerri Byrd

title: Sugar Cookies
directions: Cream butter and add sugar gradually and beat.
Add eggs one at a time beating after each addition.
Sift dry ingredients and add to cream mixture.
Chill dough 3 to 4 hours.
Roll 1/8 to 1/4 inch thick and cut in desired shapes.
Bake at 375 degrees for 6 to 8 minutes.
notes: Marked as "Good"

title: Shortbread - Christa's Mother's Recipe
directions: Cream butter, slowly add confectioners' sugar and brown sugar.
Using sifter, fold in about 3 cups of the flour.
Then turn out on lightly floured board and knead lightly, and work in rest of flour.
Do not knead.
Pat out until 1/4 inch thick - cut into shapes.
Bake until bottoms are lightly brown.
Turn onto brown paper.
Dust with powdered sugar.
Store in air tight container.
Bake at 400 degrees for 12 minutes.

title: Old Fashioned Ginger Snaps - Nana Frillett's Recipe
directions: Cream butter and sugar, then stir in 2 beaten eggs.
Add molasses and mix well.
Sift together flour, ginger, salt, and soda, and stir into above mixture.
Stand in refrigerator overnight.
Roll out and cut with round cutter on floured cloth.
Bake at 400 degrees for 10 minutes.
notes: Nana Frillett's - July 14, 1964
pdfLink: Old Fashioned Ginger Snaps - Nana Frillett's Recipe.pdf

title: Brown-eyed Susans
directions: Mix all ingredients and roll into small balls and press down with thumb.
Bake at 400 degrees for 10-12 minutes.
Mix frosting and put on cookie while they are still warm.
notes: This makes about 60-75 cookies.

title: Rum Balls with Dried Cherries and Walnuts
directions: In processor, blend Nilla Wafers, sugar, walnut and cherries.
Mix honey and rum and add to mixture.
Roll into 1" balls and toss in powdered sugar or drizzle with melted chocolate.
Let ripen in refrigerator wrapped for 24 to 48 hours.
notes: Marked as "Very Good", Happy Holidays! Hunter Folman Pastry Chef, T.D.C.
pdfLink: Rum Balls with Dried Cherries and Walnuts.pdf

title: Coated Cookie Drops
directions: Crush cookies.
In small bowl heat cream cheese and crushed cookies until well blended.
Roll into 3/4 inch balls.
Cover and refrigerate for at least 1 hour.
Melt white chocolate and Crisco until melted.
Dip cookie balls until they are completely coated.
Melt semi-sweet chocolate chips with Crisco and drizzle over cookie balls to decorate.
Place back in refrigerator until hardened.
Store in refrigerator or freezer.
notes: Yield: 7 and 1/2 dozen

title: Montana Bars - Blond Brownies
directions: Cream butter and sugar.
Mix the rest of ingredients and add to sugar butter mixture.
Grease 9x13 pan.
Bake at 350 degrees for 25 minutes.
notes: Aunt Joanie

title: Philly Cheesecake Brownies
ingredients: 1 package (19.8 ounces) Betty Crocker Fudge Brownie Mix
1 package (8 ounces) Philadelphia Brand Cream Cheese, softened
directions: Prepare brownie mix as directed on package. Pour into greased 13x9-inch baking pan.
Beat cream cheese with electric mixer on medium speed until smooth. Add sugar, mixing until blended. Add egg and vanilla; mix just until blended.
Pour cream cheese mixture over brownie mixture; cut through batter with knife several times for marbled effect.
Bake at 350°F for 35 to 40 minutes or until cream cheese mixture is lightly browned. Cool; cut into squares. Makes 24.
notes: Note: Do not use brownie mixes that include a syrup pouch.

title: Henry Haller's Chocolate Brownies
ingredients: 1 cup chopped pecans or semisweet chocolate chips
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease an 8x8-inch square pan.
Melt butter in a small saucepan, pour into a mixing bowl and stir in sugar.
Melt chocolate over low heat in the small saucepan, add to butter-sugar mixture and blend well. Stir until cool and creamy smooth.

In a separate bowl, beat eggs until light and fluffy. Add to chocolate mixture and stir until well-blended. Beat in 3 tablespoons of orange liqueur, vanilla extract, grated orange rind and instant espresso coffee powder.
Gradually add flour, blending thoroughly.
Mix in nuts or chocolate chips.

Pour into prepared pan and bake for 20 to 25 minutes, or until knife inserted in center comes out clean. Remove pan and cool on wire rack for 30 minutes. Brush brownies with remaining liqueur. Cover and cool completely before cutting into squares.
Makes 16 2-inch squares.

title: Double Frosted Brownies
directions: Prepare 1 box (1 pound) brownie mix as for cake brownies; add 0.5 cup chopped nuts.
Bake in 9x9x2 inch pan as directed on label.
Cool in pan.
For 1st frosting: Cream 0.5 cup butter until fluffy; beat in 2 tablespoons instant vanilla pudding powder and 3 tablespoons milk.
Gradually beat in 2 cups sifted confectioners' sugar.
When smooth, spread on brownies.
Chill while preparing 0.5 box fudge frosting mix.
Spread fudge frosting on first frosting.
Store refrigerated.
When ready to serve, cut in 3x1 inch bars.
Makes 27 bars.
notes: If preferred, prepare fudge frosting from 1 box (12 ounces) of chocolate fudge mix. Make frosting as directed on the label; cool before spreading on first frosting.

title: Norwegian Macaroons with Oatmeal and Almonds
ingredients: 1 cup pre-sifted flour (use out of the bag)
1 3/2 ounce can Baker's Angel Flake coconut
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Mix first 6 ingredients together; add coconut.
Stir in melted butter and margarine; add egg.
Mix well and drop by heaping teaspoons onto an ungreased baking sheet.
Leave approximately two inches between cookies to allow the edges to brown.
Flatten each cookie slightly with a fork and top with 3 or 4 almond slices and a sprinkle of nutmeg.
Bake 15 minutes. Do not overbake!
Yields approximately 36 cookies.
notes: Note: To avoid having the fork stick to the dough, dip the fork in cold water after flattening each cookie. "These exceptionally easy cookies have a rich buttery taste!"
pdfLink: Norwegian Macaroons with Oatmeal and Almonds.pdf

title: Grandmother's Christmas Cream Wafers
directions: Use a large spoon to cream butter, cream and flour.
Chill in a covered bowl until easy to handle.
Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
On a flour-covered board, roll 1/3 of the dough to a thickness of 1/8 inch. (Keep remaining dough chilled.)
Cut into 1 1/2 inch rounds.
With a spatula, transfer rounds to a piece of waxed paper which has been sprinkled with 1/2 cup of granulated sugar.
Coat each side with sugar.
Place on an ungreased baking sheet and prick 4 times with a fork.
Repeat with remaining dough.
Bake 7 to 9 minutes. Do not brown.
When cookies have cooled, put wafers together with cream filling in the middle.
Filling: Cream butter, sugar and vanilla until smooth and fluffy.
Yields 2 1/2 to 3 dozen double cookies.
notes: "A cookie that creates memories!", ...from our collection of family favorites, "This is a recipe you'll hand down to your grandchildren!", The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Cathi Van Pelt's Butter Cookies
directions: Mix by hand on a lightly floured cloth.
Roll out to 0.25 inch for tart shells and a little thicker for cookies.
Bake at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for about 10 minutes.
notes: Cathi Van Pelt

title: Tom Thumb Tarts - Beedi's Recipe
directions: Soften butter at room temperature. Add cream cheese; beat until smooth and creamy.
Add flour 1/2 cup at a time, blending well after each addition. Work with fingers to a smooth dough.
Shape into balls about 1/2 inch in diameter. Place each ball in cup of small muffin pans. With thumb press to line bottom and sides.
For filling beat eggs slightly. Combine sugar, coffee and salt. Gradually add to eggs beating well after each addition.
Add melted butter and vanilla.
Sprinkle pecans in pastry cup. Spoon filling over pecans filling cups not quite full.
Bake at 350 degrees for 20 minutes or until set.
Garnish with whipped cream.
notes: Marked as good. Makes 2 dozen small cupcake size or 4 dozen mini.

title: Butter Chewies
directions: Sift flour and brown sugar. Add butter and cut with pastry blender until like cornmeal.
Press into well buttered 9x13 pan.
Bake 375 degrees over 12-15 minutes.
Beat egg whites until stiff. Add nuts and coconuts.
Beat egg yolks, add brown sugar and salt.
Mix egg whites and egg yolks mixtures together.
Pour over baked mixture. Bake at 325 degrees for 20-25 minutes. Cut into squares.
notes: Myra Wormald

title: Date Goodies
directions: Cook together, stirring constantly for 10 minutes.
Stir in 2 to 2 1/2 cups rice Krispies.
Stir in 2 cups chopped walnuts.
Roll into balls, and roll in flaked coconut.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Lucilla Foster, 1976

title: Pecan-date Bars
ingredients: 1 pound chopped and lightly sugared Dromedary dates
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Cream butter and 2 cups sugar well; add eggs one at a time.
Beat well after each addition.
Add one cup of flour to mixture.
Mix remaining cup of flour with dates and nuts.
Add to batter.
Grease and flour a 9 x 13 baking pan and pour mixture into pan.
Bake for 25-30 minutes or until done.
Cut into squares and roll in confectioners' sugar.
Yields approximately 36 bars.
notes: Note: If using a glass dish, reduce heat to 325. "Moist and chewy!"

title: Mincemeat Filled Cookies
directions: Cream butter and sugar, then add beaten egg, salt, milk and vanilla.
Then sift flour, soda and cream of tartar together and add to first mixture and blend well.
Roll on well floured board fairly thin and cut with round cookie cutter.
Place teaspoonful of mincemeat on cookie round and place another round on top pressing down edges of cookie to seal mincemeat in.
notes: (Happy Eating!)

title: Cinnamon Cookies
directions: Mix ingredients - add cherries, nuts and dates - Roll and refrigerate
Bake at 350 degrees (slice and bake) 10-12 minutes.

title: Angel Cookies
directions: Roll in balls and pat down
Decorate with cherries, pecans, etc.
Bake at 350 degrees for 10-15 minutes
notes: Ellen Vonvalkenburg

title: Caramel Cream Sandwich Cookies with Browned Butter Frosting
ingredients: 2 1/4 cups sifted Pillsbury's Best Enriched Flour (Plain)
directions: Cream 1 cup butter. Gradually add 3/4 cup firmly packed brown sugar, creaming well.
Blend in 1 unbeaten egg yolk, then add 2 1/4 cups sifted Pillsbury's Best Enriched Flour (Plain). Stir until mixture forms a dough. Chill if necessary for easy handling.
Shape into balls about the size of a marble. Place on ungreased baking sheet and flatten to 1/8-inch thickness with the palm of the hand. Mark a design by pressing with fork in one direction.

Bake at 325 degrees for 8 to 10 minutes. Makes about 4 dozen. Bake until a very light brown, remove from sheets while warm. Place flat sides of two cookies together with frosting, sandwich-style. Cookies are also good plain.

To make the frosting: Brown slightly 2 tablespoons butter in saucepan. Remove from heat and blend in 1 1/4 cups sifted confectioners' sugar. Gradually add 1/2 teaspoon French's Vanilla and 4 to 5 teaspoons cream until spreading consistency.
notes: Good
pdfLink: Caramel Cream Sandwich Cookies with Browned Butter Frosting.pdf

title: Mary Beth's German Chocolate Caramel Brownies
directions: Melt caramels with 1/2 cup evaporated milk in sauce pan until dissolved. Set aside. (use low heat)
Combine cake mix, melted butter, and the rest of the evaporated milk.
Mixture will be doughy. Press 1/2 of mixture into bottom of a greased and floured 9 inch by 13 inch pan.
Bake in 350 degree oven for 4 minutes.
Sprinkle chocolate chips over baked crust.
Spread caramel over chocolate chips.
Crumble remaining cake mix on top.
Bake for another 15 minutes.
Remove from oven and cool slightly.
Refrigerate for 30 minutes, then cut.
Store in refrigerator.
notes: Mary Beth 11/84
pdfLink: Mary Beth's German Chocolate Caramel Brownies.pdf

title: Butterscotch Chocolate Chip Brownies
directions: Mix everything in one pan.
Melt butter, stir in sugar, then the eggs.
Add flour, salt and baking powder, then the nuts and chocolate chips.
Bake in floured and greased 10x14 pan at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
Do not overbake.

title: Wesson Wonder Brownies
directions: Sift flour, salt and baking powder.
Beat sugar into beaten eggs.
Add chocolate, oil and vanilla.
Add flour all at once - mix well.
Add nuts.
Pour into oiled 7x11 pan.
Bake 25 minutes at 350 degrees.
Cut into squares while warm - about 10 minutes after coming from the oven.
Cool.
notes: Jerre

title: Date Pinwheels
directions: Combine the dates, sugar and water in a saucepan and cook over low heat until thick (about 10 minutes). Add nuts and cool.
Allow shortening to soften at room temperature. Cream for 1 minute at high speed.
Add sugar gradually to the beater still at high speed. After all is added scrape bowl and beat 1 minute longer.
Add eggs, unbeaten one at a time and beat 1 minute after each addition at high speed.
Turn to medium speed and add sifted dry ingredients, mixing.
Chill.
Divide into 2 parts and roll out 1/4 inch thick. Spread each with some of the date filling and roll up as for a jelly roll into 2 long rolls.
Chill overnight.
Then cut with a sharp knife into slices about 1/4 inch thick.
Bake 400 degrees Fahrenheit for 10-12 minutes.
Makes 5 dozen cookies.

title: Molasses Chocolate Bars - Jerri
directions: Beat the egg and blend in sugar, molasses, oil, and vanilla.
Sift flour with salt and baking soda and add to egg mixture with chopped nuts and chocolate chips.
Mix well and spread in greased and floured 9-inch square pan.
Mark into bars (1" x 2").
Bake at 350 degrees for 45 minutes.
Let cool.
Store in tightly covered tin (28 bars).
notes: Jerri, oven 350 degrees - 45 minutes

title: Pecan Crunch Cookies
directions: Cream together butter, sugar, and vanilla.
Add crushed potato chips and pecans.
Stir in flour.
Form into small balls (use about 1 tablespoon of dough for each).
Place on ungreased cookie sheet.
Press balls flat with bottom of tumbler dipped in sugar.
Bake in 350° oven for 16-18 minutes.
notes:
Jerri
3 1/2 dozen

title: Chocolate Meringue Bars
directions: Cream shortening and sugars.
Add egg yolks and vanilla.
Sift soda, salt, and flour.
Add to egg mixture alternately with water.
Press into 9x13 cake pan and sprinkle with chocolate chips.
Beat egg whites until fluffy and gradually add brown sugar.
Spread over cookies and sprinkle with nuts.
Bake in oven at 325 degrees for 30-35 minutes.
Cut as for brownies.
notes: Jerri

title: Bullard's Chocolate Nut Bars
directions: Combine shortening and sugar. Cream thoroughly.
Add eggs 1 at a time, beating after each addition.
Sift together dry ingredients.
Gradually add to shortening mixture, mixing after each addition.
Add nuts and chocolate chips. Blend.
Spread evenly over well oiled 10 1/2 x 15 1/2 x 3/4 inch pan.
Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 25 to 30 minutes.
When almost cool cut in squares.
4 dozen bars 3 inches x 1 inch

title: Bullard's Cherry Winks
directions: Mix together flour, baking powder, soda, and salt.
Cream together shortening and sugar.
Beat in eggs, milk, and vanilla.
Mix together chopped dates, chopped nuts, and chopped cherries.
Roll into balls with a level tablespoon full.
Crush 2 1/2 cups corn flakes.
Roll ball in corn flakes and place 1/4 cherry on each one.
Bake at 375 degrees for 10-12 minutes.

title: Oatmeal Cookies
ingredients: 3 cups oats (quick or old fashioned), uncooked
directions: Beat shortening, sugars, egg, water, vanilla, and salt.
Sift together flour and soda; add to creamed mixture; blend well.
Stir in oats.
Drop by teaspoonsful onto greased cookie sheets.
Bake at 350 degrees for 12 to 15 minutes.
notes: Optional: nuts or raisins.

title: Melomakarona Honey Spice Cookies
directions: Mix all ingredients together.
Roll into small balls.
Flatten.
Bake at 325 degrees for 25 minutes.
When cool, dip in honey syrup and add nuts.
notes: Lusa Pickett

title: Honey Syrup
directions: In pan combine 1 cup sugar, 1/2 cup water, 1/2 cup honey.
Bring to boil, boil gently for 10 minutes.
Remove from heat and keep warm.

title: Holland Christmas Cookies
directions: Work margarine until soft and creamy.
Add sugar and cream until light.
Add beaten egg and almond flavoring.
Beat until smooth.
Add flour that has been sifted with salt and baking powder.
Blend well.
Roll out dough and cut with fancy cookie cutters.
Sprinkle tops with colored sugars.
Place on greased cookie tin.
Bake in hot oven 400 degrees for 10 minutes.

title: Polvorones (sugar Cookies)
directions: Cream margarine and sugar, add flour and vanilla.
Mix well and chill for several hours.
Roll on floured board and cut small round shapes.
Place on greased cookie sheet.
Bake at 350 degrees for about 15 minutes.
Dust with more sugar while warm.
Cool on rack.

title: Christmas Nut Crescents
directions: Filling: Grind 2-3 pounds walnuts in blender, add 1 1/2 cups white sugar, 1 1/2 cups brown sugar, 3/4 cup confectioners' sugar, 1/2 cup honey, 4 tablespoons melted margarine.
Mix together, then add boiling water a little at a time. Should be thick for spreading.
Dough: Dissolve 2 cakes yeast in 1 pint sour cream. Let stand.
Cream 1 pound butter, add 3 tablespoons sugar, mix.
Add 3 egg yolks and then 1 teaspoon salt. Beat well.
Mix in sour cream mixture.
Carefully add 8 cups flour - 2-3 cups at a time. Knead together with hands.
Divide dough into 10 snowball-sized balls.
Roll each out in a circle (8 inches). Cut into wedges.
Fill each with nut filling. Roll up as crescent roll. Point side down.
Bake 375 degrees for 15 minutes.
notes: Bobbie Jessix

title: Cream Puffs
directions: Add butter to boiling water, heat until butter melts.
Add flour all at once and mix, cook stirring until mixture leaves side of pan.
Remove and cool 1 minute.
Add eggs one at a time, beating at time.
Drop by heaping teaspoons about 2 inches apart on lightly greased sheet.
Bake in 450 degrees for 10 minutes, then 400 degrees for 20-25 minutes.
notes: Marked as "Very Good"; From Willetts

title: Strawberries Chantilly
ingredients: 2 pints strawberries, capped and quartered (leave 12 berries whole)
1/2 cup grated sweet baking chocolate or semi-sweet chocolate, divided
directions: Whip cream with confectioners sugar and vanilla; fold in strawberries and 1/3 cup grated chocolate.
Serve strawberry mixture over sliced pound cake.
Top with grated chocolate and whole berries.
Serves 8-12.
notes:
Note: Be sure to use extra-ripe strawberries. The measurement for vanilla is correct.
"Prepare whipped cream mixture ahead of time and assemble when ready to serve!"
The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.
Marked as "Very Good"

title: Biscuits for Strawberries
directions: Sift together.
Dust pan with flour.
Bake 425 degrees for 10-12 minutes.
notes: Good, Marked as "Very Good"

title: Old-fashioned Strawberry Shortcake
ingredients: 0.5 cup (1 stick) chilled unsalted butter, cut into bits
0.5 cup half-and-half, PLUS more for brushing on top
3 cups hulled and sliced ripe strawberries
directions: Heat oven to 425 degrees.
Grease a large baking sheet and set aside.
Biscuits: In a large mixing bowl, mix together the flour, baking powder, salt, and sugar. Add the butter and cut it in with a pastry cutter until the mixture is crumbly.

Add the half-and-half and egg, and stir just until the dry ingredients are moistened. Transfer the dough to a lightly floured work surface and knead 3 to 4 times. Roll out the dough 0.5-inch thick, cut out rounds with a 2.5-inch biscuit cutter, and arrange on the prepared baking sheet. Roll the scraps together and cut out more rounds. Brush the tops lightly with half-and-half and bake in the upper third of the oven until golden brown, 12 to 15 minutes.

Topping: While the biscuits bake, make the topping by tossing the strawberries and sugar together in a medium-size mixing bowl. In another medium-size mixing bowl, beat together the cream and vanilla with an electric mixer until thick but still soft.
Split the hot biscuits in half, spoon equal amounts of strawberries over the bottom halves, spoon the whipped cream over the strawberries, cover with the biscuit tops at an angle. Serve immediately.
notes: Adapted from "Biscuit Bliss" by James Villas

title: Chocolate Krenkles
ingredients: 6 ounces package chocolate chips - melt, cool to room temperature
directions: Cream shortening, butter, and melted chocolate.
Add dry ingredients.
Divide dough into 12 balls.
Press into muffin pan with muffin liners.
Bake at 375 degrees for 10 minutes.
Fill with ice cream - top with creme de menthe or chocolate sauce.

title: Hodge's Mom's Ice Cream
directions: Mix sugar, salt, and eggs, slightly beaten.
Pour on scalded milk, cook in double boiler until mixture coats spoon.
Cool, strain, add condensed milk, stirring well; then add whipped cream and vanilla.
Chill well before using.
notes: Excellent / My Recipe / Ice Cream / Hodge's (mom)

title: Lemon Ice Cream
ingredients: 1 pint custard; in making custard, use 1 egg, 1 tablespoon cornstarch.
directions: Squeeze lemons, slice lemons very fine, to which add all the sugar, let stand at least an hour.
Mix all ingredients, lemons and sugar last.
notes: Ann Bowen's recipe - delicious, Summer 1989

title: Red Wine Sauce for Lavender Ice Cream
directions: In heavy sauce pan bring wine, sugar and peppercorn to a boil until sugar dissolved.
Remove from heat - add tarragon and steep for 5 minutes - strain.
pdfLink: Red Wine Sauce for Lavender Ice Cream.pdf

title: Boiled Custard - Mom Hodge
directions: Place milk in double boiler and heat until skim forms over milk.
Beat the yolks slightly, add sugar and salt.
Take milk off stove (the top pan), slowly stir egg yolks into milk, stir well to mix.
Replace pan in bottom part of double boiler, cook stirring until the mixture thickens and forms a coating on the spoon.
Remove at once, cool and flavor.
If custard curdles, beat with an egg beaker.
Beat egg whites very stiff and add 3 tablespoons of powdered sugar.
Place by spoonfuls in water which is hot but not boiling.
Cover the dish.
Test occasionally by putting a knife into it; when it is done nothing will stick to the knife.
Remove from the water with a wire egg beater or split spoon and place on top of the custard.
notes: Mom Hodge

title: Pumpkin Roll
directions: Grease 10x15 jelly roll pan and line with wax paper - grease and flour wax paper.
Mix and bake at 375 degrees for 15 minutes.
Turn onto towel sprinkled with granulated sugar and remove wax paper.
Cover with fresh wax paper and roll towel, cake, and wax paper and allow to cool while rolled.
Filling:
Unroll cake and remove wax paper.
Spread filling and re-roll.
Dust with powdered sugar.
notes: VG. From Lisa Sizemore VEI

title: Apple Pie Dumplings
ingredients: 4 large Rome Beauty or Delicious apples, cored, pared
directions: Start heating oven to 425 degrees Fahrenheit.
Meanwhile, roll out half of pastry, 1/8 inch thick; cut into two 7-inch squares; place apple in center of each square.
Mix sugar, cinnamon, nutmeg; use half to fill 2 apples.
Bring opposite points of pastry up over each apple; overlap and seal. Fold over corners of dumplings to make neat ridge; trim pastry if necessary. Arrange in 8-inch by 8-inch by 2-inch baking dish.
With other half of pastry repeat steps 2, 3, and 4.
Bake dumplings about 55 minutes or till apples are fork tender and pastry is brown.
notes: Marked as "Good"

title: Syrup for Apple Dumplings
directions: Pour 1 1/2 cups boiling water over apple peel.
Simmer, covered 20 minutes.
Drain peel; stir liquid with 2 tablespoons sugar, 1/4 cup butter, 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon, 1 tablespoon grated lemon rind, and 3 tablespoons lemon juice until sugar dissolves.
Pour into dumpling dish.
Bake at 375 degrees Fahrenheit for 40 minutes, or until tender.

title: Apple Pudding with Dates and Nuts
directions: Mix all of this together well and add: 4 cups chopped raw apples, 1 cup dates, 1 cup nuts.
Bake in greased and floured pan 1 hour at approximately 350 degrees in a 9x13 pan.
Top with a lemon sauce or whipped cream and cherry.
notes: Very good. Recipe from the kitchen of Jean Frachers. Serves 8.
pdfLink: Apple Pudding with Dates and Nuts.pdf

title: Nutty Baked Apples
ingredients: 6 Golden Delicious apples, peeled and cored
1 pint vanilla ice cream or low-fat frozen yogurt, optional
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Rub prepared apples with orange juice; set aside.
Combine zwieback crumbs, almonds and brown sugar in a blender or food processor; blend into fine crumbs.
Pour mixture into a pie plate and set aside.
Beat egg white until frothy; dip each apple into the egg white and roll in nut-crumb mixture.
Stand apples in a shallow glass baking dish and fill center with preserves.
Pour water around apples to a depth of 1/4-inch.
Sprinkle sugar in the water.
Bake in a preheated 350-degree oven for 1 1/2 hours or until apples are fork tender.
Serve warm with a scoop of ice milk or yogurt, if desired.
Serves 6.
notes: Serve as a side dish or dessert! A low cholesterol recipe. Note: The apples are a "knife-and-fork" dessert. This recipe can easily be prepared in smaller amounts. The baked apples can be reheated in the microwave. "The nutty crust makes this an extra-special apple dish that is also low cholesterol!"

title: Crème Brûlée
ingredients: 1/3 cup sugar, plus 1/4 cup for the brûlée topping
directions: Preheat oven to 300°F.

In a large bowl, combine the egg yolks and the 1/3 cup sugar, whisk together until the sugar has dissolved and the mixture is thick and pale yellow. Add cream and vanilla, and continue to whisk until well blended. Strain into a large bowl, skimming off any foam or bubbles.

Divide mixture among 6 ramekins or custard cups. Place in a water bath, and bake until set around the edges, but still loose in the center, about 40–50 minutes. Remove from the oven and leave in the water bath until cooled.
Remove cups from water bath and chill for at least 2 hours, or up to 2 days.

When ready to serve, sprinkle about 2 teaspoons sugar over each custard. For best results, use a small hand torch to melt the sugar. If you do not have a torch, place ramekins under the broiler until sugar melts. Re-chill custards a few minutes before serving.
Serves 6.
notes: Adapted from The Crème Brûlée Cookbook, by Debbie Puente (Renaissance Books, 1998). Williams-Sonoma, Inc., 1999.

title: Hot Fudge Cake
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees.
Melt chocolate and butter over low heat and set aside.
Place sugar in a large mixing bowl.
Measure flour and then sift with baking powder and salt.
Combine flour mixture with sugar; add chocolate mixture.
Slowly add milk and vanilla.
Pour batter into a lightly greased 9 x 13 baking pan.
Combine the first four topping ingredients and spread over the batter.
DO NOT MIX THE BATTER AND TOPPING TOGETHER!
Bake approximately 45 minutes or until the cake is done.
Allow to cool 15 minutes before serving.
Spoon into bowls and top with vanilla ice cream.
Serves 12-14.
notes: Note: When testing for doneness of the cake, press cake lightly with finger. If your finger does not leave an imprint, the cake is done. Do not test by sticking something through to the bottom of the dish since the sauce is on the bottom. "Best warm, but it's also good when cold!"

title: Caramel Pecan Cheesecake
ingredients: 2 tablespoons milk and 1/4 cup caramel topping
directions: Combine first 4 ingredients - Pat into bottom and sides of 8-inch springform pan - Refrig.
Beat cream cheese - add 1/2 cup caramel, add eggs, milk - Blend - Pour into crust - Bake at 350 degrees - 40-45 minutes until set. Cool 15 minutes.
Combine sour cream, remaining caramel. Spoon atop cheese cake from pan. Cool 30 minutes more.
Remove sides of pan cool - chill - Garnish with pecan halves
notes: from Jerry Stone 2/91 10-12 Servings, 1-8" cheesecake, A favorite recipe from Nancy Dawson

title: Cream Cheese Cake with Sour Cream - Dingis
ingredients: 4 packages soft cream cheese (small package 3/4 pound)
1 teaspoon lemon juice or 1/2 teaspoon vanilla
directions: Make it day before serving it.
Line a 9-inch pie pan.
Use graham cracker crust - chill well.
Bake the cake at 375 degrees for 20 minutes.
Remove cake from oven.
Increase heat to 425 degrees.
Dust top with cinnamon immediately.
Let cake cool to room temperature.
Mix well and pour over cake: 1 1/2 cups thick sour cream, 2 tablespoons sugar, 1/2 teaspoon vanilla, 1/8 teaspoon salt.
Bake cake in hot oven 5 minutes.
Permit it to cool, then chill it thoroughly until ready to serve.
notes: Marked as "Very Good"
pdfLink: Cream Cheese Cake with Sour Cream - Dingis.pdf

title: Cheesecake with Strawberry Glaze
ingredients: 2 - 8 ounce packages cream cheese, room temperature
1 cup H2O (decreased by 2 tablespoons each if frozen strawberries are used)
directions: Cream butter and sugar together. Add crumbs and mix well.
Press into a 9 inch springform pan.
Mash cheese and add sugar - cream together.
Add egg yolks, sour cream, vanilla, and lemon juice - blend together.
Fold in beaten egg whites.
Pour into pan with Zwieback crust.
Bake in slow oven 300 degrees Fahrenheit or 275 degrees Fahrenheit for 1 hour.
Turn oven off and leave door shut for 1 hour more.
Then open door but leave cake in for 1/2 - 1 hour more.
Remove and cool.
Bring strawberries, 1 cup sugar, and 1 cup H2O to boil, and then simmer for 15 minutes.
Blend 1/3 cup H2O and 3 tablespoons cornstarch together, and then add to mixture stirring until thick and clear.
Strain mixture - about 1 cup glaze.
Place whole berries on cake that has been removed from pan, and pour glaze over berries and cake.
Refrigerate over night before serving.
notes: Marge Alexander - Fort Bliss. Marked as "Very Good".

title: Cottage Cheese and Cream Cheese Cake
ingredients: 1 pound Small Curd cream style Cottage Cheese
directions: Preheat oven, 325 degrees. Grease a large cheese cake pan with butter generously, dust pan with Graham Cracker Crumbs then add rest of crumbs to make a thick crust in bottom of the prepared pan.
Place cottage cheese and cream cheese in large mixing bowl (or blender) beat at high speed until well blended and creamy.
Beating with high speed blend in sugar, eggs. Reduce speed to low, add cornstarch, lemon juice and vanilla. Beat until blended smooth.
Add melted margarine or butter and sour cream, blend well again.
Pour into prepared pan. Do not stir.
Bake in 325 degree oven for 1 hour and 10 minutes-or until firm around the edges.
Turn off oven and let cake stay in oven for two hours.
Remove from oven and cool on wire rack. Chill. Remove sides of pan or loosen sides.
Cheese cake may be frozen if desired.
Serving: 16 to 20 servings.
notes: Dr Lee Chun 1986
pdfLink: Cottage Cheese and Cream Cheese Cake.pdf

title: Frozen Chocolate Mousse
ingredients: Sponge sheet cut to fit the mold
directions: Line the bottom and sides of a 5-cup Charlotte mold with a sponge sheet cut to fit the mold and brush the cake with orange-flavored liqueur.
In the top of a double boiler, melt 16 square semisweet chocolate.
Beat 2 egg yolks lightly with the mixer at moderate speed, beat in the chocolate and 3 tablespoons strong coffee and orange-flavored liqueur; mix well.
Beat 3 egg whites and fold gently into mixture.
Fold in 3/4 cup heavy cream, whipped.
Pour the mousse into the prepared mold and chill it for 1 hour.
Cover the top of mousse with a layer of sponge sheet, pressing it down slightly and brush it with orange-flavored liqueur.
Cover the mousse and freeze it; will keep for several months.
Just before serving, whip 1 1/2 cups whipping cream with 1/4 cup confectioners' sugar and 2 tablespoons orange-flavored liqueur.
Remove mold from pan and frost with whipped cream.
Decorate with chocolate curls.
Serves 8

title: Chocolate Mousse with Espresso and Dark Rum
directions: Chill 1 1/2 cups whipping cream in refrigerator.
Chill mixing bowl and beaters.
In top of double boiler, combine chocolate chips, coffee, rum, and butter.
Melt over barely simmering water. Melt to cool.
Pour remaining 1/4 cup whipping cream in cup with gelatin sprinkled over.
Allow gelatin to bloom for 10 minutes.
Lightly warm gelatin, set into cooled chocolate, and set aside.
Whip cream, mix (fold in) chocolate to whipped cream. Do not overwork the mousse.
Spoon into glasses, chill 1 hour or longer.
Yields 6-8 servings.
notes: Marked as "Very Good"
pdfLink: Chocolate Mousse with Espresso and Dark Rum.pdf

title: Frosty Holiday Bombe
directions: Chill a 2 quart melon or fluted mold.
Beat the raspberry sherbet and orange liqueur together still being thick.
Using spatula spread inside surface of mold 1 inch thick.
Freeze.
Whip lemon sherbet and creme de menthe, repeat step 3, freeze.
Remove from mold, ice with whipped cream.
Refreeze several hours.
notes: Serves 10.

title: Peach Ice Cream Mold
ingredients: 2 pounds extra-ripe peaches, peeled and chopped
directions: Place peaches in a large bowl; stir in sugar.
Allow to stand at room temperature for 30 minutes; mash peaches.
Line a 10-cup mold or bowl with plastic wrap; let plastic wrap hang over sides of mold or bowl.
Allow ice cream to soften and mix with peaches.
Place ice cream mixture in mold; cover with plastic wrap.
Freeze overnight.
When ready to serve, invert onto serving plate.
Peel off plastic wrap and drizzle with Melba sauce and garnish with sliced peaches.
Cut into wedges and serve.
Serves 10-12.
notes: Note: For ease in removing, dampen towel with hot water and place over mold for a few seconds after inverting on serving plate. "Quick, easy and spectacular!" The use of this material and the words 'Words Worth Eating' is licensed by Jacquelyn G. Legg.

title: Cherry - Berries on a Cloud
ingredients: 1 can (1 pound 5 ounces) cherry pie filling
2 cups sliced fresh strawberries or 1 pint (1 pound) frozen strawberries, thawed
directions: Heat oven to 275 degrees. Grease an oblong pan 13 x 9 x 2 inches.
Beat egg whites, cream of tartar and salt until frothy.
Gradually beat in 1 3/4 cups sugar.
Beat until very stiff and glossy, about 15 minutes.
Spread in prepared pan.
Bake 60 minutes.
Turn off oven and leave meringue in until cool, about 12 hours or overnight.
Mix cream cheese with 1 cup sugar and vanilla.
Gently fold in whipped cream and marshmallows.
Spread over meringue, refrigerate 12 hours or overnight.
Cut into serving pieces and top with Cherry - Berry Topping.
Topping: Stir 1 can (1 pound 5 ounces) cherry pie filling and 1 teaspoon lemon juice into 2 cups sliced fresh strawberries or 1 pint (1 pound) frozen strawberries, thawed.
notes: 10-12 servings.

title: Frozen Peaches and Cream Crust
ingredients: 1 cup (or more if desired) fresh peaches
directions: Combine crushed vanilla wafers and melted butter, and put over bottom and sides of freezer tray.
Heat juices to boiling, add marshmallows, stirring until dissolved.
Cool and add peaches; fold in whipped cream.
Freeze 3 to 4 hours.
notes: Mrs. Hodge

title: Strawberry Sherbet
directions: Make syrup of water and sugar in pan on medium heat.
Reduce to 1/3. Let cool.
Hull strawberries and puree in blender adding syrup slowly.
Add orange juice and sour cream.
Mix 1 minute.
Pour in bowl and freeze.
Top with mint leaves.

title: Luscious Dessert - Jerry Bird
directions: Beat 3 egg whites and 1 teaspoon cream of tartar until stiff.
Add gradually 1 cup sugar and fold in thoroughly.
Add 12 crumbled soda crackers and 1/2 cup chopped almonds or walnuts.
Grease a 9-inch pie pan and add above mixture.
Bake at 350 degrees for 30 minutes.
When crust is thoroughly cooled, fill with thickly whipped cream and folded in fruit pie filling (blueberries, cherries, etc.).
notes: Jerry Bird

title: Pineapple Delight with Marshmallows and Macaroons
directions: Mix pineapple with marshmallows, cut in quarters, macaroons, crumbled, and dates pitted and cut in small pieces.
Chill for several hours before serving.
notes: from Mrs. Hodges - 1964, Good, 6 - 8 servings
pdfLink: Pineapple Delight with Marshmallows and Macaroons.pdf

title: German Torte with Fruit
directions: Beat eggs, sugar, and vanilla well, about 4 minutes.
Fold in flour, corn starch, and baking powder.
Grease pan well and bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 15 to 20 minutes.
Let cool about 5 minutes and remove from pan.
Fill with any kind of fruit (peaches, cherries, strawberries, etc.).
Make glaze from fruit juice and cornstarch.
Place over top of fruit.
Chill well and serve.
notes: M. Ramsey - 1963; with whipping cream

title: Biscuit Tortoni with Almond Macaroons and Maraschino Cherries
ingredients: 0.5 cup and 3 tablespoons crushed almond macaroons
directions: Beat egg yolks with sugar until fluffy.
Stir in sherry and vanilla.
Beat egg whites until stiff and in peaks.
Fold egg mixture into whites.
Fold in whipped cream.
Stir 0.5 cup almond macaroons and the cherries.
Put mixture in paper dessert dishes holding 4 ounces.
Sprinkle each with a little of the remaining crushed macaroon.
Freeze until firm.
Yields 6 to 8 servings.
notes: Crushed macaroons give it a delightful almond flavor.
pdfLink: Biscuit Tortoni with Almond Macaroons and Maraschino Cherries.pdf

title: Old Fashioned Bread Pudding
directions: In saucepan, bring water and raisins to boil; let stand for 5 to 10 minutes; drain well and reserve.
Combine scalded milk and margarine; slowly add beaten eggs.
Add sugar, salt, cinnamon and vanilla; stir until blended.
Place bread cubes and raisins in an 8-inch ungreased, square glass dish; pour milk mixture over top, stirring to moisten.
Sprinkle with nutmeg.
Set glass dish in pan of hot water; bake at 350 degrees for 40 minutes, or until knife inserted in center comes out clean.
Serves 6-8.
notes: Serve plain or with cream. "Just as good cold as it is!" Warm and spicy!

title: Strawberry Shortcake Sundae
ingredients: 16 ounces frozen strawberries in syrup, thawed
directions: Toast the waffles lightly following directions on box. Cool waffles slightly. Sift confectioners sugar lightly over the top of each waffle after it has been placed on serving plate.
Top with a scoop of ice cream, strawberries and whipped cream.
Serves 8 or as many as you wish. Simply prepare as many waffles as you plan to serve.
notes: Note: The waffle makes the quickest, most delicious shortcake and the waffle holds all the juice! This dessert can be served all year since it's delicious when made with frozen berries. "Looks sensational and tastes even better!"

title: Banana Sky Scraper Sundae
ingredients: 6-8 ripe bananas, halved lengthwise and quartered
directions: Combine syrup and nuts. Place one tablespoon of the nut mixture in the bottom of each sundae glass or glass mug.
Top with a scoop of chocolate ice cream; add 4 banana pieces (cut side facing out) so they stand above the rim of the glass.
Add 1 scoop of vanilla ice cream between the banana pieces.
Top with 1 tablespoon chocolate syrup and 1 tablespoon of the nut mixture.
Spoon whipped cream on the top and garnish with a cherry.
Serve 6-8 happy people!
Note: Make as many as you wish by adjusting the amount of the ingredients. Keep the remaining nut mixture in a covered container in the refrigerator for later use.
notes: Fun to serve after a picnic or cook-out!

title: Pineapple Loaf
ingredients: 2 egg whites, beaten stiff with pinch of salt
2 3/4 cups graham crackers, crumbed and butter to hold together
directions: Cream butter and sugar.
Cook egg yolks with cream over water.
Mix with butter and sugar.
Add pineapple, pineapple juice, and egg whites.
Place layer of crumbs in long pyrex dish.
Add layer of mixture, etc.
Always have crumbs for top and bottom layers.
Top with whipped cream.

title: Orange Sponge Sheet for Mousse
directions: Butter a jelly roll pan, 11x16, line it with wax paper and butter the paper.
In a bowl, beat 4 egg yolks and 1/3 cup sugar with a whisk until mixture ribbons when the whisk is drawn.
In another bowl, beat 4 egg whites with a pinch of salt until they are stiff and beat in 1 tablespoon orange juice and 1 teaspoon grated orange rind.
Add 1/4 of the whites to the yolk mixture and fold in.
Pour the yolk mixture into the remaining whites and sift over them 1/3 cup flour and fold together.
Pour the batter into the jelly roll pan and spread it evenly with a metal spatula.
Bake at 350 degrees for 15 minutes or until it is lightly browned.
Loosen the wax paper from the sides of pan and invert the cake onto a baking sheet.
Let cool.

title: Date Pudding with Nuts and Whipped Cream
directions: Sift 1 tablespoon flour and 1 teaspoon baking powder over 1 cup chopped nuts and 1 cup chopped dates.
Beat the yolks of 3 eggs thoroughly and add 1 cup sugar gradually.
Mix with nuts and dates and combine with well beaten whites of 3 eggs.
Bake in well greased pan about 40 minutes at 325 degrees.
Serve cold with whipped cream.
notes: Baked at 325 degrees.
pdfLink: Date Pudding with Nuts and Whipped Cream.pdf

title: Orange Delight by Jerri Burd
directions: Dissolve 1 package orange jello in 1 cup hot water and 1/4 cup sugar.
Add 1/2 cup orange juice and chill.
Fold in 3/4 cup whipped cream and sliced bananas.
Butter dish and line with lady fingers.
Chill till set.
notes: Jerri Burd

title: Jean Romeros' Lemon Soufflé
directions: Prepare collar for 1-quart dish. Measure out 20 inches of waxed paper, fold and double to make 6 inches wide; wrap on outside of dish to stand 2 inches high.
Grate lemon rind and squeeze juice. Sprinkle gelatin over water in a saucepan. Let stand 10 minutes, until gelatin softens.
Place over low heat until gelatin dissolves, the mixture will be clear. Remove from heat and cool.
Combine eggs and sugar and beat at high speed in a large mixer. Beat 7 to 8 minutes until thick and light.
Combine lemon rind and juice with cool gelatin. Pour into egg and sugar mixture and beat until blended (lower speed).
Chill mixture for 10 to 30 minutes stirring frequently until it mounds.
While mixture is chilling beat 1 1/2 cups of cream in a small bowl until soft peaks form. Then fold into chilled mixture and whipped cream until no streaks of white remain.
Pour into prepared dish and chill 3 hours or until set. Remove collar gently and decorate with lemon twists and violets.
notes: Jean Romeres '97

title: Lemon Sponge Pudding
directions: Mix flour, sugar and salt.
Add lemon juice and rind and melted butter.
Beat egg yolks, add milk and add to first mixture.
Beat egg whites until stiff, not dry.
Fold into batter, set casserole or pan in pan of water and bake at 325 degrees for about 45 minutes.
notes: For Nancy. Mom. I use one large and one small casserole or whatever the pudding fits in.

title: Strawberry Tiramisú
ingredients: 1/3 cup plus 4 tablespoons Cointreau or other orange liqueur, divided
directions: Whisk preserves, 1/3 cup Cointreau, and orange juice in 2-cup measuring cup. Place mascarpone cheese and 2 tablespoons Cointreau in large bowl; fold just to blend. Using electric mixer, beat cream, sugar, vanilla, and remaining 2 tablespoons Cointreau in another large bowl to soft peaks. Stir 1/4 of whipped cream mixture into mascarpone mixture to lighten. Fold in remaining whipped cream.

Hull and slice half of strawberries. Spread 1/2 cup preserve mixture over bottom of 3-quart oblong serving dish or 13 x 9 x 2-inch glass baking dish. Arrange enough ladyfingers over preserve mixture to cover bottom of dish. Spoon 3/4 cup preserve mixture over ladyfingers, then spread 2 1/2 cups mascarpone mixture over. Arrange sliced strawberries over mascarpone mixture. Repeat layering with remaining ladyfingers, preserve mixture, and mascarpone mixture. Cover with plastic and chill at least 8 hours or overnight.
Slice remaining strawberries. Arrange over tiramisú and serve.
notes: *An Italian cream cheese that's sold at supermarkets and Italian markets.

title: Deep-dish Apple Crisp with Vanilla Ice Cream
directions: Preheat oven to 375 degrees.
Lightly grease an 8-inch glass baking dish.
Place half of the apples in the dish; top with corn syrup.
Add remaining apples, lemon juice, 1 teaspoon cinnamon and nutmeg.
Combine 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, sugar, salt, butter, flour and oatmeal.
Mix well and press firmly over apples.
Bake 50 minutes.
Top with ice cream and serve.
Serves 6-8.
notes: Marked as "Very Good"; Can be prepared, refrigerated and baked when ready to serve. "Easy to prepare! Serve warm!"
pdfLink: Deep-Dish Apple Crisp with Vanilla Ice Cream.pdf

title: Apple Cranberry Crisp
ingredients: 3 packages instant Cinnamon and Spice oatmeal
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees
Mix apples and cranberries with 2 tablespoons flour to coat. Add sugar and mix well. Place in 2 quart casserole.
Combine oatmeal and remaining ingredients. Melt butter, add to oatmeal mixture and stir well. Spoon over apple mixture.
Bake uncovered for 45 minutes. Serve with vanilla ice cream.
notes: Serves 8. From Patty Jollison 1988 Susan Dawner

title: Microwave Apple Walnut Pie
ingredients: 5 large Granny Smith apples, peeled and thinly sliced
4 tablespoons corn oil margarine, cut into small pieces
1 pint vanilla ice milk or low-fat frozen yogurt, optional
directions: Prepare apples; toss with lemon juice and set aside.
Lightly spray a 9- or 10-inch pie plate with no-stick cooking spray and fill with apples.
TOPPING: Place all topping ingredients in a bowl; use a pastry blender to cut in margarine until mixture is crumbly.
Sprinkle topping over apples in an even layer.
Cook on high for 8-10 minutes or until apples are fork tender and juices have bubbled up through topping.
Serve at room temperature with your choice of ice milk or frozen yogurt.
Serves 6-8.
notes: Note: Be sure to rotate pie plate during cooking time. The whole pie or individual servings reheat nicely in the microwave. There will be a little juice in the pie plate if you cut the pie while warm. The juice thickens as the pie cools. LOW CHOLESTEROL VARIATION: Walnuts can be reduced to 1/4 cup, or omitted. 'A delicious low-cholesterol dessert that will please all the members of your family!'

title: Apple Dumplings
directions: Peel and core apples. Cut into fourths.
Unroll and separate the crescent rolls. Place in an 8-inch square baking dish.
Sprinkle with cinnamon.
Combine butter, sugar, orange juice, and vanilla in a saucepan. Bring to a boil and remove from heat.
Pour over the rolls.
Spoon pan juice over rolls when served.
Bake at 350 degrees Fahrenheit for 30 minutes.
notes: Donna Kurtze

title: Pear and Maple Crumble
ingredients: 1/2 cup (1 stick) chilled unsalted butter, cut into small pieces
3 1/2 pounds firm but ripe Anjou pears, peeled, cored, cut into 1/2-inch pieces
directions: For Topping: Combine all ingredients in processor. Process until nuts are coarsely chopped. Cover; chill until firm, 1 hour.

For Pears: Position rack in center of oven and preheat to 350°F. Toss all ingredients except sour cream in large bowl to blend. Let stand 15 minutes. Transfer pear mixture to 13x9x2-inch baking dish. Sprinkle topping over pears. Bake until juices bubble thickly, about 30 minutes. Let stand 10 minutes. Serve warm with sour cream.
notes: Served with sour cream, this homespun dessert is a delicious combination of pears and raisins, which are tossed with maple syrup and accented with chopped crystallized ginger. The fruit is baked under a topping made sweet from brown sugar and crunchy from walnuts. From Bon Appétit.

title: Rice Pudding with Lemon Peel and Raisins
directions: Put 1 quart milk, 0.25 teaspoon salt, 0.75 cup long grain rice and 2 thin slices lemon peel (no white) into 2-quart saucepan; simmer, uncovered, until rice is tender - about 20 minutes.
Meanwhile soak 1 cup raisins in enough hot water to cover.
Remove rice from heat, remove lemon peel.
Drain raisins; mix with rice. Beat 3 egg yolks with 0.5 cup sugar; stir into rice.
Turn mixture into 1.5-quart casserole and bake at 300 degrees Fahrenheit for 25 minutes.
Sprinkle at once with 3 tablespoons confectioners' sugar and slide under broiler to caramelize.
Serve warm with cream or milk.
notes: 6-8 servings
pdfLink: Rice Pudding with Lemon Peel and Raisins.pdf

title: 7 Minute Icing
directions: Stir, then boil in a covered pan until the sugar is dissolved.
Place in a small mixing bowl: unbeaten egg white, 1/4 teaspoon cream of tartar, 1/8 teaspoon salt.
Add the hot syrup. Beat these ingredients at high speed (electric mixer) until the icing is right consistency to spread, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add while beating: 1 teaspoon vanilla.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Ellen Hodge. Serves 2-9 layer cakes.

title: Coconut Pecan Frosting
ingredients: 1 cup evaporated or half and half milk
directions: Combine evaporated or half and half milk, sugar, egg yolks, margarine and vanilla in a saucepan.
Cook over medium heat 12 minutes, stirring constantly, until mixture thickens.
Add coconut and pecans.
Beat until cool and of spreading consistency.
Makes enough to cover tops of 3-9 inch layers.
Do not frost sides of cake.

title: Graves' Mountain Lodge Lemon Squares
directions: Preheat oven at 325 degrees.
Mix first four ingredients in order given.
Spread in a 7x11 inch greased pan.
Bake for 15 minutes.
Remove from oven.
Combine remaining ingredients and spread over baked mixture.
Return to oven.
Bake 20 minutes at 350 degrees.
Frost with glaze (Combination of all ingredients).
notes: From the Kitchen of Graves' Mountain Lodge

title: Cherry-white Chocolate Drop Cookies
directions: Heat the oven to 375 degrees.
Line two baking sheets with kitchen parchment.
In a large bowl, use an electric mixer to beat the butter and both sugars until fluffy, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the egg, almond extract and milk, then mix well.
Add the flour and baking soda, then mix just until the dry ingredients are well mixed in.
Mix in the cherries, cranberries and chocolate chips.
Drop the dough in 2-tablespoon mounds on the prepared baking sheets, leaving 2 inches between them.
Bake, in batches if necessary, for 12 to 14 minutes, or until just lightly browned at the edges and still slightly soft at the center.
Leave on the baking sheet for 2 minutes, then use a spatula to transfer to a wire rack to cool completely.
notes: Nutrition Information per serving: 210 calories, 90 calories from fat (43 percent of total calories), 10 grams fat (6 grams saturated, no trans fats), 30 milligrams cholesterol, 28 grams carbohydrate, 1 gram fiber, 15 grams sugar, 3 grams protein, 40 milligrams sodium.

title: Mrs. Field's Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Cookies
ingredients: 5 cups oatmeal (Put small amounts into blender until it turns to powder. Measure first, then blend.)
directions: Cream together the butter, sugar, and brown sugar.
Add the eggs and vanilla, and mix.
Mix together the flour, blended oatmeal, salt, baking powder, and baking soda.
Mix all ingredients and add the chocolate chips, grated Hershey bar, and chopped nuts.
Bake on ungreased cookie sheets. Make golf ball sized cookies, 2 inches apart, and bake at 375 degrees for 6 minutes.
(I flattened the cookies with a spatula after they had baked for 6 minutes, then I bake them an additional 4 minutes.)
notes: Makes 112 cookies. (This recipe costs a friend of Carol's $250.00!!!!!!!!!) Carol's friend is an OR nurse at Sibley Hospital in Washington, D.C. One day she noticed an ad for "Mrs. Field's Cookie Recipe" and decided to call for it. The person answering the call told her that there would be a two-fifty charge for the recipe and she could pay by check or use a credit card — she charged it, to find out when her credit card statement arrived, that the price of this recipe was two hundred and fifty dollars — irate, she called the advertised number again, charging them with deceitful practice, to no avail. Thus, you are the recipient of "Mrs. Field's Cookie Recipe" — as this young lady promised the person on the phone that she would see to it that the entire population of the United States, and possibly the world, would receive a copy of her recipe. Do pass it on to your friends!
pdfLink: Mrs. Field's Chocolate Chip Oatmeal Cookies.pdf

title: Frozen Fruit Parfait
directions: Mix orange and lemon juice with water.
Slice bananas in juice and add other ingredients.
Mix and freeze.
Makes 18 servings.
Thaw some before serving.
Fill parfait 3/4 full and pour ginger ale on top.
notes: Recipe from the kitchen of Mary King.

title: Pear Oatmeal Cookies
ingredients: 2 fresh, medium-sized Bartlett pears, coarsely chopped
directions: Cream butter with brown sugar until smooth.
Beat in remaining ingredients except sugar until combined.
Drop by rounded teaspoons onto lightly greased baking sheet.
Sprinkle generously with sugar.
Bake in preheated 350-degree oven for 15 minutes or until lightly browned.
notes: Makes 4 1/2 dozen cookies. Nutrition facts per cookie: 62 calories, 1 grams protein, 2.1 grams fat, 10.1 grams carbohydrate, 0.6 grams dietary fiber, 9 milligrams cholesterol, 54 milligrams sodium.

title: Orange Cake with Chocolate Glaze
directions: Prepare cake mix as label directs for 2 8-inch round cake pans; cool.
To make glaze, in double boiler over, not boiling, water, melt chocolate pieces with the butter, milk and corn syrup until well blended, stirring constantly.
With small spatula, fill and frost cake layers with glaze.
Garnish with orange peel and chocolate curls.
Makes 10 servings.
notes: EARLY IN DAY:

title: Toffee Bars with Semisweet Chocolate and Pecans
directions: Preheat oven to 350 degrees. Grease a 9-by-13-by-2-inch baking pan.
Cream butter and sugar. Add egg yolk and mix well.
Sift in flour, mixing well, and then the vanilla.
Spread the batter in the prepared pan and bake for 25 minutes.
Cover the cake layer with the chocolate chips and return to the oven for 3 or 4 minutes.
Remove the pan from the oven and spread the melted chocolate evenly.
Sprinkle with the nuts and gently press them into the chocolate with the back of a fork.
Cool completely in the pan before cutting them into bars.
notes: Adapted from "The Silver Palate Cookbook" by Julee Rosso and Shella Lukins. Light, crisp, and chocolaty. Makes 30 bars.
pdfLink: Toffee Bars with Semisweet Chocolate and Pecans.pdf
